items.title: Development and preliminary psychometric evaluation of a spectacle trial-wear questionnaire for distance single-vision prescriptions
items.abstract: BackgroundExisting vision questionnaires were not designed to standardize immediate patient appraisal of a distance single-vision spectacle prescription during trial wear. This study developed and preliminarily evaluated the Adult Spectacle Trial-Wearing Experience Scale (ASTWES) for this decision point.MethodsCandidate items were informed by a structured literature search and interviews with eye-care and dispensing professionals, refined through two Delphi rounds, cognitively debriefed with 10 target patients, and piloted in 150 adults. Item reduction used corrected item-total correlations and principal-axis factoring with promax rotation. The independent formal psychometric evaluation sample comprised 393 adults within the prespecified 18–35-year age range; ordinal confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), robust maximum-likelihood sensitivity analysis, and reliability coefficients were used. An eligible subsample of 98 participants provided a 1-month satisfaction rating for exploratory association analyses.ResultsThe final questionnaire contained 9 items in 3 correlated domains: clarity and focus, comfort and stability, and environmental adaptation. Retained pilot-item loadings ranged from 0.694 to 0.890. The correlated three-factor model was supported under both CFA estimators, whereas a single-factor model fit poorly. Subscale Cronbach's alpha values ranged from 0.769 to 0.803. Omega hierarchical was 0.641, favoring subscale-first interpretation. The overall mean item score correlated with 1-month satisfaction (Spearman rho = 0.753, p < 0.001); its exploratory AUC was 0.850 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.772–0.918).ConclusionsASTWES is a concise candidate questionnaire with preliminary evidence of a correlated three-domain structure, acceptable internal consistency, and short-term clinical association in Chinese adults aged 18–35 years. Further independent patient-centered content evaluation and external validation are needed before routine use or fixed decision thresholds are considered.

items.title: Cultural context of professional identity formation: a perspective of health profession educators in Botswana
items.abstract: In Botswana, the phrase “motho ke motho ka batho—“I am because you are” is culturally a way of life and core to who we are as a people. As Batswana, our relationships and the evolution of our individual and collective identities are built on this key concept of Botho/Ubuntu. For us, Botho dictates that one does not merely “become” but “becomes with” in relation to identity formation, and by extension, professional identity formation (PIF). In this paper, the authors share their perspectives on professional identity formation (PIF) for health professions educators in the context of scarce African and non-Western epistemologies in the literature. The authors' guiding question and focus is: are the existing models/frameworks of PIF contextually relevant? If not, how can they be enriched and contextualized? This is one of the key tensions in the PIF discourse. The authors contend that contextualizing PIF efforts must integrate holistic cultural lenses and local ontologies into the current PIF models. We illustrate how leveraging indigenous knowledge frameworks encapsulated in the Botho belief system could contextualize existing PIF frameworks using a model we have termed, “Mabogo Dinku”. The phrase Mabogo Dinku is derived from a prominent Setswana proverb, “mabogo dinku a a thebana”, meaning, working together towards a common goal. The model is in a pictorial form and highlights the interconnectivity between the different frameworks. The model suggests that if any of the frameworks are misapplied the whole Botho belief system weakens and so too the concept of “becoming with”.

items.title: Prolonged infusion of meropenem for suspected intracystic infection in polycystic kidney disease during pregnancy: a case report
items.abstract: BackgroundIntrarenal cyst infection in polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is hard to confirm and harder to treat during pregnancy, when lipid-soluble antibiotics are generally avoided.CaseA pregnant woman at approximately 10 weeks’ gestation presented with recurrent fever and flank pain for over one month, with acute exacerbation one day prior to admission. Laboratory tests revealed progressively elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) levels despite repeatedly negative cultures. Serial ultrasound showed a right upper-pole renal cyst that evolved to exhibit internal septations and debris.Treatment and outcomeCyst aspiration was avoided; meropenem 1 g every 8 h was initiated on admission and converted to prolonged infusion (1 g infused over more than 3 h) on Day 4, followed by step-down oral amoxicillin–clavulanate, for a total antimicrobial course of 32 days. Fever resolved and CRP normalized; pregnancy continued uneventfully.ConclusionIn a pregnant patient with suspected PKD cyst infection, prolonged-infusion meropenem was followed by clinical improvement. The favorable response observed supports further evaluation of this therapeutic strategy, despite the absence of microbiological confirmation.

items.title: Correction: CXCL2/CXCR2 pathway regulates CD169high large macrophages to promote progression of malignant pleural effusion from lung adenocarcinoma
Two cortical mechanisms for natural audiovisual processing
items.abstract: Understanding how the human brain processes natural audiovisual information remains a central challenge in cognitive neuroscience. Progress has been limited by the difficulty of modeling complex audiovisual stimuli; prior work has therefore relied largely on short, controlled, or unimodal stimuli, leaving cortical mechanisms supporting real-world comprehension poorly characterized. Although recent AI advances enable extraction of high-dimensional, time-resolved features from naturalistic stimuli, how cortical regions dynamically prioritize auditory and visual information as time unfolds remains largely unexplored. Using large-scale fMRI data collected during movie viewing, we developed two complementary prediction-based approaches to map moment-by-moment sensory processing across cortex: one detects sustained periods when one modality predicts a region better than the other, identifying regions that switch the modality they encode for meaningful stretches of time; while the other identifies periods when both modalities predict the region well, revealing balanced audiovisual representations. Together, these analyses reveal two cortical patterns of audiovisual processing: two modality-switching ``bows" (a posterior bow encircling category-selective visual cortex and an anterior bow spanning dorsolateral frontal cortex) and an arrow-like axis jointly representing both modalities (extending from lateral occipital into temporal cortex). We further show that switching is not driven by reduced low-level information in the non-dominant modality, but by reduced cortical encoding of that information, suggesting active sensory reweighting. Modality dominance also cannot be explained simply by the dominant modality conveying a region's preferred concepts; switching regions do not merely track whichever modality expresses these concepts.Together, these systems suggest a cortical architecture that adaptively reweights sensory inputs while maintaining balanced multimodal representations during naturalistic comprehension.
items.authors: Pushpita, S. N.; Wehbe, L.

items.title: Direct CDK1 engagement underlies carbaryl-induced genotoxic cell cycle arrest
items.abstract: Carbaryl, a widely used carbamate pesticide, has been epidemiologically associated with genotoxic and carcinogenic outcomes in exposed human populations, including elevated cancer risk at several tissue sites and, in some agricultural communities, chronic tubulointerstitial kidney disease of unknown etiology (CKDu). However, the cellular mechanisms underlying these associations, and whether carbaryl acts uniformly across tissues, remain poorly defined. Screening a panel of cell lines of distinct species and lineage, we found that carbaryl elicits pronounced, dose-dependent cytotoxicity and cell cycle arrest selectively in a renal tubular epithelial line (IMCD3) and, to a lesser extent, a cervical epithelial line (HeLa), while a fibroblast line (NIH3T3) was unaffected. In IMCD3 cells, carbaryl induces S- and G2/M-phase arrest through direct binding to DNA and consequent DNA damage, triggers Bcl-2-mediated late apoptosis independently of reactive oxygen species, and drives irreversible mitotic arrest. Molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assays, and kinase measurements converge on CDK1 as a direct target of carbaryl: carbaryl destabilises the CDK1 active site and inhibits its catalytic activity, whereas CDK2 is engaged through an opposing, rigidifying mode with no functional consequence. This asymmetry provides a coherent mechanistic basis for the combined S-phase and G2/M arrest observed. Together, these findings establish carbaryl as a genotoxic, cell-cycle-disrupting agent with tissue-selective potency acting directly on CDK1, and provide a cell-based mechanistic framework for interpreting its reported associations with renal and other tissue pathologies in exposed human populations.
items.authors: Piyush, R.; Tayade, S.; Shinde, S. R.
items.title_zh: 直接作用于CDK1导致卡巴氯苯诱导的基因毒性细胞周期停滞
items.summary_zh: 卡巴氯苯是一种广泛使用的氨基甲酸酯类农药，已在人群中与基因毒性和致癌结果相关联，包括多种组织的癌症风险增加及某些农业社区的慢性肾小管间质病（CKDu）。然而，其细胞机制及在不同组织中的作用尚不明确。通过筛选不同物种和谱系的细胞系，我们发现卡巴氯苯在肾小管上皮细胞系（IMCD3）中引发显著的剂量依赖性细胞毒性和细胞周期停滞，而在宫颈上皮细胞系（HeLa）中影响较小，成纤维细胞系（NIH3T3）则未受影响。在IMCD3细胞中，卡巴氯苯通过直接结合DNA引发S期和G2/M期停滞，导致DNA损伤，触发Bcl-2介导的晚期凋亡，并驱动不可逆的有丝分裂停滞。分子动力学模拟、细胞热转移实验和激酶测定表明CDK1是卡巴氯苯的直接靶点，卡巴氯苯使CDK1活性位点不稳定并抑制其催化活性，而CDK2则通过相反的刚性模式结合，但无功能后果。这种不对称性为S期停滞提供了一个一致的机制基础。

items.title: Initiation codon context governs translation-coupled mRNA decay and coordinated expression in the human parasite Leishmania
items.abstract: In the absence of canonical, promoter-based transcriptional regulation, Leishmania has evolved alternative regulatory mechanisms for adaptive gene expression, including post-transcriptional control via differential mRNA turnover. While this mechanism is recognized as critical in Leishmania, fundamental aspects of transcript stability in these parasites remain to be elucidated, such as the role of translation initiation-mediated mRNA decay. We addressed this important gap by investigating the role of the initiation codon context (Kozak sequence) in gene expression in L. donovani. Mapping Kozak sequences across the trypanosomatid genomes revealed important differences in nucleotide preference across the genus and sub-genus levels, suggesting important cis-regulatory function. Within a single species, only a small subset of possible Kozak sequences is associated with several start codons, further supporting their role in expression control. Transgenic L. donovani lines expressing EGFP under the control of distinct Kozak variants indeed demonstrated that the nucleotide context of the start codon directly modulates both protein expression and mRNA stability, which was associated with increased recruitment of mRNA to heavy polysomes. Parasite exposure to the translation inhibitor cycloheximide restored EGFP expression driven by a weak Kozak sequence, revealing a direct link between mRNA stability and Kozak-mediated translatability. RNA-seq analysis of parasites arrested for transcription or translation elongation revealed transcripts enriched for the GO terms RNA modification and pseudouridine synthesis as key targets for translation-dependent mRNA turnover. The segregation of these transcripts into functional clusters with distinct Kozak profiles further suggests that Kozak sequence composition defines Kozak-governed regulons in Leishmania. Within this regulatory framework, the -3 nucleotide is identified as the key positional determinant driving differential transcript abundance. Our work uncovers a key role for translation initiation-coupled mRNA decay in Leishmania gene expression regulation adding a previously underappreciated layer of post-transcriptional regulation in parasite adaptation.
items.authors: SANTI, A. M. M.; COKELAER, T.; PIPOLI DA FONSECA, J.; JENKINS, P.; TIKHONOVA, E. B.; RODRIGUEZ-ALMONACID, C.; KARAMYSHEV, A.; KARAMYSHEVA, Z.; SPÄTH, G.
items.title_zh: 起始密码子环境影响利什曼原虫的翻译耦合mRNA降解与协调表达
items.summary_zh: 在缺乏经典的基于启动子的转录调控情况下，利什曼原虫进化出替代的适应性基因表达调控机制，包括通过差异化mRNA降解的转录后控制。我们研究了起始密码子环境（Kozak序列）在利什曼原虫L. donovani基因表达中的作用。对不同鞭毛虫基因组的Kozak序列进行映射，揭示了属和亚属水平上核苷酸偏好的重要差异，表明其具有重要的顺式调控功能。在同一物种中，只有少数Kozak序列与多个起始密码子相关，进一步支持其在表达调控中的作用。转基因L. donovani株系在不同Kozak变体控制下表达EGFP，显示起始密码子的核苷酸环境直接调节蛋白表达和mRNA稳定性，并与mRNA向重多核糖体的增加招募相关。翻译抑制剂环己酰亚胺的处理恢复了由弱Kozak序列驱动的EGFP表达，揭示了mRNA降解与翻译之间的直接联系。

items.title: A Large Yield Model for Crop Production and Design in Western Canada
items.abstract: With a changing climate, disease pressure, and other production threats, it is critical to ensure that crop producers are well-positioned to protect and optimize yields. In this work we present LYM-1, the first large-scale, multi-crop model for the prediction of yield performance in the Canadian prairies. This is enabled by a large dataset containing over 4.7 million yield observations across 10 different crop types, distributed over 23 growing years. Leveraging additional data sources for weather and soil properties allows the model to reason about the complex interactions between genetics, environment, and management which underlie yield. The trained model is not only effective at predicting the yield for held-out data, but also reveals scientifically and agronomically relevant effects such as the interaction between solar radiation and nitrogen uptake. We show that the architecture and training approach used in LYM-1 allows it to perform inference given incomplete queries where some model inputs are unspecified, while also establishing an advantage over popular linear and machine learning models in predictive performance.
items.authors: Ubbens, J.; Loliencar, P.; Kagale, S.

items.title: Biotin-operated ligand trapping enables dynamic spatial redistribution of protein and organelle in living cells
items.abstract: Controlling protein localization through chemical biology tools is essential for mechanistic interrogations, functional perturbations, and therapeutic development. While existing tools cover a wide range of applications, no single approach simultaneously enables inducible trapping, controlled release, and visualization of a protein of interest (POI). To address this gap, we developed Biotin-Operated Ligand Trapping (BOLT), which combines a HaloTag-fused POI with a streptavidin trap. Desthiobiotin-conjugated Janelia Fluor HaloTag ligands enable POI visualization, trapping, and biotin-operated release. We demonstrate BOLT's capacity in synchronized secretory cargo release, microtubule-directed organelle movement and hitchhiking, and ectopically localizing nuclear transcription factor. Importantly, pulse-chase BOLT further reveals bidirectional endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi trafficking of an endogenous Golgi enzyme and distinguishes recycled from newly synthesized enzyme populations using distinct HTLs. Altogether, BOLT provides an all-in-one platform to interrogate how subcellular localization regulates protein function across HaloTag-compatible systems.
items.authors: Beyers, W. C.; Plutkis, S. E.; Rutcher, K. R.; Sun, J. L.; Haas, M. R.; Hutton, M. S.; Kim, H. K.; Chavez, A.; Pruett-Miller, S. M.; Vevea, J. D.; Lavis, L.; Chang, C.-L.
items.title_zh: 生物素操作的配体捕获实现活细胞中蛋白质与细胞器的动态重分布
items.summary_zh: 通过化学生物学工具控制蛋白质定位对于机制研究、功能干扰和治疗开发至关重要。现有工具虽然应用广泛，但没有单一方法能同时实现诱导捕获、控制释放和目标蛋白（POI）可视化。为填补这一空白，我们开发了生物素操作的配体捕获（BOLT），将HaloTag融合的POI与链霉亲和素捕获结合。Desthiobiotin结合的Janelia Fluor HaloTag配体实现了POI的可视化、捕获和生物素操作释放。我们展示了BOLT在同步分泌货物释放、微管导向的细胞器运动和搭便车，以及异位定位核转录因子的能力。重要的是，脉冲追踪BOLT进一步揭示了内源性高尔基酶的双向内质网-高尔基运输，并利用不同的HTLs区分回收与新合成的酶群体。总体而言，BOLT提供了一个一体化平台，以研究亚细胞定位如何调节HaloTag兼容系统中的蛋白质功能。

items.title: Synaptic density imaging associates with performance but not self-report in autism
items.abstract: Autism is a common neurodevelopmental condition with considerable between-person variability and unknown biological etiology. Diagnosis of autism in adults relies on measurement of performance (e.g., clinician rating of social behavior, standardized assessment of cognition) and self-report of autism features. Our prior work revealed a strong relationship between clinician ratings of social function in autism and in vivo measures of synaptic density as measured by [11C]UCB-J PET (Matuskey et al., 2025). However, it is not understood how the measured aspects of the autism phenotype index underlying biology. Here, in a sample of 12 autistic adults, we address this question by relating synaptic density imaging to a range of performance measures, such as cognition and face recognition, in contrast to self-report measures. Our results identify a dissociation between these measurement types in that synaptic density correlates strongly with measures of performance but shows virtually no relationship with self-report. These findings suggest that, while self-report and performance measures share variance in characterizing phenotypes in autism, they diverge when mapping onto the underlying biology. Results suggest that higher synaptic density may index a general mechanism that facilitates social and cognitive performance across a range of tasks. These data also indicate that performance and self-report measures are not interchangeable in capturing brain-behavior correspondences in autism, a finding that can guide measure selection in future biomarker studies and clinical research.
items.authors: Naples, A. J.; Cayir, S.; cukar-capizzi, C.; Wolf, J. M.; Mcclelland, J. E.; Robertson, E. C.; Sawant, S. S.; Matuskey, D.; McPartland, J.
items.title_zh: 自闭症中突触密度成像与表现相关但与自我报告无关
items.summary_zh: 自闭症是一种常见的神经发育障碍，个体间差异显著且生物学病因尚不明确。成人自闭症的诊断依赖于表现（如临床社交行为评分、标准化认知评估）和自我报告的自闭症特征。我们之前的研究发现，自闭症患者的临床社交功能评分与通过[11C]UCB-J PET测量的体内突触密度之间存在强相关性。然而，尚不清楚这些自闭症表型的测量如何与基础生物学相关。在本研究中，我们对12名自闭症成人进行分析，将突触密度成像与认知和面孔识别等多种表现测量进行关联，发现突触密度与表现测量强相关，但与自我报告几乎没有关系。这些结果表明，自我报告和表现测量在表征自闭症表型时共享方差，但在映射基础生物学时存在分歧。结果提示，较高的突触密度可能指示一种促进社交和认知表现的普遍机制。

items.title: Thalamic Dysconnectivity and Negative Symptoms in Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorder
items.abstract: Background and Hypothesis Negative symptoms in schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD) are associated with poor functional outcomes and reduced quality of life; however, effective treatments remain limited. A better understanding of the underlying brain mechanisms is needed to develop better treatments. Neuroimaging studies implicate multiple brain networks in negative symptoms, though findings remain heterogeneous, potentially reflecting the multidimensionality of both symptoms and brain networks. Larger, more systematic dissections are required to identify the key hub(s) underlying negative symptoms. Study Design Structural MRI data from 394 participants (210 SSD, 184 healthy controls [HC]) were analyzed to identify cortical thickness and subcortical volume demonstrating both SSD-HC differences and associations with negative symptoms measured by the Brief Negative Symptom Scale (BNSS). Regions meeting both criteria were selected as seeds for resting-state functional connectivity analyses in 143 SSD patients to examine association with negative symptoms and their subdomains. Study Results The thalamus was the only region demonstrating significant structural abnormalities both in SSD and an association with BNSS total score (p-FDR<0.05). Functional-network-defined thalamic subregions were subsequently examined. Several thalamic hypoconnectivities were significantly corresponded with negative symptoms, involving thalamic subregions associated with the cortical default mode, somatosensory, medial temporal, and dorsal attention networks (p=0.001, corrected<0.05). Blunted affect showed the most extensive thalamic connectivity alterations, involving the striatum, cerebellum, and temporoparietal junction/superior temporal sulcus (TPJ-STS). Thalamic hypoconnectivity with TPJ-STS was also associated with overall negative symptoms and anhedonia. Conclusions This study identifies the thalamus as a central hub of negative symptom-related dysfunction in SSD and highlights specific thalamic subnetworks as potential targets for circuit-based interventions.
items.authors: Kunitoki, K.; Adhikari, B. M.; Ankeeta, A.; Gao, S.; Ma, Y.; Straub, K. T.; Dos Santos Alves Maria, G.; Pagan, A. F.; Warner, A. R.; Du, X.; Kochunov, P.; Hong, L. E.

items.title: Clustered and diffuse sensory corticostriatal wirings define complementary interneuron circuits
items.abstract: In the striatum, interneurons tightly control the activity of output neurons, the striatal projection neurons (SPN). Among these striatal interneurons, parvalbumin-expressing (PV) and somatostatin-expressing (SOM) cells exhibit markedly distinct electrophysiological and anatomical properties, suggesting differential integration into striatal circuits and distinct forms of feedforward inhibition onto SPN. However, it remains unclear whether differences already emerge at the level of corticostriatal connectivity and if they shape specific interactions with cortical inputs to SPN. Here, we investigated the spatial organization of the projections from the primary and secondary somatosensory areas (S1 and S2), onto striatal PV and SOM interneurons and SPN. With a combination of anatomical tracing and functional circuit mapping, we characterized key features of corticostriatal connectivity, including input number, origin, spacing, overlap and strength. We found that input spacing and strength, at both the individual cell and population levels, were the principal features distinguishing PV and SOM interneurons. In contrast, connectivity differed primarily in input number and laminar organization across S1 and S2. Our findings suggest two potential modes of interaction between interneurons and SPN connectivity: one in which PV interneurons receive S1 inputs structured in large clusters, that densely overlap with those of neighboring SPN, providing an anatomical substrate for potential neuronal assemblies. And another in which SOM interneurons also receive abundant cortical inputs, but thinly disseminated across S1 and S2 and that overlap little with those of SPN, potentially shaping these cell integration through input cross-interaction. These cell-type principles of corticostriatal wiring may support distinct forms of striatal computation.
items.authors: Contadini, J.; Fino, E.; Bureau, I.

items.title: Learning source weights for target-position estimation: comparing fixed weights and an input-dependent rule
items.abstract: Estimating an object's location requires combining uncertain measurements. Weights derived from an earlier calibration may become inappropriate when measurement errors change. We examined whether learning from noisy reference measurements improves position estimates, and whether weights computed from current inputs improve further than one learned set of weights used throughout evaluation. In simulations, we generated noisy position measurements of a target that remained fixed within each trial. Each two-input method combined the current measurement with the mean of three initial measurements. Measurement-accuracy reductions and added measurement offsets applied only after initialization. The estimator received no current or previous true target position. We repeated coordinate calibration, training, validation, and independent evaluation 100 times in each of four error conditions. Recalibration and fixed-weight learning explained most of the improvement over earlier supplied weights under reduced measurement accuracy and temporal correlation. With occasional large measurement errors, input-dependent weighting reduced mean squared error by 4.05% relative to learned fixed weights and assigned lower mean weights to measurements with added offsets. Its additional benefit was below 0.5% under independent errors and reduced current accuracy, while fixed weights had slightly lower mean error under temporal correlation. Methods using longer observation histories performed better in several conditions. Sensitivity analysis showed that shared coordinate bias and correlated reference errors limit conclusions about physical accuracy. The results show benefits and limits of recalibration, input-dependent weighting, and observation history within these measurement models.
items.authors: Kobayashi, J.

items.title: SroA links SigS-dependent stress signaling to metabolic remodeling in Staphylococcus aureus
items.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus encounters diverse environmental conditions during colonization and infection, including fluctuations in nutrient availability, oxidative stress, and oxygen limitation. Adaptation to these environments requires regulatory systems that coordinate stress responses with metabolic physiology. The extracytoplasmic function sigma factor SigS contributes to stress adaptation and virulence in S. aureus and directly activates expression of the sroAB operon, which encodes the small proteins SroA and SroB. Previous work demonstrated that SroA participates in feedback regulation of sigS expression, but the broader physiological role of SroA has remained unclear. To further define the regulatory functions of SroA, we performed RNA sequencing following inducible overexpression of sroA in S. aureus. Transcriptome analysis identified altered expression of genes associated with nitrate respiration, nucleotide biosynthesis, stress responses, and nutrient acquisition. Northern blot and quantitative RT-PCR analysis confirmed repression of narG and narJ transcripts following SroA overexpression. Consistent with these transcriptional changes, SroA overexpression impaired nitrate reduction and produced a modest but significant growth disadvantage under anaerobic conditions in chemically defined medium supplemented with glucose and nitrate. In addition to repression of nitrate respiration genes, SroA overexpression reduced expression of genes involved in de novo purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis, while transcripts associated with stress responses and nutrient acquisition, including sosA and pstS, were increased. Together, these findings support a role for SroA in modulating nitrate respiration-associated pathways and growth under conditions supporting anaerobic respiration, linking SigS-dependent stress signaling to metabolic adaptation in S. aureus.
items.authors: Alqahtani, S. A.; Pasham, S.; Alsulami, J.; Al Ali, A.; Aubee, J. I.; Tomlinson, B. R.; Kennedy, S.; Felton, E. A.; Shaw, L. N.; Thompson, K. M.
items.title_zh: SroA将SigS依赖的应激信号与金黄色葡萄球菌的代谢重塑联系起来
items.summary_zh: 金黄色葡萄球菌在定植和感染过程中面临多种环境条件，包括营养可用性波动、氧化应激和缺氧。适应这些环境需要协调应激反应与代谢生理的调控系统。外细胞功能σ因子SigS在应激适应和毒力中发挥作用，并直接激活sroAB操纵子的表达，编码小蛋白SroA和SroB。研究表明，SroA参与sigS表达的反馈调控，但其更广泛的生理角色尚不明确。为进一步定义SroA的调控功能，我们在金黄色葡萄球菌中进行sroA的诱导过表达后进行了RNA测序。转录组分析发现与硝酸盐呼吸、核苷酸生物合成、应激反应和营养获取相关的基因表达发生了改变。Northern印迹和定量RT-PCR分析确认SroA过表达后narG和narJ转录本受到抑制。与这些转录变化一致，SroA过表达削弱了硝酸盐还原，并在补充葡萄糖和硝酸盐的化学定义培养基中，在厌氧条件下产生了适度但显著的生长劣势。

items.title: Lactate epigenetically shapes tumor cell states in H3K27M diffuse midline gliomas
items.abstract: H3K27M diffuse midline gliomas (DMGs) are lethal and lack treatment options. These tumors exhibit tumor heterogeneity with aggressive oligodendrocyte precursor (OPC)- and mesenchymal (MES)-like cell states. Because all tumor cells bear H3K27M, tumor heterogeneity has been attributed to microenvironmental cues that remain obscure. H3K27M DMGs exhibit increased glycolysis and the Warburg effect to produce lactate. Lactate can directly modify histone lysines including H3K27Lac, and we hypothesized that lactate epigenetically regulates tumor cell states in H3K27M DMGs. We undertook a comprehensive and integrated analysis of H3K27M DMG cell lines, animal models, tumor tissues, and magnetic resonance spectroscopy in patients to decipher the epigenetic roles of lactate. Here, we report that H3K27M cells uniquely exhibit elevation of the activating mark H3K27Lac. We observed significant heterogeneity in lactate levels within tumors, and the addition of exogenous lactate resulted in marked increases in H3K27Lac and the expression of critical OPC- and MES- like gene signature genes, which correlates with poorer patient outcomes. Our therapeutic approach leverages the inhibition of CBP/p300, which deposits both H3K27Lac and H3K27ac. Targeting CBP/p300 effectively reduces both H3K27Lac and H3K27ac levels, suppresses key OPC- and MES-like signatures, and shows efficacy in preclinical models. Collectively, our findings identify lactate as a key player in the epigenetic regulation of tumor cell state heterogeneity and suggest that targeting this pathway offers promise for addressing the heterogeneous complexities of H3K27M DMGs.

items.title_zh: 乳酸在H3K27M弥漫性中线胶质瘤中的表观遗传调控作用
items.summary_zh: H3K27M弥漫性中线胶质瘤（DMGs）致命且缺乏治疗选择。这些肿瘤表现出肿瘤异质性，具有侵袭性的少突胶质细胞前体（OPC）和间充质（MES）样细胞状态。我们假设乳酸在H3K27M DMGs中通过表观遗传机制调控肿瘤细胞状态。我们对H3K27M DMG细胞系、动物模型、肿瘤组织和患者的磁共振波谱进行了综合分析。结果显示，H3K27M细胞中激活标记H3K27Lac显著升高，肿瘤内乳酸水平存在显著异质性，外源性乳酸的添加导致H3K27Lac和关键OPC及MES样基因表达显著增加，与患者预后不良相关。我们的治疗策略通过抑制CBP/p300来降低H3K27Lac和H3K27ac水平，抑制关键的OPC和MES样基因特征，并在临床前模型中显示出疗效。

items.title: Dual regulation of chemical stress-induced DDI2/3 expression by a transcription factor Fzf1 and nucleosome in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
items.abstract: DDI2 and DDI3 (DDI2/3) are duplicated genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae that exhibit strong induction by a transcription factor Fzf1 in response to chemical treatments like cyanamide (CY) and methyl methanesulfonate (MMS). Although, like DDI2/3, SSU1, YHB1 and YNR064C also contain an Fzf1-binding consensus sequence CS2 and are coordinately regulated by Fzf1, these genes are only modestly induced by CY and MMS. To identify additional cis-acting elements in the DDI2/3 promoter, we made DDI2/3 promoter deletions in a reporter system and identified upstream repressing sequences (URS) spanning 480 nucleotides. To test a hypothesis that the chromatin structure constitutes the URS, we utilized a yeast strain capable of histone H3/H4 depletion by shifting carbon sources. Following histone depletion, DDI2/3 were strongly induced in an Fzf1 dependent manner, while YHB1 was repressed. Interestingly, under histone depletion conditions, CY or MMS treatment further increased expression of all Fzf1-regulated genes to comparable levels in an Fzf1 dependent manner. A genome-wide MNase-seq analysis showed that CY treatment reduced the nucleosome occupancy at the mapped DDI2/3 URS region in wild-type cells, but not in in fzf1{Delta} cells. These findings collectively indicate that Fzf1 plays dual roles in regulating the DDI2/3 response to CY. Firstly, it binds CS2 and serves as a transcription activator. Secondly, it is required for the chromatin remodeling at URS. This two-tier regulation at the DDI2/3 promoter helps to explain why DDI2/3 achieve much higher fold induction by CY and MMS than other Fzf1-regulated genes, suggesting Fzf1 to be a candidate pioneer transcription factor.
items.authors: Du, Y.; Lin, A.; Brown, J. A. R.; Howe, L.; Xao, W.

items.title: Metatranscriptomic Identification of Co- and Incidental Infections in Marine Turtles Reveals Complex Disease Aetiologies
items.abstract: Traditional veterinary pathology investigations on wild animals generally conclude a primary cause of death based on a combination of observed clinical signs, gross and microscopic lesions, microbial culture and PCR. However, these methods may fail to capture the broader microbial community of the host. We employed metatranscriptomic sequencing to characterise the potential pathobiome of necropsied marine turtles, comparing these findings with corresponding veterinary pathology reports. Tissue samples were collected from 76 individuals spanning three species of marine turtles -- the green turtle (Chelonia mydas), the hawksbill turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata), and the loggerhead turtle (Caretta caretta) -- across the coastline of New South Wales, Australia. Reported causes of mortality ranged from infectious disease to trauma. We identified a diverse range of parasites within the genera Neospirochis, Hapalotrema, Paraorgymatobothrium, Eimeria and Callitetrarhynchus, and bacteria including the genera Aeromonas, Clostridium, and Vibrio. Novel viruses of the families Astroviridae, Caliciviridae, Hepaciviridae, Hepeviridae, Nyamivirdae, Orthomyxoviridae, Picobirnaviridae and Rhabdoviridae were also identified. In cases where infectious disease was noted in the pathology report, we frequently observed high pathogen read counts consistent with the listed primary diagnoses. However, we also detected a range of incidental infections involving eukaryotic parasites, bacteria, and viruses. The diversity of infectious agents detected in marine turtles suggests that the observed disease outcomes are unlikely to be driven by a single causative agent, but rather by complex interactions between host health, the pathobiome, and environmental stressors. We discuss the potential implications for turtle health and conservation.
items.authors: Lim, L.; Lang, B.; Fenton, H.; Rose, K. C.; Hall, J.; Holmes, E. C.

items.title: Patronin condensation integrates recognition, protection and organization of microtubule minus ends
items.abstract: Microtubule minus ends are central to non-centrosomal microtubule organization, yet how their recognition, protection and molecular organization are integrated remains unclear. Here we show that Drosophila Patronin forms dynamic condensates at microtubule minus ends through a prion-like domain (PrLD). PrLD-mediated condensation cooperates with the CKK domain and a second CKK-independent recognition region to convert weak or broadly distributed microtubule-binding activities into persistent minus-end recognition and tracking. Replacing the PrLD with a heterologous phase-separating HNRNPA1 IDR restores minus-end targeting, indicating that condensation capacity rather than PrLD primary sequence is critical. Patronin condensates further form a protective cap that resists minus-end depolymerization and recruit the cytoskeletal regulators Sas-4, Katanin and Ena. Disrupting PrLD multivalency impairs Patronin localization at multiple developmental sites and causes early organismal lethality. Thus, Patronin condensation creates a physiologically essential microtubule minus-end compartment coupling end recognition, stabilization and cytoskeletal organization.
items.authors: Zhang, B.; Yang, J.; Yu, S.; Zhou, K.; He, L.; Huang, L.; Liang, X.; Wang, H.; Chen, J.

items.title: A dsRNA Virus Converts Early Endosomes into Stable Replication Organelles Through Maturation Arrest and Retrograde Transport
items.abstract: Infectious bursal disease virus (IBDV) and infectious pancreatic necrosis virus (IPNV) are major animal pathogens that impose a heavy burden on the poultry and aquaculture industries. Yet, major aspects of their unique replication program remain unknown. IBDV is unusual among double-stranded RNA viruses in that it replicates in association with host endosomes. We previously demonstrated this association to be orchestrated by the viral protein VP3 and the early endosomal lipid phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate [PtdIns(3)P], suggesting an essential role for VP3 in forming birnaviruses specialized replication compartments. Here, combining high-resolution fluorescence and correlative light-electron microscopy with diverse molecular and biochemical analyses, we define how the IBDV protein VP3 targets and remodels host endosomes, and establish that endosome-associated replication is conserved in members of the Birnaviridae family. We show that IBDV VP3 targets early endosomes via the PtdIns(3)P effector Early Endosomal Antigen 1 (EEA1) to arrest their maturation and prompt their association with the Golgi complex via ESCPE-1-mediated retrograde transport. We further show that IPNV also exploits endosomal membranes for replication in a PtdIns(3)P dependent manner, although for this virus VP3 engages endosomes through an EEA1-independent mechanism yet to be determined. This work uncovers how birnaviruses exploit a single viral protein to orchestrate endosome remodeling and intracellular trafficking to establish specialized replication compartments while revealing both conserved and host-adapted features of birnaviruses replication.
items.authors: Gimenez, M. C.; Ferrero, D.; Issa, M.; Moussaoui, S.; Cabrini, M.; Reboucas Paixao, A.; Liu, L.; Ganesan, S.; Acharya, D.; Boermel, M.; Zaremberg, V.; Verdaguer, N.; Terebiznik, M.

items.title: ESX-1 remodels the Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen storage compartment in macrophages
items.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) secretes antigenic proteins that drive protective T cell responses, yet how Mtb intracellular localization affects the trafficking and spatiotemporal distribution of mycobacterial antigens in macrophages remains elusive. Here, we developed a split fluorescent protein reporter to monitor the dynamics of the TB vaccine lead antigen Ag85B in infected human macrophages. We discovered that Mtb triggers the formation and remodeling of two distinct types of Mtb Antigen Storage Compartment (MASC) that retains Ag85 within macrophage membranes. Using subcellular spatial proteomics, we profiled the composition of the MASC, identifying both the Mtb and macrophage proteins that constitute these compartments. Unexpectedly, MASCs are defined by metabolic compartmentalization and rewiring to lipid metabolism in both the macrophage and Mtb. Thus, Mtb builds via the ESX-1 system a metabolically distinct antigen storage compartment in immune cells, with potential implications for antigen selection and delivery in TB vaccine development.
items.authors: Luk, C. H.; Auchynnikava, T.; Fearns, A.; Ortiz Canseco, J.; Lockwood, P. K.; Charoy, C.; Gutierrez, M. G.
items.title_zh: ESX-1重塑巨噬细胞中的结核分枝杆菌抗原储存区
items.summary_zh: 结核分枝杆菌（Mtb）分泌抗原蛋白以驱动保护性T细胞反应，但Mtb在细胞内的定位如何影响巨噬细胞中抗原的运输和时空分布仍不清楚。我们开发了一种分裂荧光蛋白报告系统，以监测感染人类巨噬细胞中结核疫苗主要抗原Ag85B的动态。研究发现，Mtb诱导形成和重塑两种不同类型的Mtb抗原储存区（MASC），在巨噬细胞膜内保留Ag85。通过亚细胞空间蛋白组学，我们分析了MASC的组成，识别出构成这些区的Mtb和巨噬细胞蛋白。意外的是，MASC通过代谢区隔和脂质代谢重塑而被定义。因此，Mtb通过ESX-1系统在免疫细胞中构建了一个代谢上独特的抗原储存区，这对结核疫苗开发中的抗原选择和递送具有潜在影响。

items.title: Disentangling maternal pregnancy and fetal-specific plasma signatures through integrated proteomics and site-specific N-glycoproteomics
items.abstract: During pregnancy, mother and fetus co-exist albeit as two physiologically distinct individuals, connected through the placenta and the umbilical cord. This connection allows for the exchange of vital substances, while individual blood homeostasis remains intact. We hypothesized that comparing maternal and cord plasma (N-glyco)proteomes would provide insights into the biological communication and unique physiological state of each individual. As comparing only matched maternal and umbilical cord blood plasma misses a crucial identifier in determining whether observed changes are related to infancy, pregnancy or both, we designed a triad study by adding a non-pregnant women control group. This allowed us to distinguish pregnancy-specific proteins and their potentially altered N-glycosylation from those in infancy. We found that the fetus and mother have distinct proteomes, N-glycoproteoforms and alternative complement regulation. Moreover, we observed that pregnancy in women led to specific N-glycosylation changes on a select set of primarily HDL-associated and acute-phase proteins. Lastly, our data provide evidence for an early fetal development of the humoral immune system as especially fetal IgM displayed distinctive N-glycosylation signatures.
items.authors: Jager, S.; Kalaidopoulou Nteak, S.; Reznikov, G.; Rodrigues Ianiski, F.; Visser, R.; Sinitcyn, P.; Vidarsson, G.; Heck, A. J. R.

items.title: Environmental correlates of understory plant diversity and distribution in a temperate climate-change refugium
items.abstract: Aim Regional climate-change refugia - areas where abiotic conditions related to hydrology and topography sustain unique plant communities despite an otherwise unsuitable regional macroclimate - have been essential for maintaining biodiversity through past climatic transitions. At fine spatial scales, regional refugia can also contain microrefugia, where canopy structure and topography strongly buffer understory microclimate. We tested whether such microrefugia structure understory plant communities within a regional climate-change refugium, where sheltered, groundwater-fed canyons have sustained a biogeographically distinctive flora since the Last Glacial Maximum. Location Temperate forest in the North American Great Plains, Nebraska, USA. Methods In a 20.2-ha forest inventory plot spanning a sharp topographic gradient, we quantified diversity, composition, and distributions and of understory woody and herbaceous plants across seven functional groups along fine-scale topographic, light, and soil moisture gradients. Results Woody species density and richness were significantly higher within sheltered microrefugia in canyon bottoms and on forested slopes and strongly decreased with increasing canopy openness, whereas C4 grass richness was highest along the exposed, high-light forest-prairie ecotone, reflecting divergent functional group responses to microclimate buffering. Soil moisture structured richness across functional groups: woody plant and C3 grass richness peaked at moisture extremes, sedge richness at intermediate moisture variability, and C4 grass richness declined with increasing moisture variability. Both woody and herbaceous understory plants showed strong variation in composition with topography; in particular, woody seedlings and graminoids exhibited strong species turnover with increasing elevation. Main Conclusions These results demonstrate that topographically driven microrefugia support disproportionate understory biodiversity and suggest that protecting both regional refugia and finer-scale microrefugia will be critical for conserving plant communities, including species documented exclusively in microrefugia, as macroclimate continues to change.
items.authors: McNichol, B. H.; Dunn, C.; Granville, D.; Hoffart, L.; McGuire, B.; Ridder, A.; Wang, R.; Russo, S. E.

items.title: STEM-LM: Spatio-Temporal Ecological Modeling via Masked Language Model for Multi-Species Distribution
items.abstract: Species distribution models (SDMs) are central to biodiversity forecasting and conservation decision-making. As ecological datasets grow in size, dimensionality, and resolution, there is a need for flexible yet scalable SDMs tailored to large-scale species observation data. Inspired by the masked modeling approach in natural language processing and genomics, if we treat each species' presence or absence as a token, and a site's species assemblage together with its spatio-temporal and ecological covariates as analogous to a sentence, we can learn joint co-occurrence structure by reconstructing masked species from their neighboring sites. We propose STEM-LM, a Transformer-based SDM that applies masked language modeling to multi-species distribution modeling with explicit consideration of spatio-temporal structure. By applying dynamic masking rates during training, a single trained model can support both purely spatio-temporal/ecological prediction and prediction conditioned on arbitrary subsets of observed species. On a North American butterfly dataset, a Northeast US demersal fish trawl survey, and a global plant distribution dataset, STEM-LM has the highest discrimination (AUROC) among all compared methods, and its rank-monotonicity (continuous Boyce index) is either the best or close to the best.
items.authors: Li, J. K.; Lim, W.; Rheem, R.; Callahan, F.; Raskin, L. Y.; Lemmon-Kishi, M.; Nielsen, R.

items.title: Abundance redistribution increases predator-prey interaction potentials among North American birds
items.abstract: Species are dramatically shifting their geographical ranges, yet the consequences of these spatial redistributions on species interactions have not been examined at broad spatial and temporal scales. Here, we investigate how the redistribution of species abundance over the past 50 years affects the potential for predator-prey interactions among North American birds. We first predict potential predator-prey interactions based on existing data and functional traits, then construct a novel, abundance-weighted metric of interaction potential for each pair of predator and prey in local communities. Across North America, the potential for predator-prey interactions has been increasing over time. We further show that this widespread increasing trend in interaction potentials is mostly driven by higher abundances of predator species. The spatial redistributions of predators and prey lead to turnover of interactions within local communities, and the turnover is less associated with changes in climate but more associated with human-induced land use changes. Our novel approach and results highlight the importance of considering traits, abundance, and species interactions - including known and potential interactions - when studying the ecological consequences of species range shifts.
items.authors: Zou, H.-X.; Hsieh, C.; Zarnetske, P. L.; Zhu, K.; Weeks, B. C.

items.title: Categorical rhythmic patterns do not predict song preference in zebra finches
items.abstract: Categorical rhythmic patterns are fundamental features found in language and music across cultures. In humans, these rhythmic patterns occur in both vocal production and perceptual preference, highlighting a link between rhythmic production and preference. Categorical rhythmic patterns have recently been identified in animal vocalisations too, but whether rhythm production is linked with rhythmic preferences in non-human animals remains unclear. Within this context, zebra finches (Taeniopygia castanotis) are of particular interest, as both sexes develop a song preference, and their song has been suggested to exhibit an isochronous temporal structure. Here, we tested for the first time whether zebra finches prefer songs containing discrete rhythmic patterns, using operant preference tests with either two or four rhythmic patterns. Our results show that no categorical rhythmic pattern was consistently preferred across the population, although responses varied among individuals. These findings indicate that categorical rhythmic patterns are unlikely to be a primary driver of song preference in zebra finches. Together with previous work in other vocal-learning birds, our results suggest that preferences for categorical rhythmic patterns may not be universal and could instead reflect species-specific features of vocal displays rather than the rhythmic categories characteristic of human music.
items.authors: Maiolini, M.; Spierings, M.

items.title: "Mine" or "yours"? Acoustic structure of food calls predicts sharing decisions in marmosets
items.abstract: Foraging and feeding are often associated with vocalisations across animal species. Food calls may function to claim ownership of resources or recruit others to feeding sites, yet their potential role in facilitating food sharing remains poorly understood. This study investigates the relationship between food calls and food-sharing behaviour in common marmosets (Callithrix jacchus), focusing on adult-infant interactions, where food transfers are most frequent. We analysed over 1000 food interactions across six groups, categorising events as non-sharing (without begging or despite begging) or sharing (proactive, resisted, or facilitated). We examined the spectro-temporal structure of food calls produced immediately before each interaction. Food transfers were more likely to occur when preceded by a food call, suggesting a functional link between food calls and sharing. Random forest models reliably classified food calls according to interaction type, while generalized linear mixed models identified acoustic variation associated with sharing outcomes. Our results suggest that food calls encode information to either encourage or deter conspecific (infant) approach, influencing food transfer outcomes. These findings highlight the role of food calls in modulating social interactions around food in marmosets, advancing our understanding of vocal communication and its integration with cooperative behaviours in primates.
items.authors: Wierucka, K.; Winiger, S.; Sehner, S.; Burkart, J. M.

items.title: A look inside the net: freshwater turtles assort with conspecifics in feeding aggregations
items.abstract: Historically, non-avian reptiles were assumed to be non-social - yet recent studies show diverse social behaviours in squamates, crocodilians, and turtles. Here, we investigate social structure within feeding aggregations of three freshwater turtle species caught in baited traps in a coastal marsh over 12 years. In 488 instances in which traps contained turtles, 45% contained multiple individuals, and these aggregations were strongly positively assorted by species. Midland painted turtles (Chrysemys picta marginata) and Blanding's turtles (Emydoidea blandingii) were captured with conspecifics more often than expected in non-social null models. Snapping turtles (Chelydra serpentina), the largest species in this study, were captured with conspecifics at a frequency similar to that predicted by null models, and were avoided by heterospecifics. This suggests that species differences play a role in how feeding aggregations are structured, with painted and Blanding's turtles driving strong positive species assortment while avoiding snapping turtles around food sources. We did not detect significant intraspecific sex assortment in any of the three species, nor did turtle body size strongly affect the probability of aggregating with conspecifics at the perceived food source in the traps. Our study illustrates how long-term monitoring data can be used to investigate social structure in wild populations, an approach that may be valuable for species of conservation concern.
items.authors: Menzies, C. M.; James, R.; Riley, J.; Davy, C. M.; Dakin, R.

items.title: Ambient-Condition Visualization of Metalloenzyme Reactive Intermediates Enabled by the SHINERS Paradigm
items.abstract: Reactive metal-oxygen intermediates are central to metalloenzyme catalysis, yet their low populations and short lifetimes make vibrational characterization under aqueous reaction conditions challenging. Here, we establish shell-isolated nanoparticle-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SHINERS) as a powerful vibrational approach for visualizing reaction-associated metal-ligand signatures of reactive metalloenzyme states. Across the heme and non-heme iron enzymes TauD, VioC, CYP119, and TqaLNc, isotope-sensitive features provide vibrational information on reactive coordination states. In TauD and VioC, isotope-sensitive features provide vibrational characterization of Fe(IV)=O intermediates. In CYP119, an isotope-sensitive Fe(IV)=O vibration is assigned to P450 Compound I generated by m-CPBA, including under lauric-acid turnover conditions. Most notably, in TqaLNc, combined 18O- and 15N-sensitive vibrational responses support formation of the proposed (R)HN-Fe(IV)=O coordination state and the dynamic-coordination mechanism underlying selective C-N bond formation. These results demonstrate that SHINERS can serve as a powerful technique for the in situ vibrational visualization of reactive intermediates and their coordination states in metalloenzyme catalysis.
items.authors: Liao, L.; Li, Q.-Q.; Zhang, X.; Liu, J.; Chen, Z.-H.; Zhou, Y.; Bao, Z.; Ma, H.; Yang, L.; Wang, X.; Wang, C.; Ren, B.; Li, J.-F.; Wang, B.

items.title: Circular Data Analysis for Spatial Omics
items.abstract: Many biological quantities in omics are inherently periodic or directional, including circadian phase, cell-cycle position, and cellular orientation. Treating such quantities as ordinary linear variables can introduce artificial discontinuities and obscure biological interpretation. Circular methods are well developed across directional statistics, bioinformatics, and spatial statistics, but practical guidance for omics applications remains limited. We present key considerations for circular data analysis in single-cell and spatial omics, including the provenance and observational unit of the circular quantity, the inferential or predictive objective, the distinction between tissue composition and residual spatial dependence, and the choice of appropriate models. We describe relevant approaches for circular representation, inference, clustering, regression, machine learning, and spatial analysis, together with representative R software. Their practical use is illustrated through spatial transcriptomic case studies of derived circadian peak phase in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease and latent cell-cycle position in human ovarian cancer. These examples demonstrate how the definition of the angle, its observational unit, and tissue heterogeneity shape appropriate analysis and interpretation, including when spatial modeling is not warranted. We conclude with practical recommendations and directions for future methodological development.
items.authors: Shin, J.; Yoo, J.; Cho, Y.; Gupta, A.; Mao, P.-H.; Thakkar, K.; Eddy, T. A.; Chung, K. J.; Kim, J.; Jeon, H.; Xie, J.; Chung, D.

items.title: Complex folding kinetics of multi-domain proteins disentangled with periodic forces by magnetic tweezers
items.abstract: Force spectroscopy enables direct investigation of the interplay between free energy and transition kinetics in proteins and nucleic acids. However, multi-domain proteins often display multiple intermediate structures with diverse stabilities and kinetics, making equilibrium conditions difficult to achieve and out-of-equilibrium experiments challenging to interpret. We introduce a single-molecule force spectroscopy assay using periodic forces and high-resolution magnetic tweezers to bridge different stabilities, selectively enhance intermediate populations, and rigorously analyze multi-domain protein folding kinetics at quasi-equilibrium. By applying well-defined periodic square force functions with tunable steady states, we first validate our framework on the two-state folder {lambda}6-85, demonstrating that periodic force experiments can reproduce equilibrium kinetics. Extending this approach to the multi-domain protein mimic (Protein L), we show that tuning force, frequency, and amplitude enhances populations of distinct intermediate states. Finally, we dissect the entangled states of the hybrid two-domain protein {lambda}-L, where a 100-fold difference in domain kinetics precludes equilibrium analysis, by expanding from a two-state to a three-state periodic force protocol to direct intermediate populations. Our assay and analysis framework open new possibilities for deciphering complex multi-domain folds and their multi-dimensional folding pathways.
items.authors: Quintana-Catano, C. A.; Hartmann, A.; Schlierf, M.
items.title_zh: 利用磁镊子研究多域蛋白的复杂折叠动力学
items.summary_zh: 力谱学能够直接研究蛋白质和核酸中自由能与转变动力学的相互作用。然而，多域蛋白常表现出多种中间结构，具有不同的稳定性和动力学，使得平衡条件难以实现，非平衡实验的解释也具有挑战性。我们引入了一种利用周期性力和高分辨率磁镊子的单分子力谱实验，旨在连接不同的稳定性，选择性增强中间态的丰度，并严格分析多域蛋白的折叠动力学。在对双态折叠体{lambda}6-85进行验证后，我们证明了周期性力实验可以重现平衡动力学。进一步扩展到多域蛋白模型（蛋白L），我们展示了调节力、频率和幅度可以增强不同中间态的丰度。最后，我们通过将双态周期性力协议扩展到三态，解析了混合双域蛋白{lambda}-L的纠缠态，克服了域动力学的100倍差异对平衡分析的限制。我们的实验和分析框架为解读复杂蛋白折叠提供了新思路。
items.l1_lead: 利用周期性力和高分辨率磁镊子，我们成功研究了多域蛋白的折叠动力学，揭示了不同中间态的丰度调节机制，为理解复杂蛋白折叠提供了新方法。
items.l2_summary:
本研究利用磁镊子技术探讨多域蛋白的复杂折叠动力学，重点关注蛋白质和核酸中自由能与转变动力学的相互作用。力谱学作为一种直接研究手段，能够揭示蛋白质折叠过程中的多种中间结构及其稳定性和动力学特征。然而，多域蛋白常常表现出多种中间态，导致平衡条件难以实现，非平衡实验的解释也变得复杂。为了解决这一问题，研究团队引入了一种结合周期性力和高分辨率磁镊子的单分子力谱实验，旨在连接不同稳定性，选择性增强中间态的丰度，并对多域蛋白的折叠动力学进行严格分析。

在对双态折叠体λ6-85的验证中，研究表明周期性力实验能够有效重现平衡动力学。进一步扩展至多域蛋白模型（蛋白L），研究发现通过调节施加的力、频率和幅度，可以显著增强不同中间态的丰度。这一发现为理解多域蛋白的折叠过程提供了新的视角。最后，研究团队将双态周期性力协议扩展至三态，成功解析了混合双域蛋白λ-L的纠缠态，克服了域动力学之间高达100倍的差异对平衡分析的限制。

通过这一系列实验和分析，研究为复杂蛋白折叠的解读提供了新的思路，展示了磁镊子技术在生物物理研究中的潜力和应用价值。这项研究不仅深化了对多域蛋白折叠过程的理解，也为未来相关领域的研究奠定了基础。

items.title: Pathogenic DRP1 variants reveal a role for biomolecular condensation in mitochondrial fission
items.abstract: Fission is essential for proper mitochondrial function and for cellular homeostasis. Dysfunction in mitochondrial fission is associated with several neurological disorders, including the rare and lethal encephalopathy EMPF1, which is caused by de novo heterozygous DNM1L variants. DNM1L encodes the mitochondrial fission mechanoenzyme DRP1, which can intrinsically self-assemble and induce membrane scission. Wild-type DRP1 puncta that appear throughout the cytoplasm are thought to be pre-scission complexes of well-ordered oligomeric assemblies. Immunofluorescence imaging of patient-derived EMPF1 fibroblasts carrying assembly-deficient DNM1L variants reveals elongated mitochondrial networks consistent with impaired fission. Despite this loss-of-function phenotype, these cells retain essentially wild-type numbers of DRP1 puncta. We confirmed the previously reported inability of purified pathogenic DRP1 variants p.Gly363Asp and p.Gly401Ser to assemble under conditions in which WT DRP1 forms helical polymers. Under macromolecular crowding conditions, however, both wild-type and mutant DRP1 access condensed states whose formation depends on protein concentration and solution conditions. Acute treatment of EMPF1 fibroblasts with 1,6-hexanediol preferentially alters DRP1 puncta fluorescence intensity and distribution in mutant cells relative to wild type, indicating genotype-dependent differences in puncta material properties. Together, these findings support a model in which DRP1 puncta occupy a continuum of condensed states, only a subset of which mature into fission-competent assemblies, revealing biomolecular condensation as a previously unrecognized layer of DRP1 regulation. Biasing DRP1 along this continuum may provide a mechanistic basis for impaired fission in EMPF1 and suggest opportunities to restore productive assembly in select pathogenic contexts.
items.authors: Ross, K. A.; Travis, A. M.; Harwig, M. C.; Young, M. S.; Rodas Montejo, E. H.; Farah, M. J.; Donohue, M. J.; Taylor, R. W.; Olahova, M.; Hill, R. B.

items.title: Discovering Latent Scientific Concepts through Discrete Representation Learning
items.abstract: Scientific imaging is undergoing a fundamental transformation. Advances in multiplex immunofluorescence, computational pathology, and electron microscopy now enable observation of biological and physical systems at unprecedented spatial resolution. Rather than simply classifying known objects, these data offer the opportunity to discover previously unknown organizational principles. However, scientific image datasets are typically highly curated, information-rich, and limited in size, making reliable representation learning particularly challenging. We show that standard continuous self-supervised adaptation can become unstable in this regime, allowing teacher representations to drift and degrading downstream transfer. We introduce Kodiak, a discrete representation learning architecture that discovers latent scientific concepts through Sinkhorn-balanced codebook assignments. Instead of learning unconstrained continuous embeddings, Kodiak constructs a reusable vocabulary of discrete concepts that provides stable supervision for both masked-patch prediction and cross-view representation learning within a single-stage framework. Across five scientific imaging domains, including multiplex immunofluorescence for pancreatic cancer pathology and scanning electron microscopy, Kodiak consistently improves representation quality under both continued foundation-model adaptation and training from scratch. Beyond improved classification and transfer,the learned concepts are interpretable, reusable, and produce spatially coherent concept maps that support applications such as cell phenotyping, segmentation-free patch phenotyping, spatial niche discovery, tissue organization, and materials characterization. We view Kodiak as the representation-learning engine of our foundation model for spatial biology. More broadly, our results suggest that discrete representation learning provides a principled foundation for discovering reusable latent scientific concepts that can accelerate scientific interpretation across imaging domains.
items.authors: Stoimcev, M.; Verma, M.; Filliol, A.; Skamagki, M.; Flowers, S.; Cohen, J.; Azadian, Z.; Newlin, N.; Abdel-Mottaleb, M. S.; Dzeroski, S.; Romesser, P.; Lowe, S.; Dimitrova, N.

items.title: Genetic dissection of DNA damage response pathways reveals divergent modulation of PD-1 blockade response in colorectal cancer
items.abstract: Although MSI-H/dMMR colorectal cancers and the rarer subset with pathogenic POLE exonuclease domain mutations can benefit from immune checkpoint blockade, MSS colorectal cancer remains largely refractory, raising the question of whether other DNA damage response defects may also confer sensitivity to immunotherapy. Here, we performed a systematic in vivo screen of recurrently altered DNA damage response (DDR) genes to determine whether distinct repair defects modulate response to PD-1 blockade in MSS colorectal cancer. Using a genome-edited murine model in immunocompetent mice, we found that DDR perturbations produced heterogeneous outcomes, indicating that the immunologic consequences of DNA repair deficiency may be pathway-specific. Loss of Brca1, Brca2, Atm, and Fanca enhanced response to anti-PD-1 therapy, whereas Atr and Msh6 deficiency were associated with poor benefit. Brca1/2-deficient tumors showed the strongest regressions, supporting a link between core homologous recombination deficiency and increased immune sensitivity. In an independent cohort of colorectal cancer patients treated with ICB from the MSK-IMPACT Clinical Sequencing Cohort, BRCA1 alterations were associated with improved survival status, while FANCA alterations showed a similar trend. Because ATM is therapeutically targetable, we evaluated pharmacologic ATM inhibition in MSS colorectal cancer. Sustained ATM inhibition induced immune-related transcriptional programs in vitro and, when administered as a pre-treatment in vivo, enhanced the antitumor activity of PD-1 blockade. Together, these findings suggest that selected DDR alterations may represent candidate biomarkers of immunotherapy sensitivity, while ATM inhibition may provide a rational combination strategy to enhance PD-1 blockade in MSS colorectal cancer.
items.authors: Fece de la Cruz, F.; Wong, E.; Barnes, H.; Fella, K.; Curtis, J.; Phat, S.; Myers, D. T.; Patel, P. S.; Braverman, J.; Yilmaz, O. H.; Corcoran, R. B.
items.title_zh: DNA损伤响应通路的遗传解析揭示结直肠癌中PD-1阻断反应的不同调节
items.summary_zh: 尽管MSI-H/dMMR结直肠癌及少数具有致病性POLE外核酸酶域突变的亚型可从免疫检查点阻断中获益，但MSS结直肠癌仍然大多无反应，提出了其他DNA损伤响应缺陷是否也能增强免疫治疗敏感性的问题。我们在免疫功能正常的小鼠模型中系统筛查了反复改变的DNA损伤响应（DDR）基因，以确定不同修复缺陷是否调节MSS结直肠癌对PD-1阻断的反应。结果发现，DDR扰动产生了异质性结果，表明DNA修复缺陷的免疫学后果可能是通路特异性的。Brca1、Brca2、Atm和Fanca的缺失增强了对抗PD-1治疗的反应，而Atr和Msh6的缺失则与较差的获益相关。Brca1/2缺失肿瘤显示出最强的回归，支持核心同源重组缺陷与免疫敏感性增强之间的联系。在MSK-IMPACT临床测序队列中，BRCA1改变与生存状态改善相关，而FANCA改变也显示出类似趋势。由于ATM可作为治疗靶点，我们评估了MSS结直肠癌中的药物ATM抑制。

items.title: CRISPR-Cas9 Editing of Myeloid Lectins Reveals Target-Dependent Transcriptional Remodeling in Tumor-Associated Macrophages
items.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) integrate multiple microenvironmental signals, including lectin-mediated recognition of tumor-associated glycans. Although several myeloid lectins have been implicated in tumor-macrophage interactions, their contributions to immunosuppressive TAM phenotypes remain poorly defined. We implemented a CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) workflow in primary human monocytes to enable comparative loss-of-function interrogation of five potentially immunosuppressive lectins we previously reported. CRISPR-Cas9 RNP delivery conditions were benchmarked in freshly isolated monocytes using CD14 as a technical target, followed by sgRNA editing efficiency screening for CLEC4E, CLEC6A, CD209, SELL, and SIGLEC9 in HeLa S3 cells. Selected guides were applied to primary monocytes before co-culture in a 3D model with BT474 breast cancer cells. Editing was quantified by Sanger-sequencing deconvolution, while co-culture-derived CD45+ macrophages were isolated by fluorescence-activated cell sorting and characterized by bulk RNA sequencing. All five lectins were successfully perturbed, although gene editing efficiency remained target- and donor-dependent. Transcriptomic analysis revealed target-specific reprogramming and recurrent immunometabolic responses. mTORC1 signaling was consistently enriched, together with the remodeling of cholesterol homeostasis, fatty acid metabolism, and oxidative phosphorylation. CLEC6A deletion achieved attenuation of hypoxia-, angiogenesis-, and TNF/NF-kB-associated programs. CD209 and SIGLEC9 deletion similarly reduced hypoxia- and angiogenesis-associated signatures while promoting lipid and oxidative metabolism. CLEC4E perturbation induced broad remodeling of lipid and oxidative metabolism and stress-response, despite comparatively limited editing efficiency. Comparative lectin perturbation thus identified CLEC6A as the strongest candidate for further mechanistic investigation, while CLEC4E showed broad transcriptional remodeling despite lower editing efficiency, supporting its prioritization for improved genetic interrogation. Responses to CD209 and SIGLEC9 targeting further support tumor glycan-myeloid signaling as a regulator of TAM state. Overall, lectin perturbation redirected TAM transcriptional states through distinct immunometabolic programs rather than a uniform pro-inflammatory polarization, highlighting lectin-dependent immunometabolic regulation as a promising axis for further investigation.
items.authors: Trindade, G.; Pinto, M.; Domenici, G.; Escandell, J.; Brito, C.
items.title_zh: CRISPR-Cas9编辑髓系凝集素揭示肿瘤相关巨噬细胞转录重塑
items.summary_zh: 肿瘤相关巨噬细胞（TAMs）整合多种微环境信号，包括凝集素介导的肿瘤相关糖基识别。尽管已有多种髓系凝集素与肿瘤-巨噬细胞相互作用相关，但其对免疫抑制性TAM表型的贡献尚不明确。本研究采用CRISPR-Cas9核糖核蛋白（RNP）工作流程，对五种潜在的免疫抑制性凝集素进行功能缺失比较研究。通过在新鲜分离的单核细胞中使用CD14作为技术靶点，优化了CRISPR-Cas9 RNP递送条件，并在HeLa S3细胞中筛选了CLEC4E、CLEC6A、CD209、SELL和SIGLEC9的sgRNA编辑效率。选定的引导RNA应用于初级单核细胞，并与BT474乳腺癌细胞在3D模型中共培养。通过Sanger测序定量编辑效果，利用荧光激活细胞分选法分离共培养衍生的CD45+巨噬细胞，并通过大规模RNA测序进行表征。所有五种凝集素均成功编辑，尽管基因编辑效率依赖于靶点和供体。转录组分析揭示了靶点特异性重编程和反复的免疫代谢反应，mTORC1信号通路持续富集，同时伴随胆固醇稳态和脂肪酸重塑。

items.title: Telomere Maintenance Is Acquired at Liposarcoma Dedifferentiation, and Genetically Longer Telomeres Are Associated With Liposarcoma Risk
items.abstract: PURPOSEHow sarcoma subtypes engage telomerase versus alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT), and with what consequence, is incompletely defined. METHODSWe analyzed 11,792 patients with sarcoma sequenced across 19 centers in AACR Project GENIE v20.0. Telomerase activation was defined as TERT promoter mutation, amplification, or rearrangement, and ATRX/DAXX inactivation served as the ALT proxy, each assessed only where the assay interrogated the locus. Findings were tested for TERT expression in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), for overall survival (OS) in MSK-IMPACT 50K, and for replication in an independent Foundation Medicine cohort. Mendelian randomization (MR) in FinnGen tested germline telomere length. RESULTSTelomerase activation (8.8%) and ATRX/DAXX loss (8.0%) were mutually exclusive across subtypes (odds ratio [OR], 0.52; 95% CI, 0.29 to 0.92) and segregated by histology. In MDM2-amplified dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS), telomerase was activated through TERT amplification (17.2%) or rearrangement (2.7%), never promoter mutation (0/261), and never with ATRX/DAXX loss (0/49; P = .011). TERT-amplified tumors expressed TERT (TCGA; P = .002), and amplification was largely focal. Telomere maintenance alterations were present in 28.0% of DDLPS versus 8.7% of well-differentiated liposarcoma (P < .001) and predicted shorter OS in DDLPS (hazard ratio, 2.04; 95% CI, 1.23 to 3.39; P = .005). ATRX/DAXX loss was more frequent in uterine than extrauterine leiomyosarcoma in GENIE (adjusted OR, 1.96) and in the independent cohort (OR, 1.95; both P < .001). Genetically longer telomeres were associated with liposarcoma (OR per SD, 4.10; 95% CI, 2.15 to 7.81). CONCLUSIONSarcoma telomere maintenance is histology-specific and mutually exclusive. In liposarcoma it is acquired at dedifferentiation through focal TERT amplification or ALT and identifies DDLPS with inferior survival. CONTEXT SUMMARYO_ST_ABSKey ObjectiveC_ST_ABSWhich telomere maintenance mechanism does each sarcoma subtype use, and when during progression is it acquired? Knowledge GeneratedAcross 11,792 sequenced sarcomas, telomerase activation and ATRX/DAXX loss were mutually exclusive and segregated by histology. Dedifferentiated liposarcoma activated telomerase through TERT amplification or rearrangement, not promoter mutation, acquired telomere maintenance alterations at roughly three times the rate of well-differentiated liposarcoma, and these alterations identified DDLPS with shorter overall survival. Mendelian randomization linked genetically longer telomeres to liposarcoma susceptibility. RelevanceTelomere maintenance status is a candidate prognostic biomarker in DDLPS and a rationale for mechanism-matched evaluation of telomerase-directed and ALT-directed therapies.
items.authors: Pan, M.; Chi, J.; Zhi, L.; Zhou, M. Y.; Bui, N.; Ganjoo, K.

items.title: A Framework to Monitor Editing of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Medical Documentation
items.abstract: Objective: To develop and evaluate a framework for characterizing clinician editing of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated[KS1.1] documentation and assess its feasibility for health system-level monitoring of AI scribes. Materials and Methods: We analyzed outpatient encounters in which an AI scribe was used at a single academic health system, examining the History of Present Illness (HPI) and Assessment and Plan (A&P) sections of notes. We characterized edits on three dimensions[KS2.1][AG2.2]: lexical edit intensity based on Levenshtein distance, embedding edit intensity BERT[KS3.1]Score, and clinical edit intensity based on removed and added UMLS[KS4.1][AG4.2] concepts.[KS5.1][AG5.2] We analyzed the Positive Predictive Value (PPV) of clinical edit intensity as a measure of clinically meaningful editing using clinicians as the gold standard, examined correlations among dimensions, and designed exponentially weighted moving-average control charts to monitor longitudinal changes in clinician editing behavior.[KS6.1][AG6.2] Results: 268,379 encounters were included (267,654 HPI, 267,594 A&P). Clinical edit intensity [ ]1 had an 88.9% PPV for clinically meaningful editing. Lexical and embedding edit intensity were highly correlated (Spearman {rho} 0.95), while clinical edit intensity was less strongly correlated with both ({rho} 0.77-0.81). Longitudinal monitoring detected changes coinciding with system-wide rollout.[KS7.1][AG7.2] Discussion:[KS8.1][AG8.2] Clinicians edited A&Ps more heavily than HPIs, potentially reflecting greater attention to content involving clinical decision-making. Over one-third of sections involved clinical concept changes, and clinical edit intensity identified clinically meaningful edits while providing information complementary to lexical editing measures. Conclusion: Clinician editing can be characterized at scale using complementary editing dimensions, providing a scalable signal for post-deployment surveillance of the human-AI documentation process.

items.title: Simpler is not always better: Phylodynamic misspecification and deep-learning corrections
items.abstract: Phylodynamics bridges the gap between epidemiology and pathogen genetic data. The birth-death (BD) model and its extensions serve to infer the average number of secondary infections R and the infection duration d from time-scaled pathogen phylogenies. Moreover, more complex models add extra parameters, such as the average length of the incubation period, the proportion of superspreaders in the infected population, or the speed-up in detection after contact-tracing. However, these additional parameters come at an important computational cost: While the simplest, BD, model, has a closed-form solution, its extensions do not and require numerical methods for their likelihood computation. This leads to increased computational times and potential numerical errors. Therefore, the BD model remains the favorite researchers' choice for real dataset analyses, and is often applied even in cases where more complex epidemiological aspects are present. We investigated, using simulations, how model misspecification influences inference of R and d in the phylodynamic framework. We showed that the use of models not accounting for various epidemiological aspects leads to bias. In particular the simplest, BD, estimator tends to underestimate R in the presence of super-spreading, incubation or contact-tracing, which might be dangerous from the public health prospective. In contrast, deep-learning-based estimators for complex models, accounting for multiple epidemiological factors, performed well in our simulations both on the data where those factors were present and where they were absent. This motivates the use of complex epidemiologically realistic estimators, whose design has recently become possible thanks to deep learning.
items.authors: XIE, R.; Gascuel, O.; ZHUKOVA, A.

items.title: Effectiveness of an automated text message intervention for weight management in postpartum women with overweight or obesity (Supporting MumS (SMS)): a UK wide, multicentre, two arm, parallel group, randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract: Objective To test the effectiveness of a postpartum behavioural intervention delivered by automated text messaging in reducing weight. Design Two parallel group, multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Setting Recruitment from five areas across the United Kingdom (Belfast, Bradford, Stirling, London and Cardiff) through healthcare and community pathways, including social media. Participants A diverse sample of 892 women between 6 weeks and 24 months postpartum, aged 18 years or more and with a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 or more, enrolled between May 2022 and May 2023: 445 were randomised to the intervention and 447 to an active control (comparator). Interventions 12 months of fully automated text messages with embedded behaviour change techniques and two-way messaging components to support weight loss and maintenance of weight loss in the postpartum period by targeting dietary, physical activity and weight management behaviours. The comparator group received 12 months of text messages on child health and development tailored to child age. Main outcome measures Primary outcome was weight in kilograms at 12 months (end of intervention). Secondary outcomes recorded at 6 and 12 months were changes in weight (at 6 months), body mass index, proportions of women with weight gain more than 5 kg, waist circumference, self-reported dietary intake, physical activity and infant feeding practices. Results 674 (75.6%) participants were included in the primary analysis. There was no difference found in the adjusted mean weight change between the intervention and active control groups (-0.1 kg (95% confidence interval -1.0 to 0.8, P= 0.84). Sensitivity analyses did not change these results. There was a small improvement in Fat and Fibre Barometer scores at 12 months in the intervention compared with control group (adjusted mean difference 0.09, 95% CI: 0.04 to 0.14; P<0.001) and an increase in physical activity scores (International Physical Activity Questionnaire Short Form) at 12 months in the intervention group compared with the control group (adjusted mean difference 405.3 total MET minutes/week, 95% CI: 141.3 to 669.3; P= 0.003). At 12 months, infants in the intervention group consumed more eggs (adjusted mean difference 0.47 portions/week, 95% CI: 0.14 to 0.81; P= 0.01), beans/lentils (adjusted mean difference 0.40 portions/week, 95% CI: 0.09 to 0.71; P= 0.01), and nuts (adjusted mean difference 0.35 portions/week, 95% CI: 0.06 to 0.64; P= 0.02) than those in the control group. Conclusions A 12 month automated, interactive behavioural weight management intervention delivered by text message did not support weight loss for postpartum women but did have a positive impact on diet, physical activity and infant feeding behaviours. Trial registration ISRCTN Registry ISRCTN16299220

items.title: Development of AWaRe quality indicators for optimal antibiotic use
items.abstract: Background: The WHO AWaRe (Access/Watch/Reserve) book gives detailed guidance on the optimal use of antibiotics across primary care and hospital settings aiming to improve the quality of antibiotic use. Objectives: To develop model sets of appropriate and feasible quality indicators (QIs) based on the WHO AWaRe system, that are widely implementable across primary care, hospital, and general healthcare system settings to support optimal antibiotic use. Methods: Indicators from a scoping review were revised to focus on clinical infections in the AWaRe book. They were assessed using two rounds each of the Global Delphi Technique and RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method evaluating appropriateness and feasibility at national and global levels respectively. In Round 1 of each method, panellists rated clarity and suggested revisions or new indicators. Round 2 results are reported. The indicators were then reviewed to create a priority list based on WHO book antibiotic choice recommendations, burden of disease, and positive measurement. Results: The AWaRe QIs covered common primary and hospital infections listed in the AWaRe book and general patient and population level indicators. There were 102 quality indicators (Primary Care: 46; Hospital: 39; General: 17) included in Round 2 of the Delphi Technique and 136 indicators (Primary Care: 56; Hospital: 60; General: 20) in Round 2 of the RAND/UCLA method.. The prioritisation process resulted in 20 core indicators (Primary Care: 10, Hospital: 8, General: 2). Conclusion: AWaRe quality indicators have been derived to support optimal antibiotic use, and inform stewardship programs.
