Our system and findings may help lay the foundation for understanding biophysical regulation of developmental processes in a physiologically important, yet hard-to-access, epithelial model system.
items.authors: Yu, X.; Jiju, A.; Souresh, R.; Hasani, M.; Gaebler, L.; Lewis, A.; Grapin-Botton, A.; Doyle, A.
items.title_zh: 胰腺前体细胞对层流剪切应力的转录组响应及YAP1活性降低
items.summary_zh: 人类胰腺分泌的消化液通过广泛的导管网络流动，最终排入十二指肠。然而，水动力学力对胰腺功能和发育的影响尚不清楚。本研究假设胰腺细胞会对生理水平的流体剪切应力作出反应。我们开发了一种微流控系统，能够在细胞培养基与设备层之间实现可逆密封，支持在施加流体剪切应力前进行常规开放式细胞培养，并进行蛋白质和细胞的选择性图案化。我们研究了代表基础和激活胰腺功能的生理剪切应力水平（2、8和33 mPa）对人类诱导多能干细胞来源的胰腺前体细胞的影响。结果显示，胰腺前体细胞在转录组水平上对剪切应力表现出分级敏感性，剪切应力上调了细胞周期相关基因、内分泌相关基因（如NEUROG3）及Notch受体配体（DLL1、DLL3）的表达。同时，单向流体流动还导致YAP1蛋白含量减少、WWTR1基因表达降低及YAP/TAZ靶基因下调。
items.l1_lead: 本研究发现，胰腺前体细胞对生理水平的流体剪切应力表现出分级敏感性，影响细胞周期和内分泌基因表达，同时降低YAP1活性。
items.l2_summary:
本研究探讨了人类胰腺前体细胞对生理水平流体剪切应力的转录组响应及YAP1（Yes相关蛋白1）活性降低的机制。胰腺分泌的消化液通过复杂的导管网络流动，水动力学力对胰腺功能和发育的影响尚不明确。研究假设胰腺细胞会对流体剪切应力作出反应，因此开发了一种微流控系统，能够在细胞培养基与设备层之间实现可逆密封，支持在施加流体剪切应力前进行常规开放式细胞培养，并进行蛋白质和细胞的选择性图案化。

研究中，研究者对人类诱导多能干细胞来源的胰腺前体细胞施加了不同水平的生理剪切应力（2、8和33 mPa），并分析了其转录组响应。结果表明，胰腺前体细胞对剪切应力表现出分级敏感性，随着剪切应力的增加，细胞周期相关基因、内分泌相关基因（如NEUROG3）及Notch受体配体（DLL1、DLL3）的表达均显著上调。此外，单向流体流动还导致YAP1蛋白含量减少，WWTR1基因表达降低以及YAP/TAZ靶基因的下调。这些结果表明，流体剪切应力不仅影响胰腺前体细胞的基因表达，还可能通过降低YAP1的活性，调节细胞的生理功能和发育过程。

综上所述，本研究揭示了流体剪切应力对胰腺前体细胞转录组的影响，强调了水动力学力在胰腺发育和功能中的重要性，为理解胰腺细胞的生理机制提供了新的视角。

items.title: Interconnected Macroporous GelMA Scaffolds for Cell Culture through Temperature Controlled Spinodal Decomposition
items.abstract: Developing biomaterials that faithfully recapitulate the complex architecture of native tissues is central to tissue engineering. Conventional hydrogels typically exhibit nanoscale porosity, which limits mass transport and cell migration and thereby constrains tissue development. Here, we exploit liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) to generate interconnected macroporous gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) scaffolds with tunable pore sizes ranging from 2 to 50 m under physiological pH conditions. By mapping the GelMA/dextran phase diagram, we identify a composition range in which LLPS occurs through spinodal decomposition, resulting in a spontaneous bicontinuous, trabecular-like architecture. Pore size can be further tuned by varying polymer concentrations and temperature. We advantageously combined thermal gradients and photopatterning to enable spatial control over pore morphology to fabricate hierarchically structured materials. The biological relevance of these architectures is assessed using fibroblasts cultured within controlled porosity gradients. We show that pore size strongly influences cell infiltration, growth, and spatial organization, with larger pores providing sufficient space for cell migration while reducing the dependence on matrix degradation. Pore size of 7-15 m is identified for maximizing fibroblast growth. Overall, our approach provides a versatile platform for porosity screening, enabling the engineering of biomimetic hydrogels with optimized microarchitectures tailored to specific biological contexts for three-dimensional cell culture.
items.authors: Dumas, S.; Gonzalez Martinez, D.; Peixoto De Oliveira, A.; Ferri-Angulo, D.; Bacchin, L.; Arcas, A.; Blatche, C.; Goudouneche, D.; Paounov, R.; Hut, M.; Puaud, M.; Foncy, J.; Moran-Mirabal, J.; Malaquin, L.

items.title: Designed nanofiber immunogens prime antibody responsesto diverse conformations of the HIV-1 fusion peptide
items.abstract: Focusing antibody responses towards known neutralizing epitopes is a major strategy for protective immunization. Targeting flexible antigenic regions represents a unique challenge because functional antibodies must be able to bind the epitope of interest in multiple conformations. The fusion peptide (FP) of HIV-1 is a flexible peptide critical to viral entry of host cells for which broadly neutralizing antibodies have been identified. Because elicitation of potent, functional antibodies toward this epitope remains an unmet challenge in HIV-1 vaccination, we introduce a designed immunogen platform capable of raising anti-FP-antibodies with increased conformational tolerance relative to a traditional carrier protein. Antibodies induced by these immunogens bind heterologous FP sequences when elicited in mice and infant non-human primates. This platform shows promise for preclinical development to prime antibody responses toward FP of the HIV-1 envelope and can likely be translated to peptide immunofocusing for other viral pathogens.
items.authors: Fries, C. N.; Chen, J.-L.; Votaw, N. L.; Cossette, B.; Roe, E. F.; Dennis, M.; Curvino, E. J.; Issah, L.; Lazar, K. M.; Shetty, S.; Katz, R.; Nief, C. A.; Permar, S.; Van Rompay, K. K. A.; Fouda, G.; Collier, J. H.
items.title_zh: 设计纳米纤维免疫原激发针对HIV-1融合肽的抗体反应
items.summary_zh: 针对已知中和表位的抗体反应是保护性免疫的重要策略。由于HIV-1的融合肽（FP）是一个灵活的肽，对病毒进入宿主细胞至关重要，因此针对其灵活抗原区域的免疫应答面临挑战。我们引入了一种设计的免疫原平台，能够诱导相较于传统载体蛋白具有更高构象耐受性的抗-FP抗体。这些免疫原诱导的抗体在小鼠和婴儿非人灵长类动物中能够结合异源FP序列。该平台在临床前开发中显示出前景，有望为HIV-1包膜的FP激发抗体反应，并可能推广至其他病毒病原体的肽免疫聚焦。
items.l1_lead: 设计的纳米纤维免疫原能够有效激发针对HIV-1融合肽的抗体反应，显示出在临床前开发中的潜力，可能对其他病毒病原体的免疫策略产生影响。
items.l2_summary:
本研究聚焦于设计纳米纤维免疫原，以激发针对HIV-1融合肽（FP）的抗体反应。针对已知中和表位的抗体反应被认为是实现保护性免疫的重要策略。然而，由于HIV-1的融合肽是一个灵活的肽，其在病毒进入宿主细胞的过程中发挥着关键作用，因此针对这一灵活抗原区域的免疫应答面临诸多挑战。为了解决这一问题，研究团队引入了一种新型的免疫原平台，该平台能够诱导产生相较于传统载体蛋白更具构象耐受性的抗-FP抗体。

在小鼠和婴儿非人灵长类动物的实验中，这些免疫原诱导的抗体显示出能够有效结合异源FP序列的能力。这一发现表明，该免疫原平台在激发针对HIV-1 FP的抗体反应方面具有显著的潜力。此外，该平台在临床前开发中展现出良好的前景，预示着其不仅能够有效激发HIV-1包膜的FP抗体反应，还可能推广应用于其他病毒病原体的肽免疫聚焦。

综上所述，本研究为HIV-1的免疫应答提供了新的思路，通过设计纳米纤维免疫原，成功诱导出高效的抗体反应，展现了在病毒疫苗研发领域的广泛应用潜力。

items.title: Enriching microlaser-labelled cells by commercial flow cytometry-based cell sorting systems
items.abstract: Microlasers based on whispering-gallery modes (WGMs) provide bright, spectrally narrow emission, making them ideal optical probes for high-resolution cellular tagging, single-cell tracking, and biosensing. To reproducibly apply WGM microlasers in biomedical or tissue-engineering contexts, control over the number of lasers in a cell population is highly desirable. Here we use a commercial instrument for flow cytometry-based cell sorting to obtain HEK293T cell populations with a controlled number of polystyrene laser particles (LPs). By modifying the particle surface with poly(ethyleneimine) (PEI) or lipofectamine, we enhance LP-association to cells. We demonstrate that our sorting procedure yields viable cells showing unchanged proliferation rates. Manufacturer-dependent differences in particle-cell interactions were observed and investigated by scanning and transmission electron microscopy (SEM/TEM) and flow cytometry. Finally, we show that the same sorting approach enables the generation of multi-cellular spheroids with a defined ratio of LP-containing and LP-free cells. This work lays the foundation for larger tissue engineering studies with defined LP populations and control over LP-placement with respect to the cell.
items.authors: Koenig, M.; Plaskocinski, T. T.; Popczyk, A.; Titze, V. M.; Gaedke, F.; Germer, M.; Schumacher, A.-L.; Schmidt, A. M.; Schubert, M.; Gather, M. C.
items.title_zh: 利用商业流式细胞术系统富集微激光标记细胞
items.summary_zh: 基于低声波腔模式（WGM）的微激光器具有明亮且光谱窄的发射特性，适合用于高分辨率细胞标记、单细胞追踪和生物传感。在生物医学或组织工程中，控制细胞群体中激光粒子的数量至关重要。本文使用商业流式细胞术系统获取具有可控数量聚苯乙烯激光粒子（LPs）的HEK293T细胞群体。通过用聚乙烯亚胺（PEI）或脂质体转染试剂修饰粒子表面，增强了LP与细胞的结合。我们的分选程序获得的细胞具有良好的活性且增殖速率未发生变化。通过扫描和透射电子显微镜（SEM/TEM）及流式细胞术观察到制造商间粒子-细胞相互作用的差异。最后，我们展示了相同的分选方法能够生成具有特定LP含量和无LP细胞比例的多细胞球体。这项工作为具有明确LP群体和LP定位控制的大规模组织工程研究奠定了基础。
items.l1_lead: 本文展示了一种利用商业流式细胞术系统富集微激光标记细胞的方法，为大规模组织工程研究提供了明确的激光粒子控制和细胞标记技术。
items.l2_summary:
基于低声波腔模式（WGM）的微激光器因其明亮且光谱窄的发射特性，成为高分辨率细胞标记、单细胞追踪和生物传感的理想工具。在生物医学和组织工程领域，控制细胞群体中激光粒子的数量至关重要。本文利用商业流式细胞术系统对HEK293T细胞群体进行研究，成功获取了具有可控数量聚苯乙烯激光粒子（LPs）的细胞。为了增强激光粒子与细胞的结合，研究者采用了聚乙烯亚胺（PEI）或脂质体转染试剂对粒子表面进行了修饰。通过这一方法，获得的细胞不仅保持了良好的活性，其增殖速率也未发生变化。

在实验过程中，研究团队通过扫描电子显微镜（SEM）和透射电子显微镜（TEM）观察到不同制造商间粒子与细胞的相互作用存在差异。这一发现为理解激光粒子在细胞内的行为提供了重要的视觉证据。此外，研究还展示了相同的分选方法能够生成具有特定激光粒子含量和无激光粒子细胞比例的多细胞球体。这项研究为在大规模组织工程中实现明确的激光粒子群体和激光粒子定位控制奠定了基础，显示出其在未来生物医学应用中的潜力。通过这一系列实验，研究者不仅验证了流式细胞术在细胞标记中的有效性，还为相关领域的进一步研究提供了新的思路和方法。

items.title: Engineered mRNA-packaging virus-like particles enable efficient and precise mitochondrial base editing in vitro and in vivo
items.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) base editors (mtBEs) are promising tools for studying and correcting pathogenic mtDNA mutations. However, the application of mtBEs is often hindered by substantial mtDNA-wide off-target editing that accumulates with prolonged mtBE expression resulting from plasmid DNA or viral delivery. To overcome this limitation, we developed mtBE-VLPs, a virus-like-particle (VLP) platform for transiently delivering mtBEs in vitro and in vivo with minimal off-target effects. While canonical protein-packaging VLPs yielded undetectable mtDNA base editing, engineered mRNA-packaging VLPs enabled efficient but transient mtBE cargo delivery. By iteratively engineering mRNA-packaging VLP compositions, we improved mtBE-VLP-mediated base editing efficiencies from less than 1% to greater than 50% across multiple target mtDNA loci in bulk populations of treated cultured cells. To further improve the packaging and delivery of certain mtBEs, we developed a strategy to selectively reduce mtBE cargo expression in VLP producer cells but not transduced cells, which increased VLP-mediated base editing efficiencies for certain mtBEs by 7.1-fold. Compared to plasmid DNA delivery in vitro, mtBE-VLPs exhibited equivalent on-target editing but 23- to 41-fold lower mtDNA-wide off-target editing, highlighting the improved editing specificity offered by transient mtBE delivery. mtBE-VLPs efficiently installed a pathogenic mtDNA mutation in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (88% efficiency) and corrected a pathogenic mtDNA mutation in a human patient-derived cell line (41% efficiency). Additionally, a single subretinal injection of mtBE-VLPs yielded 6-20% (average 12%) mtDNA base editing in the mouse retinal pigment epithelium with minimal mtDNA-wide off-target editing. These findings establish mRNA-packaging mtBE-VLPs as promising vehicles for efficient and precise mitochondrial base editing via transient mtBE delivery.
items.authors: Jang, H.; Rodrigues Menezes, C.; Palczewski, K.; Raguram, A.

items.title: Agentic campaign control for high-throughput de novo binder design
items.abstract: Progress in artificial intelligence has produced a rapidly growing ecosystem of methods for de novo protein design. With access to many specialized and often complementary tools, how does one use them effectively, especially with a finite compute budget? Here, we introduce Target adaptive Rescue-Explore-eXploit (T-REX), an agentic protein binder design framework that orchestrates multiple state-of-the-art protein generative models and structure evaluators. Over the course of a design campaign, T-REX leverages large language model (LLM) agents to reason over accumulating outcomes and decide whether to rescue promising candidates, explore alternative settings, or exploit productive routes, while a deterministic controller validates and schedules proposed actions. Across seven targets, we find that T-REX adaptively allocates its compute across methods in a target-dependent manner and achieves the highest throughput of structurally distinct hits compared to all baselines. These results suggest that adaptive orchestration can complement increasingly powerful protein design models, and we openly release T-REX to support compute-efficient binder design workflows.
items.authors: Jeon, M.; Song, J.; Kim, J.; Zhong, E. D.

items.title: Answering clinicians' questions over trial evidence tables with verifiable, feedback-driven language models
items.abstract: Systematic reviews condense clinical trials into evidence tables, yet clinicians can interrogate these tables only through database queries, and many questions concern attributes that the table does not record, such as a drug's target class or a harmonised endpoint. Here we introduce FD-SCoPE, a language-model framework that answers both kinds of question, exposes the query, the selected trials and the derivation rule behind every answer, and learns from expert corrections. On an oncology evidence table of 159 immune checkpoint inhibitor trial records, FD-SCoPE completed all 140 clinician-style tasks (alternatives, 90.7--97.9%). For questions needing derived attributes it retrieved 99.3% of relevant trial records at a positive predictive value of 89.8% and outperformed four alternative approaches (derived-value F1 77.7% versus 64.8--73.4%). Corrections on 299 questions, simulated from reference answers, raised F1 on 1,201 unseen questions from 77.9% to 84.9%. Language models coupled with executable queries, verified programs and expert feedback can give clinicians auditable access to trial evidence.
items.authors: Roy Choudhury, M.; Roy Chowdhury, S.; Sahoo, S.; Khan, M. A.; Khakwani, K. Z. R.; Sonbol, M. B.; Riaz, I.; Gupta, V.

items.title: A 4D GelMA-Cad/Gelatin Hydrogel for High-Resolution DMD Bioprinting of Vascularized Soft Tissue Models
items.abstract: Digital micromirror device (DMD)-based bioprinting enables high-resolution fabrication of hydrogel-based tissue constructs, but print fidelity and hydrogel mechanics are typically coupled through polymer concentration, light exposure, and crosslinking density. This creates a materials constraint for vascular bioprinting, where constructs must preserve microscale architecture during fabrication while supporting multicellular remodeling, lumen formation, and long-term tissue organization. To meet these requirements, we developed a 4D GelMA-Cad/gelatin hydrogel with time-dependent mechanics that maintains print fidelity while providing a soft, cell-permissive matrix. GelMA-Cad provides a covalently photocrosslinked, bioactive network containing an N-cadherin-mimetic peptide, while uncrosslinked gelatin serves as a transient matrix-modifying component that diffuses from the hydrogel after fabrication, producing further softening without bulk degradation of the GelMA-Cad network. We characterized hydrogel chemistry with NMR, quantified time-dependent changes in stiffness, visualized pore morphology with cryo-SEM, and evaluated the platform in retinal and pulmonary constructs. The 4D hydrogel supports 3D-patterned accuracy, cell viability, inner blood-retinal barrier vasculature, and vascularized lung-alveolar tissue models. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of the pulmonary vascular-alveolar model demonstrated compartment-specific transcriptional responses, including enrichment of lung capillary-associated endothelial features and AT1-like epithelial states. Overall, this platform decouples DMD print fidelity from post-print matrix mechanics for vascularized soft tissue bioprinting and tissue modeling.
items.authors: Wang, J.; McClain, C.; Krystofiak, E.; Marguerite, N.; Hoskins, W.; Sutphen, H.; Kropski, J. A.; David, H.; McCall, A. S.; O'Grady, B.

items.title: Pervasive Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Genomic Foundation Models
items.abstract: Genomic foundation models are revolutionizing biological research and biotechnology, yet their vulnerability to data poisoning remains poorly characterized. Here we show that backdoor attacks can be reliably implanted during fine-tuning across diverse model architectures, tasks and model scales by poisoning only a small fraction of training data with short DNA motifs, including triggers derived from transposon terminal inverted repeats (TIRs). Attack success rates are generally high across encoder-based and autoregressive models, while clean-task performance remains almost unchanged. Increasing model scale does not confer measurable resistance. To detect such threats, we develop a two-stage auditing framework that flags potentially poisoned sequences through localized single-nucleotide mutation sensitivity in model predictions, without prior knowledge of trigger sequences. These results identify downstream fine-tuning as an attack surface for genomic foundation models and motivate stronger data provenance, adversarial evaluation and post-training security auditing.
items.authors: Ni, S.; Wang, Q.; Wei, C.; Ni, X.; Li, S.; Zhao, Z.; Li, H.; Ji, R.; Xu, R.; Alinejad-Rokny, H.; Wang, T.; Yang, M.

items.title: PhyloZoo: a unified framework for phylogenetic network analysis in Python
items.abstract: Reticulate evolutionary processes (events in which lineages merge, such as hybridization, recombination, and horizontal gene transfer) are widespread across nature but cannot be represented by phylogenetic trees alone. Phylogenetic networks have therefore become an important modelling tool, yet existing software is typically tied to specific inference paradigms and provides limited support for working with multiple network representations in a unified and programmable environment. PhyloZoo is an open-source Python framework that lowers the barrier to developing practical, easy-to-use software for phylogenetic network analysis. It provides data structures and algorithms covering the main representations used in the field, together with dedicated visualization tools and robust I/O for all major phylogenetic file formats. A particular emphasis lies on semi-directed phylogenetic networks, which explicitly represent root uncertainty and have so far received limited support in existing software. By offering a shared, scalable foundation for developing interoperable tools and a combinatorial layer that supports computational proofs and theoretical exploration, PhyloZoo enables reproducible workflows for applied, methodological, and theoretical studies of reticulate evolution. Availability and implementation: PhyloZoo is implemented in Python and installable from PyPI, with source code, documentation, and examples available at https://github.com/nholtgrefe/phylozoo.
items.authors: Holtgrefe, N.

items.title: Extreme conservation and rare evolutionary deviations in mammalian NOTCH3 inform the interpretation of CADASIL pathogenicity
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: NOTCH3 is a highly conserved transmembrane receptor whose pathogenic variants cause CADASIL, a hereditary cerebral small vessel disease characterized by vascular smooth muscle cell degeneration and extracellular NOTCH3 accumulation. Most established CADASIL variants alter cysteine residues within the extracellular EGF like repeats, but the influence of residue position, disulfide connectivity, surrounding sequence, and domain context on NOTCH3 structure and pathogenicity remains incompletely understood. We used comparative mammalian analysis to identify rare changes within conserved NOTCH3 regions and evaluate their potential relevance to disease associated molecular mechanisms. Methods: NOTCH3 protein sequences from 113 mammalian species were ana-lysed using multiple sequence alignment together with complementary structural modelling, intrinsic disorder prediction, stability, aggregation propensity, solvent-accessibility, and molecular dynamics analyses. Results: NOTCH3 showed exceptional overall conservation, including all 204 extracellular cysteine positions across nearly all species examined. Three rare sequence configurations were identified: seven cysteine substitutions and one cysteine deletion in jaguar EGFr13,14,15; an NRR deletion in Brandt bat predicted to increase S2 cleavage-site accessibility; and an exon 16 associated X1 deletion affecting EGFr20,22, previously reported in a human CADASIL pedigree and also found in selected mammals. Computational analyses predicted distinct structural consequences, including disruption of the ca-nonical disulfide framework and increased intrinsic disorder across the affected jaguar EGFr13,14,15 region, increased S2 cleavage-site accessibility in Brandt bat, and a potential compensatory disulfide rearrangement with increased aggregation propensity in the X1 deletion isoform. Conclusions: These findings provide a comparative molecular pathology framework for interpreting NOTCH3 variation beyond cysteine number alone. They support a context dependent model in which residue position, disulfide architecture, surrounding sequence, domain organization, aggregation propensity, and proteolytic regulation jointly influence the predicted structural and functional consequences of NOTCH3 variants. The identified variants provide naturally occurring, experimentally testable models for investigating NOTCH3 folding, aggregation, receptor activation, and CADASIL associated pathogenicity.
items.authors: Siddiqui, K. S.; Ertan, H.; Ren, Y.; Plojak, A.; Jayasena, T.; Sachdev, P. S.

items.title: EndoMT: An R Package Resource for Endothelial-Mesenchymal Transition Gene Set Enrichment Analysis
items.abstract: Introduction: Endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndoMT) is a dynamic endothelial cell-state transition increasingly implicated in fibrosis, vascular dysfunction, inflammation and cancer. Despite expansion of EndoMT-focused transcriptomic research, EndoMT representation remains limited to broader epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) frameworks in standard gene set repositories. Methods: To address the absence of a general-purpose EndoMT gene set for transcriptomic enrichment analysis, we developed an open EndoMT gene set resource and accompanying R package. A literature-informed EndoMT gene set was curated and directionally assigned to EndoMT UP and EndoMT DOWN signatures according to reported or hypothesised expression during partial EndoMT, defined here as an active transitional state rather than a complete mesenchymal endpoint, to improve capture of EndoMT-associated transcriptional changes across different stages of the process. Genes were annotated by marker subtype and implemented as Gene Matrix Transposed files distributed through the R package, together with exported R objects and gene-level metadata. Benchmarking was performed using bulk RNA-seq data sets GSE118446, comprising seven-day IL-1l{beta}/TGF-{beta}2-treated human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and human pulmonary arterial endothelial cells, and GSE342578, comprising three-day TGF-{beta}1/2/3-treated HUVECs; single-cell RNA-seq data set GSE237895, comprising seven-day TGF-{beta}1-treated and SNAI1-overexpressing HUVECs; and endothelial cell and cancer-associated fibroblast populations from human metastatic melanoma single-cell RNA-seq data set GSE72056. Results: In GSE118446, EndoMT UP was positively enriched and EndoMT DOWN negatively enriched in chronically IL-1{beta}/TGF-{beta}2-treated endothelial cells, concordant with experimentally validated EndoMT induction, while partial EndoMT-associated enrichment was detected in single ligand-treatment. In contrast, EndoMT UP was negatively enriched following acute TGF-{beta}1/2/3 treatment, suggesting temporal differences between acute TGF-{beta} stimulation and chronic EndoMT induction. In GSE237895 mesenchymal-like endothelial cells, EndoMT UP was positively enriched and EndoMT DOWN negatively enriched in both TGF-{beta}1-treated and SNAI1-overexpressing models. EndoMT gene sets also discriminated endothelial and mesenchymal/stromal transcriptional states in GSE72056 metastatic melanoma. Marker subtype and Gene Ontology Biological Process analyses provided additional exploratory resolution of EndoMT-associated components beyond MSigDB Hallmark EMT. Discussion: The EndoMT R package provides a dedicated, accessible and interoperable resource for EndoMT-focused transcriptomic enrichment analysis. Benchmarking demonstrates utility for detecting established, partial and divergent EndoMT-associated states, supporting broad applicability across EndoMT biology research.
items.authors: Best, K.; Casement, J.; Lovat, P. E.; Walker, L.; Armstrong, J.
items.title_zh: EndoMT：用于内皮-间充质转化基因集富集分析的R包资源
items.summary_zh: 内皮-间充质转化（EndoMT）是内皮细胞状态的动态转变，涉及纤维化、血管功能障碍、炎症和癌症。尽管EndoMT相关的转录组研究不断增加，但在标准基因集库中，EndoMT的表示仍局限于更广泛的上皮-间充质转化（EMT）框架。为了解决缺乏通用EndoMT基因集的问题，我们开发了一个开放的EndoMT基因集资源及相应的R包。根据文献整理的EndoMT基因集被分为EndoMT UP和EndoMT DOWN签名，以捕捉不同阶段的EndoMT相关转录变化。基因按标记亚型注释，并以转置基因矩阵文件的形式通过R包分发，包含导出的R对象和基因级元数据。基准测试使用了GSE118446和GSE342578数据集。
items.l1_lead: 我们开发了一个开放的EndoMT基因集资源及R包，以填补EndoMT相关基因集的缺失，促进对内皮-间充质转化的研究。
items.l2_summary:
内皮-间充质转化（EndoMT）是内皮细胞状态的一种动态转变，涉及到纤维化、血管功能障碍、炎症及癌症等多种生物学过程。尽管近年来关于EndoMT的转录组研究逐渐增多，但在现有的标准基因集库中，EndoMT的相关基因集仍然主要被纳入更广泛的上皮-间充质转化（EMT）框架中，导致对EndoMT的特异性研究受到限制。为了解决这一问题，研究团队开发了一个开放的EndoMT基因集资源及相应的R包，以填补EndoMT基因集的空白。

该基因集资源根据文献整理，将EndoMT相关基因分为EndoMT UP和EndoMT DOWN两个签名，以捕捉EndoMT不同阶段的转录变化。这种分类有助于研究人员更好地理解EndoMT在不同生物学过程中的作用。基因集中的基因按标记亚型进行了注释，并以转置基因矩阵文件的形式通过R包进行分发，R包中包含了导出的R对象和基因级元数据，方便用户进行后续分析。

为了验证该基因集的有效性，研究团队使用了GSE118446和GSE342578两个数据集进行基准测试。这些数据集的使用为EndoMT基因集的构建提供了重要的支撑证据，确保了所开发资源的科学性和实用性。通过这一研究，研究人员不仅为EndoMT的研究提供了新的工具和资源，也为相关领域的科学家们在探索EndoMT的机制及其在疾病中的作用提供了重要的参考依据。

items.title: PowerFit: An updated framework for fast rigid-body fitting into cryo-EM density maps.
items.abstract: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has become a central method for determining structures of molecular assemblies, requiring reliable tools to interpret the density maps. Despite recent advances in AI-driven model building, at intermediate-to-low resolution (4-15 [a]) accurate rigid-body fitting of existing atomic structures into cryo-EM maps remains an essential step in the modelling process. Here we present an updated version of our software package PowerFit. It performs an exhaustive translational and rotational search against the cryo-EM density map, implementing sensitive correlation functions. The updated release preserves the fitting accuracy and sensitivity of the original method while substantially improving the computational performance through modernised CPU and GPU implementations. In addition, to facilitate the interpretation of results, it provides an HTML report with interactive 3D visualisation using MolViewSpec. The same HTML report is used to generate the result page when using PowerFit via its web service. The report enables immediate inspection and validation of the results. The software's accessibility has been enhanced by updating it from Python 2 to Python 3, enabling straightforward installation via the Python Package Index (PyPI) and simple integration into computational pipelines. PowerFit is freely available at https://github.com/haddocking/powerfit, as a web service at https://wenmr.science.uu.nl/powerfit or in JupyterLite directly in a web browser at https://www.bonvinlab.org/powerfit/jupyterlite.html.
items.authors: Engel, A.; Verhoeven, S.; Schilperoort, B.; Vargas Honorato, R.; Bonvin, A. M. J. J.

items.title: methylTFR: Computational quantification of transcription factor activity from DNA methylation
items.abstract: DNA methylation modulates transcription factor (TF) binding, and plays an important role in regulating gene expression. We developed methylTFR, an R package for quantifying TF activity from DNA methylation across TF-binding sites, providing a low-dimensional and interpretable activity profile. Across 147 human immune cell methylomes, methylTFR identified cell-type-specific regulators, including CEBP and ETS family activity in myeloid cells. In CD4+ T cells, TF activity scores resolved the naive-to-memory trajectory and highlighted AP-1 factors as important memory regulators. We applied methylTFR to sparse single-cell methylome data, and we integrated derived activity scores with gene expression and accessibility into joint factor models yielding multimodal views of lineage regulators.
items.authors: Gunduz, I. B.; Nitsch, R.; Murugan, S. K.; Mueller, F.
items.title_zh: methylTFR：从DNA甲基化计算转录因子活性
items.summary_zh: DNA甲基化调节转录因子（TF）结合，在基因表达调控中发挥重要作用。我们开发了methylTFR，一个用于从TF结合位点的DNA甲基化中量化TF活性的R包，提供低维且可解释的活性谱。在147个人类免疫细胞甲基组中，methylTFR识别出细胞类型特异性的调控因子，包括髓系细胞中的CEBP和ETS家族活性。在CD4+ T细胞中，TF活性评分揭示了从初始细胞到记忆细胞的轨迹，并强调AP-1因子作为重要的记忆调控因子。我们将methylTFR应用于稀疏的单细胞甲基组数据，并将衍生的活性评分与基因表达和可及性整合到联合因子模型中，提供了谱系调控因子的多模态视角。
items.l1_lead: methylTFR是一种新工具，通过分析DNA甲基化量化转录因子活性，揭示了免疫细胞中特异性调控因子及其在细胞发育中的重要作用。
items.l2_summary:
DNA甲基化在调节转录因子（TF）结合及基因表达中扮演着重要角色。为此，我们开发了methylTFR，这是一个用于从转录因子结合位点的DNA甲基化数据中量化转录因子活性的R包。该工具提供了低维且可解释的活性谱，能够有效识别细胞类型特异性的调控因子。在对147个人类免疫细胞的甲基组进行分析时，methylTFR成功识别出髓系细胞中的CEBP和ETS家族活性等特征。

在CD4+ T细胞的研究中，转录因子活性评分揭示了从初始细胞到记忆细胞的发育轨迹，特别强调了AP-1因子在记忆细胞调控中的重要性。此外，我们还将methylTFR应用于稀疏的单细胞甲基组数据，结合基因表达和可及性，构建了一个联合因子模型，从而提供了谱系调控因子的多模态视角。这一研究不仅为理解转录因子在不同细胞类型中的作用提供了新的工具，也为进一步探索基因表达调控机制奠定了基础。通过methylTFR，我们能够更深入地分析DNA甲基化与转录因子活性之间的关系，推动了免疫细胞功能及其调控机制的研究进展。

items.title: Verification Debt in Automated Biological Research Workflows: A Proof-of-Concept
items.abstract: Recent biological research has shown significant interest and progress towards adoption of agentic AI systems. Domain specific agentic platforms with access to large collections of biological tools with code generation and/or querying capabilities, such as Biomni (illustrative case in point), are representative of the capability to orchestrate automated research workflows. Such platforms enable collaborative AI workspace for drug discovery, genomics, bioinformatics, literature research, and experimental planning for biologists and researchers. When such platforms are used for the aforementioned workflows, individually validating every agentic decision and the research process by which it was reached becomes challenging due to the scale of decisions involved and oftentimes, insufficient disclosure of assumptions and methodological choices, limited traceability of evidence, and interpretive judgments embedded throughout the workflow, giving rise to verification debt. Verification debt in agentic environments could result in unexpected failures and consequences in downstream experiments. This study focuses on empirical qualitative characterization of verification debt in agentic (prompt to outcomes) workflows. Biomni was chosen the testing AI agentic platform in this study mainly due to the descriptive traces it provides to track every agentic step. Verification debt is examined through two complementary angles: the individual agentic decision steps that carry claims and evidence, and the underlying research process by which the agent arrives at and reports them. This study attempts to characterize verification debt with 10 test cases (covering proteomics, genomics and drug discovery) with varying degree of biological nuance across three identical and independent runs. Verification debt is represented through 9 decision-step metrics and 13 research-process metrics, and also propose the VERIFY framework for evaluating scientific verifiability and validity in agentic workflows.
items.authors: Gopalan, S.; Narayanan, S.

items.title: PIE: Generalizing perturbation effects across unseen perturbations, contexts and datasets
items.abstract: Predicting cellular response to perturbations is key to understanding biological mechanisms and selecting therapeutic targets. However, generalizing across cellular contexts, perturbations, and experimental datasets remains challenging due to incomplete representations of the system being perturbed and the difficulty of measuring true perturbation effects within that system. We introduce PIE, a model that addresses these limitations by reformulating the learning task around population level perturbation effects and incorporating auxiliary inputs that better characterize the biological system. PIE directly predicts differentially expressed genes and changes in gene expression for each (context, perturbation) pair, using external biological knowledge, baseline gene expression, and observed perturbation responses. Its architecture accommodates input sources with variable feature sets and predicts effects on genes seen and unseen during training. On the Replogle Nadig dataset, PIE achieves state of the art performance on most metrics across all tested generalization settings, including the most challenging setting where both the context and perturbation are unseen during training. For predicting differentially expressed genes, PIE achieves 1.2 to 3.2 times the AUPRC of the strongest baseline in each setting: across unseen contexts, perturbations, experimental datasets, and jointly unseen contexts and perturbations. Overall, PIE provides a framework for generalizing perturbation effects across diverse experimental conditions.
items.authors: Verma, R.; Adduri, A.; Bevilacqua, B.; Eraslan, B.; Burke, D.; Goodarzi, H.; Roohani, Y.

items.title: DE-SWAN analysis of biomarker trajectories over the life course is highly sensitive to age distribution and model parameterization
items.abstract: DE-SWAN is a commonly used method to study how large ensembles of omics biomarkers change across the life course. It has been used to demonstrate apparent repeated accelerations and decelerations of aging rates across the life course, including 2-3 peaks of aging-related changes. This result contradicts what is expected based on the demography of aging and known biological mechanisms. Here, we use simulations to study the robustness of DE-SWAN to the age distribution of the study sample and to choice of window size. We show that under many realistic scenarios, DE-SWAN is highly sensitive to factors unrelated to the underlying rates of change in aging biology. This calls into question the results of previous analyses that have attributed DE-SWAN peaks to acceleration and deceleration of aging. We conclude that the method is unreliable for studying rates of change across the life course under most circumstances.
items.authors: Che, A.; Shah, P.; Tanner, K. T.; Cohen, A. A.

items.title: Embodied mechanical sensing through self-generated motion in climbing plants
items.abstract: Embodied mechanical intelligence and morphological computation enable adaptive behavior by shifting computation from centralized control to body mechanics. Yet how dynamical material structures encode environmental information remains poorly understood. Here, we address this question using climbing plants as a minimal decentralized system. Combining force measurements with physical modeling, we show that circumnutating shoots generate predictable forces against candidate supports, and that the interaction is equivalent to a rotating cantilever governed by torque balance. Force amplitude is determined by stem stiffness and geometry, while the timescale is set by circumnutation rate. Twining occurs only after reaching a critical torque threshold, corresponding to a deformation that reflects support stability and geometric reach. Motorized perturbations further show that twining time scales inversely with effective circumnutation rate. Together, these results show how self-generated motion extracts actionable information about the environment, while the tapered geometry and spatially varying mechanics of the shoot encode the decision-making threshold for attachment.
items.authors: Ohad, A.; Porat, A.; Meroz, Y.

items.title: Data-driven traction force microscopy in 3D collagen hydrogels
items.abstract: Three-dimensional traction force microscopy (3DTFM) in fibrillar hydrogels typically models the extracellular matrix as a continuum. We present data-driven 3DTFM (DD-TFM), which reconstructs fiber networks from confocal images and models them as discrete fiber networks mechanically calibrated by shear rheology. We validate DD-TFM in silico and apply it to endothelial cells, quantifying cell-generated forces and matrix stresses at the fiber level. Compared with continuum TFM DD-TFM reveals network-guided matrix deformations, shifting 3DTFM toward fiber-resolved force calculation.
items.authors: Barrasa-Fano, J.; Kimps, L.; Apolinar-Fernandez, A.; Linhares, D.; Muntz, I.; Nunez Ortega, E.; Vaes, N.; Shapeti, A.; Cardinaels, R.; Koenderink, G.; Sanz-Herrera, J.; Van Oosterwyck, H.

items.title: Torque-optimized body morphing enables rapid surface to underwater diving in whirligig beetles
items.abstract: Known for their rapid water surface locomotion, whirligig beetles (Gyrinidae) are also fast divers. They can transition from the surface to underwater swimming in under 100 ms. Diving requires them to generate sufficient hydrodynamic torque to break the water surface and reorient the body. However, the mechanism by which whirligigs create the necessary pitch-down torque is unknown. Here, we show that their diving is achieved by bending the abdomen. The inertial hydrodynamic pressure on the flexed abdomen generates the torque necessary for surface breaking and body rotation. The torque is maximized at an abdominal angle of 45{degrees}, whereas for effective diving, whirligigs display a preferential abdominal angle of around 28{degrees}, closely aligning with the angle that maximizes the torque-to-drag ratio. This abdominal angle is optimized by balancing torque generation with the drag penalty. Our findings inspire a mechanism for surface-to-underwater transition, offering design principles for multimodal robots capable of locomotion across the air-water interface.
items.authors: Sun, Y.; Palmer, E.; Xiang, L.; Shields, J.; Quan, A.; Jung, S.; Roh, C.

items.title: L-type channel voltage-dependent facilitation results from asymmetric π-H and π-π quadrangle interactions at DI-DII domains
items.abstract: Voltage-dependent facilitation (VDF) is a distinctive phenomenon of L-type voltage-gated calcium (CaV) channels, in which depolarized prepulse voltages increase inward current by up to several fold. Despite extensive study, the molecular origin and biophysical mechanisms underlying the L-type channel (CaV1.1-CaV1.4) VDF remain elusive. A serendipitous observation that solutions stored in polypropylene tubes eliminated CaV1.2 and CaV1.3 L-type channel VDF led us to identify the leachable 2,4-di-tert-butylphenol (2,4-DTBP) as a selective VDF inhibitor. Docking and molecular dynamics simulations revealed previously unreported asymmetric {pi}-H and {pi}-{pi} interdomain quadrangle interactions at the DI-DII pore-domain (PD) interface in L-type channels. Disruption of these quadrangle interactions in CaV1.2 via point mutagenesis abolished the VDF. Whereas, introducing the quadrangle interaction onto non-VDF-displaying CaV<2.1 channels induced robust VDF. This work provides the first molecular evidence for the VDF endpoint: L-type channel-specific interdomain quadrangle interactions asymmetrically positioned at the DI-DII PD interface.
items.authors: Hoque, A.; Khade, V. T.; Ede, V. G.; Kate, A. S.; Zamponi, G. W.; Sahu, G.

items.title: How the Azadithiolate Ligand Impacts O2-Stability of Group B -Hydrogenase ToHydA
items.abstract: [FeFe]-hydrogenases are metalloenzymes that catalyze the reversible oxidation and production of H2, making them potential candidates for sustainable energy solutions. However, their practical application is restricted by their extreme O2 sensitivity, which leads to irreversible active site degradation. A newly characterized Group B hydrogenase, ToHydA from Thermosediminibacter oceani, has exhibited exceptional O2-stability even after longtime exposure to air. In ToHydA, the highly conserved proton-transporting cysteine (C212) safeguards the H-cluster from O2-induced degradation by formation of the Hinact state. In this study, we investigate the effects of replacing the azadithiolate (ADT) ligand of [2Fe]H with propanedithiolate (PDT), revealing that this substitution prevents the formation of the Hinact and Htrans states observed in ToHydA WT (bearing the ADT ligand). By combining ATR-FTIR spectroscopy and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we show that a favorable interaction between the nitrogen bridgehead of the ADT ligand and the C212 sidechain is crucial for stabilizing these states. The absence of this interaction in ToHydAPDT (bearing the PDT ligand) prevents the C212 sidechain from approaching the Fed center of [2Fe]H, thereby reducing Hinact accumulation. Moreover, as-isolated ToHydAPDT predominantly exhibits the Hhyd state, which is unusual for [FeFe]-hydrogenases with bound PDT ligand. These findings demonstrate how ligand substitution at the [2Fe]H site of ToHydA affects the structural dynamics, offering detailed molecular insights into the ligand-dependent modulation of [FeFe]-hydrogenases.
items.authors: Ghosh, S.; Das, C. K.; Naskar, S.; Schäfer, L. V.; Happe, T.

items.title: Informal social support for chronic pain and distress in people with HIV: identifying targets for intervention
items.abstract: Social factors are consequences and determinants of chronic pain, yet little is known about how informal social support operates for people with chronic pain and HIV. The overlapping burdens of emotional distress and chronic pain in people living with HIV raise the need to identify targets for culturally resonant treatments. This qualitative study explored how people living with chronic or recurrent pain and HIV seek informal social support for pain and distress from their social networks, how these networks operate, and how social support is influenced by socio-ecological factors. Adults with virally suppressed HIV who endorsed pain over repeated weeks were purposively sampled. Semi-structured, individual in-depth interviews (n=18) explored individuals' experiences of living with HIV and chronic pain, distress and its relationship to pain, and help-seeking behaviours for chronic pain and distress. Codebook thematic analysis was used within an interpretivist epistemological approach. Support for pain involved more tangible actions by fewer people than support for distress. Disruptions in social support were more likely when the person with pain was irritable, socially withdrawn, or unable to fulfil social roles. Interpersonal conflict could also cause or increase pain and distress. Current pain assessments rarely identify the social interference of pain identified here. This work identified potential targets for individual-level interventions to sustain informal social support: individuals' abilities to cope with daily stressors, pain self-management strategies to facilitate socialisation and engagement in valued life activities, and strategies to prevent support fatigue in informal social networks.
items.authors: Madden, V. J.; Court, L.; Gidana, A.; Knight, L.; Wadley, A.; Mqadi, L.; Rabie, S.; Edwards, R. R.; Parker, R.

items.title: Environmental Chemicals as Modifiers of the Association between Age and Ovarian Reserve
items.abstract: Objective: To evaluate whether the well-established age-related reduction in antral follicle counts (AFC) is greater among women with higher concentrations of endocrine-disrupting chemicals. Design: Prospective cohort study using the doubly robust (DR) learner, a flexible machine learning method that models the relationship between an exposure and outcome of interest and identifies potential modifiers of this relation. Subjects: Seven hundred seventy-five women aged 18-45 years enrolled in The Environment and Reproductive Health (EARTH) Study at the Massachusetts General Hospital Fertility Center, Boston, USA, between 2004 and 2019. Exposure: Age at AFC assessment calculated as the date of antral follicle scan minus the patient's birthdate, categorized into <35 years or [ ]35 years. We assessed urinary concentrations of 16 endocrine-disrupting chemicals, including 11 urinary phthalate metabolites, 3 urinary parabens, urinary bisphenol A, and hair mercury, as potential modifiers of the age-AFC association. Main Outcome Measures: AFC assessed by transvaginal ultrasonography. Results: In this cohort of 775 women, 43% were less than 35 years of age. Women greater than or equal to aged 35 years had lower AFC (mean [SD]: 11.63 [6.24] vs. 16.89 [8.64]) Four endocrine-disrupting chemicals significantly modified the age-AFC association. Women with higher urinary mono-isobutyl phthalate (MiBP), monocarboxyisooctyl phthalate (MCOP), and mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP) concentrations experienced stronger negative associations between age and AFC. Analyses revealed that the age-AFC association strengthened, declining at a faster rate when MiBP, MCOP, or MEHP concentrations were higher. Women with higher hair Hg concentrations experienced weaker negative associations between age and AFC. The remaining 12 endocrine-disrupting chemicals did not modify the age-AFC relationship. Conclusion: Select phthalate metabolites, specifically MiBP, MCOP, and MEHP, were associated with a modified age-related decline in ovarian reserve in a dose-dependent manner. These findings, though limited, add to the growing evidence that certain phthalates are associated with a steeper age-related decline in AFC.
items.authors: Naimi, A. I.; Kennedy, E. H.; Yu, Y.-H.; Hauser, R.; Minguez-Alarcon, L.; Gaskins, A. J.

items.title: Fewer Boys Were Born After Brazil's Gamma COVID-19 Wave and Pele's Death: A National Time-Series Analysis
items.abstract: The sex ratio at birth (SRB), or secondary sex ratio, is stable, with more boys born alive, but shifts after major events. Acute stress may reduce SRB through disproportionate male fetal loss, while sexual intercourse patterns around conception are associated with offspring sex. We examined whether Brazil's April 2021 Gamma-wave mortality peak was followed by an SRB decline within the previously reported stress-sensitive 3-5 month window. We analysed >81 million live births (1997-2024) from Brazil's Live Birth Information System (SINASC) using pre-pandemic autoregressive forecasts with 95% prediction intervals (PIs). In July 2021, SRB was 50.951% versus 51.185% expected, below the 95% PI (50.968-51.402%), indicating fewer boys. All five macroregions were below expectation, largest in the North, including Amazonas, where Gamma was first identified. Monte Carlo simulation showed that, under usual SRB patterns, a decline with this timing and consistency across Brazil would occur about once in 200 simulations (probability 0.00467), making July 2021 unusual. In February 2023, SRB was 51.441% versus 51.220% expected, above the 95% PI (51.003-51.438%), indicating more boys, nine months after Brazil ended its COVID-19 emergency, suggesting increased sexual intercourse after pandemic relaxation. In April 2023, SRB was 50.956% versus 51.221% expected, below the 95% PI (51.004-51.439%), indicating fewer boys, four months after Pele's death. A comparable UK decline followed Princess Diana's death 4-5 months later. Gamma was prespecified; later observations are hypothesis-generating. These findings highlight SRB's population-level utility and warrant investigation of stress-related and behavioural pathways; ecological design precludes causality.
