Furthermore, two-dimensional gate-field maps show that the crossing time evolves systematically with electrostatic tuning, demonstrating that the hidden valley dynamics are electrically controllable. These results show that time-integrated circular polarization can give a false-negative indication of valley polarization in multichannel valley emitters.
items.authors: Yuto Urano, Lata Chouhan, Nurul Fariha Ahmad, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Daichi Kozawa, Ryo Kitaura

items.title: Learning Lattice Parameters from Powder X-Ray Diffraction Data Using Invariants
items.abstract: We present a machine learning (ML) method to determine unit cell parameters from powder X-Ray diffraction (XRD) data using a novel invariant lattice representation. In ML, the data representation used can have a substantial impact on the prediction quality. Previous approaches have directly predicted lattice parameters ($a,b,c,\alpha,\beta,\gamma$) from XRD inputs. However, these parameters depend strongly on the unit cell reduction or convention used. In this work, we construct an invariant representation of the reciprocal lattice that is independent of primitive cell convention, based on the bispectrum--a descriptor built from spherical harmonic projections of lattice points. The calculation of the lattice bispectrum is differentiable, and we demonstrate how to invert it using gradient-based optimization initialized from a nearest-neighbor lookup. We show that with a fixed ML model architecture, using the lattice bispectrum as the ML target rather than the unit cell parameters leads to more accurate lattice parameter predictions. For example, using the MP-20 dataset, the bispectrum reduces length mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 11.08% to 2.43% and angle MAPE from 12.15% to 2.45% compared to direct prediction with the same model architecture. We additionally benchmark our approach against pre-existing XRD to crystal structure models such as Crystalyze and assess its performance on experimental data. Beyond unit cell representation, we anticipate this invariant lattice representation could serve more broadly as a geometry-aware target for other crystallographic machine learning tasks such as structure generation.
items.authors: Elyssa Hofgard, Kyucheol Min, Nofit Segal, David W. Mittan-Moreau, Aria Mansouri Tehrani, Vanessa Oklejas, Rafael G\'omez-Bombarelli, Jigyasa Nigam, Daniel W. Paley, Aaron S. Brewster, Tess Smidt

items.title: Quenched fluctuation-induced force arising from polarization disorder
items.abstract: We investigate the zero-temperature behavior of the fluctuation force induced by the quenched disorder of electric dipoles frozen randomly into a material. Examples of such materials include relaxor ferroelectrics. In terms of the setup and geometry, we focus on a layered system comprising two coplanar semi-infinite slabs separated by a distance $\ell$ as well as a system comprising a neutral atom in the vacuum located at a distance $\ell$ above the surface of a semi-infinite slab. For both systems, we consider the cases where the quenched random dipolar disorder occurs inside the bulk as well as on the surface of the slabs. In all of these cases, we find that the bulk (surface) dipolar disorder-induced force grows with the mean square quenched electric dipole moment per unit volume (area). The bulk (surface) dipolar disorder-induced pressure between two semi-infinite single-layered slabs decays with $\ell^{-3}$ ($\ell^{-4}$), whereas the bulk (surface) dipolar disorder-induced force on an atom in the vacuum near a slab containing the disorder decays with $\ell^{-4}$ ($\ell^{-5}$). We also find that the quenched dipolar disorder-induced force between two coplanar slabs can be repulsive in a three-layered dielectric system that obeys a zero-frequency analogue of the Dzyaloshinskii-Lifshitz-Pitaevskii condition, and serve to enhance the ``nanolevitation effect" if the latter is present in the disorder-free system.
items.authors: Bing-Sui Lu

items.title: Causality violations in cluster GW+DMFT: Exact Lehmann moments and the necessity of non-local vertex corrections
items.abstract: The $GW$ approximation is known to violate causality, yielding self-energies with unphysical poles in the upper half of the complex frequency plane. The combined $GW$+DMFT approach attempts to cure this by injecting the exact local self-energy. Using exact diagonalization on minimal Hubbard clusters, we rigorously benchmark the analytic structure of the $GW$ and $GW$+DMFT self-energies. We demonstrate a ``dimer anomaly'': on the two-site dimer, inversion symmetry forces the non-local self-energy to be purely real, masking the causality violation. Moving to the non-bipartite three-site Hubbard ring, where hopping frustration yields a finite imaginary part in the non-local self-energy, we prove that both $GW$ and $GW$+DMFT violate the Matsubara causality condition. By analytically evaluating the exact Lehmann moments, we derive a closed-form expression for the high-frequency tail of the self-energy, $C = U^2\,\mathrm{Var}(d)\,I$, and show that standard methods fail to capture the exact equal-time two-particle correlators required to enforce it. The equal-time correlators that govern this tail are precisely those encoded in the high-frequency asymptotics of the fully irreducible vertex $\Lambda$; nevertheless, our intermediate-frequency analysis demonstrates that the local-only truncation of $\Lambda$ in $GW$+DMFT leaves non-local RPA resonances uncorrected. The two diagnostics are logically independent: $GW$+DMFT satisfies the necessary high-frequency condition $C\succeq0$ yet still violates the Matsubara sign condition at finite frequencies. Taking the interpolation-free real-axis evaluation of the exact self-energy as the primary causality certificate, with rational continuation as supporting evidence, we establish a rigorous benchmark demonstrating that local self-energy corrections are insufficient to guarantee a causal analytic structure on frustrated clusters.
items.authors: Michael O. Atambo

items.title: Complete Magnetic Hierarchy in Bichromatically Driven Unconventional Magnets
items.abstract: We establish a general framework for engineering unconventional magnetism using bichromatic driving. We identify a sharp hierarchy: for a bichromatic drive with a generic even commensurate frequency ratio, the leading continuum $q$-wave magnet generates components only up to order $q-2$, whereas lattice higher-gradient terms supply the missing $q-1$ and $q$ parities and complete the hierarchy through order $q$. We explicitly illustrate this new revised hierarchy on a $d$-wave altermagnet irradiated by a circularly-linearly polarized light, and show that the asymmetry of the driving field is transferred to the light-dressed electronic structure, producing momentum-asymmetric dispersions beyond the static and single-frequency limits. We further show that this band asymmetry is absent in the leading continuum expansion and originates from higher-gradient lattice terms that are converted by the bichromatic drive into odd-in-momentum contributions. Extending the analysis to higher-order unconventional magnets, we further obtain complete magnetic hierarchies for all $q$-parity unconventional magnets. Our results establish bichromatic Floquet driving as a general route for generating mixed-parity magnetic hierarchies and dynamically engineering unconventional magnetism.
items.authors: Pei-Hao Fu, Sayed Ali Akbar Ghorashi

items.title: MLS and CALIPSO Evidence for a Warm-Pool Transition in Tropical Convective Moistening and Cloud Ice
items.abstract: Upper-tropospheric water vapor and cloud ice associated with tropical deep convection are central to water-vapor and high-cloud feedbacks. We investigate a warm-pool transition in tropical convective moistening using 20 years of Aura Microwave Limb Sounder (MLS) Version 5 H2O and cloud-ice observations (August 2004-December 2024), together with Cloud-Aerosol Lidar with Orthogonal Polarization (CALIOP) aboard the Cloud-Aerosol Lidar and Infrared Pathfinder Satellite Observations (CALIPSO) mission (June 2006-June 2023). The combined day-plus-night CALIPSO product (CALIPSO-A) provides an independent ice-cloud constraint; the H2O column shown on the CALIPSO grid is derived from Modern-Era Retrospective Analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2), not from CALIOP. We combine objective sea surface temperature (SST) breakpoint fitting, cross-sensor ice water path (IWP) comparisons, Clouds and the Earth's Radiant Energy System (CERES) longwave, shortwave, and net cloud radiative effect (CRE), and Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM (IMERG) precipitation diagnostics from the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission. MLS and CALIPSO-A show cloud-ice maxima over deep-convective warm-pool regions and identify warm-regime SST breakpoints near 299-300 K. Normalized MLS and CALIPSO-A IWP vary coherently in the western Pacific and tropical mean. CERES indicates that stronger longwave CRE in the warm regime is partly offset by stronger shortwave cooling, while GPM IMERG confirms that MLS IWP increases with convective rain rate. These results show that convective moistening and cloud-ice production across the tropical warm-pool transition are persistent cross-sensor features of the tropical atmosphere.
items.authors: Isabel Nucera, Jonathan H. Jiang, Yiyang Zhang, King-Fai Li, Bin Zhao, Hwayon Choi, Yong-Sang Choi

items.title: Black-Scholes for the land: modelling savannah response to rain as a dynamic world model
items.abstract: Carbon credits, offsets and index insurance rest on counterfactuals: what the land would have done under the same weather without management, or what a bad season cost. Current baselines fail in two ways: some ignore rain, others condition on rain linearly and annually. But the true response lags the rain, depends on hidden state such as moisture from other sources, and responds differently from pixel to pixel. Focussing on grassland pasture as a proof of concept, we fit a temporal world model of MODIS greenness conditioned on CHIRPS rain over two 45 km^2 sites in Laikipia, Kenya: a transition density map for greenness given recent and current rainfall. We use it, conceptually, as Black-Scholes is used. Inverting the model on observed greenness it yields an implied residual, everything the land did that the rain does not explain. Two capabilities drop out of this solution: 1) attribution, what the land did beyond the rain; 2) sensitivities, derivatives of the rollout with respect to rain and state, close analogues of the Greeks. On Laikipia test sites, our learned model recovers three-month greenness with 23% less error than a history-only baseline and 13% less than the best hand-written model on unseen years. In the 2022 drought, the land ended 0.17 NDVI below normal; the rain that failed explains roughly half of that, and under normal rain with the same residual it would still have ended 0.10 below. Delta, the derivative of greenness with respect to rain, is computed at every pixel and averages 0.075 NDVI per extra 100 mm of rain. A Delta at every pixel is an exposure to rain that can be hedged, allowing efficient pricing of contracts and accurate attribution.
items.authors: Thomas Pitts

items.title: A Multivariable Approach to the Regional Calibration of the Galvez Davison Index across Mexico Climate Regimes
items.abstract: The G\'alvez Davison Index (GDI) is a thermodynamic diagnostic designed to summarize convective favorability in the tropical regions, yet its transferability across complex terrain and heterogeneous hydroclimates remains uncertain. Here we assess the climatological behavior and precipitation relevance of the GDI over Mexico using ERA5 hourly fields and CHIRPS daily precipitation for 1981 to 2024. We characterize the seasonal cycle and spatial contrasts of GDI and evaluate its association with rainfall using grid point and regional Pearson and Spearman correlations between daily maximum GDI and daily precipitation. To introduce an independent convective proxy, we also quantify the relationship between hourly GDI and ERA5 outgoing longwave radiation (OLR). Event level discrimination skill is assessed with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the curve (AUC) across regions and months. While GDI precipitation correlations are moderate and region dependent, GDI OLR coupling is consistently stronger, partly because OLR approaches a lower bound once deep convection develops, supporting its use as an intermediate proxy between thermodynamic favorability and rainfall. However, GDI values are systematically lower over elevated terrain because of the pressure level formulation of the index, which should be considered when interpreting the GDI over mountainous regions. ROC results indicate skill above random chance in nearly all region month combinations, with AUC frequently exceeding 0.75 during the core convective season. Building on these diagnostics, we propose a regionally calibrated GDI convective regime scale for May to October, adapted from the original GDI framework but recalibrated for Mexico using event conditioned distributions defined from OLR and precipitation and quantified with bootstrap uncertainty.
items.authors: Mauricio L\'opez-Reyes, Carlos Calvo-Sancho, Angel Meulenert, Jos\'e Francisco Le\'on-Cruz, Jose Manuel G\'alvez, Javier D\'iaz Fernandez, Juan Jes\'us Gonz\'alez-Alem\'an, Mar\'ia Luisa Mart\'in P\'erez

items.title: A Net Flux-Weighted Analytical Generalization of the Greenhouse Effect Beyond the Gray Approximation
items.abstract: Analytical greenhouse models traditionally rely on the gray approximation, simplifying radiative transfer but treating optical depth as an unconstrained parameter that yields unrealistic surface temperatures. We derive an exact, closed-form solution directly from Schwarzschild's equations for a non-gray atmosphere. While the gray approach is physically inadequate because it over-weights saturated bands that carry negligible net energy transport, we show that the non-gray formulation constrains column optical depth via the surface net radiative flux, naturally accounting for the atmospheric window without ad hoc corrections. The resulting effective optical depth penalizes saturated cores due to the negative spectral covariance between opacity and transmission. This shifts the computed surface equilibrium to an observationally consistent 288 K, yielding a purely radiative Transient Climate Response of +2.18 K under doubled \ce{CO2}, fully consistent with Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change estimates. The framework eliminates any theoretical basis for greenhouse-effect saturation. While not intended to replace three-dimensional general circulation models, this work reconciles classical radiative transfer with modern climate estimates, demonstrating that proper flux-weighting aligns analytical theory with anthropogenic warming.
items.authors: Carmine Serio

items.title: Entropy-Stable and Well-Balanced Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for the Compressible Euler Equations in Vector-Invariant Form
items.abstract: We develop structure-preserving methods for the compressible Euler equations with gravity in vector-invariant form and potential temperature as a prognostic variable within the flux-differencing discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DGSEM) framework. By discretizing the nonconservative terms as symmetric and antisymmetric products, we derive two-point numerical fluxes that conserve both the thermodynamic entropy and the total energy. Moreover, we design an entropy-stable numerical flux that is well-balanced for both isothermal and isentropic background states. All properties are shown to carry over to the high-order DGSEM on general curvilinear meshes. Several numerical examples confirm the theoretical findings and show the robustness and accuracy of the scheme for use in modern dynamical cores for atmospheric flows.
items.authors: Marco Artiano, Kieran Ricardo, Oswald Knoth, Peter Spichtinger, Hendrik Ranocha

items.title: Coupled Seasonal Data Assimilation of Sea Ice, Ocean, and Atmospheric Dynamics over the Last Millennium
items.abstract: "Online" data assimilation (DA) is used to generate a seasonal-resolution reanalysis dataset over the last millennium by combining forecasts from an ocean--atmosphere--sea-ice coupled linear inverse model with climate proxy records. Instrumental verification reveals that this reconstruction achieves the highest correlation skill, while using fewer proxies, in surface temperature reconstructions compared to other paleo-DA products, particularly during boreal winter when proxy data are scarce. Reconstructed ocean and sea-ice variables also have high correlation with instrumental and satellite datasets. Verification against independent proxy records shows that reconstruction skill is robust throughout the last millennium. Analysis of the results reveals that the method effectively captures the seasonal evolution and amplitude of El Ni\~{n}o events, seasonal temperature trends that are consistent with orbital forcing over the last millennium, and polar-amplified cooling in the transition from the Medieval Climate Anomaly to the Little Ice Age.
items.authors: Zilu Meng, Gregory J. Hakim, Eric J. Steig

items.title: Flo: A data-driven limited-area storm surge model
items.abstract: We present Flo, a data-driven storm surge model, covering the North Sea, Norwegian Sea and Barents Sea. The model is built using the Anemoi framework for creating machine learning weather forecasting systems, developed by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and partners. The model is based on a graph neural network, and is capable of simulating water level due to atmospheric effects (wind stress and inverse barometer effect, i.e. the non-tidally induced part of the total water level; the residual water level) at a horizontal resolution of 4 km and a temporal resolution of 1 hour with a quality comparable to the numerical model on which it was trained. The model was trained using a dataset consisting of 43 years of atmospheric data from the 3-km Norwegian Reanalysis hindcast for mean sea level pressure and winds, and the NORA-Surge hindcast for water level. Evaluation was done by comparing results from hindcast runs of the Flo model against independent observations of more than 90 water level gauges along the European coast, and against the NORA-Surge hindcast. The evaluation shows that Flo produces hindcasts with accuracy similar to the NORA-Surge hindcast, and it is shown that the model can resolve key physical processes. As the NORA-Surge hindcast used for training does not include data assimilation, Flo is not expected to systematically outperform the numerical model when evaluated against observations. Nevertheless, the present work represents an important step towards complementing traditional physics-based storm surge modelling with machine learning approaches and the framework establishes a strong foundation for future developments, particularly for training storm surge models that offer more flexibility for incorporating observations and other additional data sources.
items.authors: Nils Melsom Kristensen, Mateusz Matuszak, Paulina Tedesco, Ina Kristine Berentsen Kullmann, Johannes R\"ohrs

items.title: Nutation Damping from Core-Mantle Boundary Topography
items.abstract: Periodic gravitational forcing by the Moon and Sun produces small oscillations in Earth's rotation known as nutations. Nutations are amplified by a resonance with a natural motion of the liquid core called the Free Core Nutation, whose amplitude is limited by friction-like processes at the core--mantle boundary. Previous studies have attributed this damping to the dissipation of electric currents induced in the lower conducting mantle, but, given current knowledge of the lower mantle, electromagnetic coupling appears insufficient to fully account for the observed lag. We show that additional dissipation arises from the interaction of the tidal flow inside the core with the topography of the core--mantle boundary, which excites internal waves that extract energy and momentum from the flow. Adapting a theory originally developed for tides over seafloor topography, we find that the observed damping can be fully accounted for by a topography of typical amplitude $\sim 5$ km dominated by features of wavelength $\sim$1500~km. The dissipation is highest when the upper core is neutrally buoyant. Such amplitudes are larger than typical inferences from global seismic studies but are not ruled out, given regional seismic evidence for kilometer-scale features and the sparse constraints at these scales.
items.authors: J. Rekier, S. A. Triana, A. Barik, D. Abdulah, W. Kang

items.title: Eigenwaves: Finite-frequency Eigenrays in Elastic Anisotropic Media
items.abstract: The Eigenray method solves two-point boundary-value ray-tracing problems in heterogeneous anisotropic elastic media using a variational formulation based on the eikonal equation. Here, we extend the method to finite frequencies using the trajectory-mechanics formulation in which finite-frequency effects are represented by a frequency-dependent potential that couples phase and amplitude. We show that finite-frequency propagation can be described within the same variational framework through an equivalent effective medium, preserving the structure of the original method while introducing corrections to trajectories, phase, amplitudes, geometric spreading, wavefront curvature, and caustic behavior. The resulting Eigenwave formulation requires only local modifications of the ray velocity and its derivatives and reduces to classical ray theory in the high-frequency limit. Numerical examples involving multipathing and cusp caustics demonstrate accurate modeling of finite-frequency propagation effects. While ray-based amplitudes become unreliable near caustics, a phase-space (Maslov) treatment successfully reproduces finite-difference wavefield solutions. These results establish Eigenwave theory as a unified framework connecting ray theory and finite-frequency wave propagation in heterogeneous anisotropic media.
items.authors: Zvi Koren

items.title: Broadband Ground-Motion Synthesis by Conditioning Denoising Diffusion Models on Low-Frequency Waveforms
items.abstract: Seismic hazard and structural analyses require broadband ground-motion time histories, yet the high-frequency band (above 1~Hz) is the hardest to obtain: physics-based simulations are too costly at these frequencies, and stochastic methods lose the deterministic phase, directivity, and long-period coherence that control structural demand. We present HighFEM-2, a latent denoising-diffusion waveform model trained with rectified flow matching on a multi-modal diffusion transformer. It synthesizes three-component acceleration up to 50~Hz, conditioned on a low-frequency waveform below the source corner frequency and on magnitude, hypocenter and station location, and $V_{S30}$. The low-frequency waveform supplies the deterministic source, path, and directivity, so the network learns only the regional high-frequency scattering. Conditioning each station on its own waveform lets HighFEM-2 generate records for all stations of an earthquake that share its source and low-frequency path terms. Trained on 195{,}138 Italian INSTANCE records ($M_w$ 1.4--6.5, within 200~km), HighFEM-2 produces realistic waveforms: it reproduces observed peak amplitudes with small bias ($0.042 \pm 0.088$ log units for PGA, $0.057 \pm 0.090$ for PGV) and matches observed envelopes, Fourier spectra, and integrated velocity and displacement. The conditioning waveform can come from a simulation or a filtered record, and ensembles of realizations sample the high-frequency variability given that input. HighFEM-2 thus provides fast, regionally calibrated broadband time histories for hazard and risk assessment, including near-fault scenarios where recordings are scarce.
items.authors: Kadek Hendrawan Palgunadi, Simon Dirmeier, Maria Koroni, Laura Ermert, Men-Andrin Meier

items.title: Efficient, Geometry-only Prediction of Advection-dominated Particle Transport through Saturated Soils
items.abstract: The environmental transport of microplastic particles has raised concerns because of their potential ecological and human-health impacts. A particular challenge for experiments on microplastic transport in soils is the fact that soil is a highly complex and non-transparent porous medium. Thus, our knowledge of transport mechanisms of microplastics in soils and related ecological implications is still limited and computational simulations offer an additional possibility to obtain important insights into the physical transport behaviour of microplastics. Yet, direct particle-resolved simulations in realistic soil structures for macroscopic sample sizes remain a computational challenge. We introduce an efficient pore-network model, minD-PNM, that predicts particle breakthrough curves in water-saturated soils using experimental X-ray micro-computed tomography ($\mu$CT) pore geometries as the only input. The model combines an approximately $t^{-3}$ pore-scale transit time distribution with a minimum-dissipation partition of multi-inlet-multi-outlet pores, and propagates these distributions through the pore network to predict breakthrough curves. We benchmark minD-PNM against lattice Boltzmann and immersed boundary simulations for small systems, and against microplastic column experiments in quartz sediments for macroscopic sample sizes. In both cases, the predicted breakthrough curves agree well with the corresponding reference data. Because it requires only geometric information, minD-PNM scales to macroscopic sample volumes offering a practical tool for contaminant-hydrology studies of particulate pollutants.
items.authors: Hao Liu, Rizwan Khaleel, Markus Rolf, Martin G. J. L\"oder, Christina Bogner, Stephan Gekle

items.title: Buried Fiber-Optic Geolocalization with Distributed Acoustic Sensing
items.abstract: We present a scalable method for geolocalizing buried fiber-optic cables using Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) and traffic-induced quasi-static seismic signals. Assuming access to one end of the fiber, the method fuses DAS measurements with vehicle trajectories obtained from either video tracking or vehicle-mounted GPS. The fiber geometry is estimated by minimizing the mismatch between the measured and physics-based synthetic strain-rate maps. The framework combines a matched-filter initialization with neural-network-based trajectory optimization, enabling robust convergence under realistic noise and trajectory-uncertainty conditions. Simulation and field experiments demonstrate sub-meter localization accuracy, often on the order of tens of centimeters, and strong agreement with manual calibration by tap-testing. This approach provides a practical tool for mapping poorly documented underground fiber infrastructure and for supporting urban sensing applications.
items.authors: Khen Cohen, Natanel Nissan, Ofir Nissan, Ariel Lellouch

items.title: Synthesis of Buprenorphine from Morphine
items.abstract: Buprenorphine is a WHO essential medicine widely used to treat pain and opioid addiction, which is currently manufactured from thebaine, a morphinan alkaloid obtained from the poppy plant. However, thebaine has a low abundance in natural poppy strains, its production is geographically concentrated, and recent years have seen global shortages. These factors present a potential vulnerability in the buprenorphine supply chain. Herein, we report the synthesis of buprenorphine from morphine, the most abundant and cheapest poppy alkaloid. To streamline the synthesis, with practical manufacture in mind, our route combines multiple transformations into several one-pot sequences. The synthesis of buprenorphine from a more available starting material may help to ensure continued supply of this critical therapeutic.
items.authors: Robert Messias, Jonathan C. Moore, Kieran D. Jones, Stephen P. Argent, Aakarsh Saxena, Hon Wai Lam

items.title: Toward a New Paradigm for Renewable Biopolymer Selection: A Structure–Processing–Architecture–Property–Scalability Framework (Alginate, Cellulose, Lignin, Chitosan, and Starch)
items.abstract: Renewable biopolymers are increasingly explored as alternatives to fossil-derived materials, yet bio-based origin alone does not determine performance or commercial relevance. This review compares alginate, lignin, cellulose, chitosan, and starch through an integrated structure–processing–architecture–property–scalability framework. Molecular functionality — carboxylate-rich, aromatic, hydroxyl-rich, amine-rich, crystalline, branched, and charged structures — is linked to processing pathways and to the resulting coatings, fibers, crosslinked networks, porous structures, carbon materials, and composite architectures. A dedicated cross-cutting discussion then argues why the three comparison axes dominant in the existing literature, chemistry, biodegradability, and application category, each fail, on their own, to predict which material and processing combination is actually useful for a given job, and what a comparison needs to include instead. The review closes with application-specific design rules to support material and processing selection for sustainable packaging, thermal insulation, water purification and separations, CO2 capture, energy storage and electrocatalysis, biomedical scaffolds and controlled release, and construction materials.
items.authors: Parastou Kharazmi

items.title: A Decision-Making Framework for Renewable Biopolymer Selection: Integrating Structure, Processing, Properties, Scalability, Techno-Economics, and Life-Cycle Assessment
items.abstract: Renewable biopolymers are often compared by feedstock origin, biodegradability, or isolated material properties. These comparisons do not, by themselves, support an engineering decision because a useful material is not a polymer in isolation: it is a biopolymer processed into a defined architecture for a specified application and manufactured under practical constraints. This study presents a semi-quantitative multi-criteria decision-making framework for selecting renewable biopolymer systems across alginate, cellulose, lignin, chitosan, and starch. The framework evaluates a material–processing route–architecture–application decision unit through five linked dimensions: molecular functionality, processing compatibility, resulting architecture, applicationrelevant performance, and scalability. Scores are accompanied by evidence-confidence flags and are tested under three application-specific weighting scenarios — balanced, performance-led, and manufacturability-led — so that the framework reports conditional candidates and genuine ranking reversals rather than a universal material ranking. Sustainable packaging coatings and films, thermal-insulation panels and porous materials, and adsorption-based water treatment using biopolymer sorbents are used as contrasting demonstration cases. For packaging, barrier performance under relevant humidity, mechanical integrity, food-contact compatibility, converting compatibility, and end-of-life are prioritised. For insulation, thermal conductivity at realistic moisture content, density, dimensional stability, drying intensity, moisture management, and manufacturability are prioritised. For water treatment, adsorption capacity and selectivity, regeneration and reuse, aqueous-state stability, and feedstock cost and availability at scale are prioritised. The method explicitly separates reported evidence from missing evidence, and the worked sensitivity analysis finds genuine ranking reversals for packaging and insulation alongside a stable, target-class-specific robust result for water treatment. Available technoeconomic and life-cycle evidence is incorporated as illustrative, application-specific data points rather than as a substitute for a dedicated assessment. The framework provides a reproducible bridge between qualitative renewable-biopolymer reviews and application-specific materialsystem design.
items.authors: Parastou Kharazmi

items.title: Diabat 2.0: A Comprehensive Diabatization Toolkit for Multichromophoric Systems
items.abstract: The construction of physically meaningful quasi-diabatic states and the evaluation of their electronic couplings are essential for describing nonadiabatic processes in molecular aggregates and other multichromophoric systems. Existing software implementations, however, are often restricted to dimers, two-state models, or particular types of quasi-diabatic states. Here, we present Diabat 2.0, a comprehensive toolkit for multistate diabatization in multichromophoric systems. It constructs the adiabatic-to-diabatic (ATD) transformation based on the adiabatic-state wave functions and energies obtained from external quantum chemistry calculations, yielding quasi-diabatic states and their electronic couplings in a nearly black-box manner. Diabat 2.0 implements several advanced ATD methods, including a general approach that can reliably construct quasi-diabatic states with diverse charge and excitation distributions without prescribing state types. This enables Diabat 2.0 to support diabatization in a broad range of scenarios that involve not only conventional charge-transfer, locally excited, and correlated triplet pair states, but also a variety of exotic states, such as mixed radical-triplet states, trion states, radical-coupled triplet-pair states, and charge-localized dicationic states. These capabilities are demonstrated in applications to several multichromophoric systems that pose substantial challenges to existing software.
items.authors: Yu-Chen Wang, Yicheng Qin, Yi Zhao, WanZhen Liang

items.title: Physics-Guided Soft Sensing under Sparse Laboratory Measurements and Temporal Regime Shifts in Industrial Monoammonium Phosphate Production
items.abstract: Industrial plants collect high-frequency telemetry while critical quality variables may be measured only every few hours. We study soft sensing for an industrial monoammonium phosphate process using 260,642 one-minute records and 1,325 paired laboratory observations. The grey-box model reconstructs latent acid properties from conductivity and combines them with material-balance calculations to estimate molar ratio and downstream density. Validation is entirely chronological: nine pre-gap rolling tests, a short-term regime-transfer test, a strict external post-gap test on 438 future laboratory pairs, and ten post-gap rolling comparisons. To prevent uncontrolled extrapolation, the conductivity input to the fitted latent-property mappings is limited to the range observed in the corresponding training data. Ridge and LSBoost remain more accurate than the physics-guided model, particularly in the independent long-horizon evaluation. The results show that physical structure improves interpretability but does not by itself ensure temporal robustness, motivating regime-aware monitoring, recalibration, and fallback logic for industrial virtual telemetry.
items.authors: German A. Karnup, Andrey N. Sychev, Oleg A. Telminov, Evgeny S. Gornev

items.title: Dual-Ligand Engineering of a Stable and High-Utilization Iron Complex Anolyte for Alkaline All-Iron Flow Batteries
items.abstract: Alkaline all-iron flow batteries offer a low-cost and inherently safe approach to large-scale energy storage, but Fe-complex anolytes remain limited by insufficient coordination stability, solubility, and utilization at high concentrations. Here, we develop a dual-ligand Fe(TEA)(PS) anolyte using triethanolamine as the primary ligand and pyridine-3-sulfonate (PS) as the secondary ligand. The secondary ligand reinforces the Fe coordination environment through pyridyl-N coordination while introducing a hydrophilic sulfonate group. Computational calculations and Fe K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal an enlarged molecular configuration and a more saturated coordination environment. Fe(TEA)(PS) exhibits a reversible Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox couple at -0.87 V versus SHE and a solubility of 1.41 M in 2 M NaOH. The resulting full cell achieves 95.12% electrolyte utilization at 1.0 M and a peak power density of 422.8 mW cm -2 . It retains 98.28% of its capacity over 1200 cycles at 100 mA cm -2 . Moreover, a cell containing 0.8 M Fe(TEA)(PS) maintains 96.87% capacity after 1800 cycles, corresponding to a decay rate of only 0.0017% per cycle. These results establish second-ligand engineering as an effective strategy for developing stable, highly soluble, and highly utilized Fe-complex anolytes for alkaline all-iron flow batteries.
items.authors: Heng Wang, Zhiyu Wang, Tianyu Yang, Hongtao Xie, Yingjia Hu, Qing Wang

items.title: Neural Kinetics: Learning Kinetics as Transport in Compositional Space
items.abstract: Complex bio-derived and fossil mixtures contain thousands of molecules whose individual structures and reaction pathways cannot be fully resolved, making conventional mechanism-based kinetic modelling impractical. A reaction network detailed enough to describe every formula-level transformation would contain far more reactions and parameters than the available data can constrain. We propose to overcome this limitation by representing mixtures directly as abundance fields on a compositional grid indexed by molecular descriptors, specifically carbon number (#C) and double-bond equivalent (DBE), and by learning a time-conditioned, chemistry-informed operator that maps the initial composition to predict a later state. The evolution rates of the chemical space are learned by a two-dimensional Fourier neural operator (FNO) acting jointly on a set of heteroatom classes, with normalized time and compositional coordinates appended as input channels. Because experimental data are limited, we enlarge the training set with synthetic trajectories generated from the measured samples, pre-train on this ensemble, and then calibrate a small subset of parameters on the measured distributions. We tested the framework on a case of oxidation of a complex hydrocarbon mixture that is tracked by FTICR-MS over sixty seconds of reaction. On an independent sample the framework, that we named NeuralKinetics, reproduced the measured endpoint class composition within a mean absolute error of approximately one percent and arranged the heteroatom classes correctly on the compositional grid. The second test was an entirely different system: litter decomposition in a peatland warming experiment, also followed by FTICR-MS but over two years. The developed operator accurately predicted the endpoint class composition of the held-out sample proving that the framework is flexible enough to adapt to diverse reactive systems.
items.authors: Paolo Guida, Naydu Zambrano Urrutia, Elia Colleoni, Shekhar R Kulkarni, Kevin Van Geem, William L. Roberts

items.title: Multiscale Insights into CO2 Chemisorption and Proton Transfer in Choline-Imidazolate based Deep Eutectic solvents: Exploring the Effect of Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Alkanolamine on Reaction Pathways and Product Distribution
items.abstract: Understanding how solvent composition governs competitive CO 2 chemisorption within solvents is essential for the rational design of solvents for CO 2 capture. In this work, we combine density functional theory (DFT), classical molecular dynamics (cMD), and microkinetic modeling to investigate CO 2 chemisorption in choline-imidazolate based systems containing different alkanolamine hydrogen bond donors (HBDs): monoethanolamine (MEA), diethanolamine (DEA), and methyldiethanolamine (MDEA). By systematically characterizing the thermodynamics, kinetics and liquid structure influence, our results show that within these systems, choline is the preferred CO 2 -binding site unless a HBD is present. Accordingly, the MEA system shifts almost entirely to amine-centered carbamate formation, the DEA system retains carbamate dominance but with stronger competition from choline-centered capture, and the MDEA system which additionally includes water shifts back toward choline-centered carbonate together with a competitive water-assisted bicarbonate pathway. The findings illustrate how CO 2 chemisorption in multicomponent liquids is controlled by a combination of intrinsic reaction thermodynamics, liquid-structure, and CO 2 concentration. More broadly, this work provides insights that will facilitate molecular-level design of solvents for CO 2 uptake and regeneration.
items.authors: Osasumwen J. Ikponmwosa, S.M Gulam Rabbani, Stephen P. Vicchio, Rachel B. Getman

items.title: Sisyphus: A Topology-Compiled Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Platform with Structure-Only Input and Bayesian Parameter Refinement
items.abstract: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models provide a mechanistic framework for drug disposition, but compound-specific parameterization remains a practical constraint when experimental absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) measurements are unavailable. Sisyphus is an open-source platform that compiles ordinary differential equations from a typed physiological graph and uses molecular structure plus dose to generate oral maximum plasma concentration (Cmax) predictions. Seven fitted models support ADME estimation and a four-track geometric blend of mechanistic, direct machine-learning, clearance-based, and distribution-based predictions. This revision reconciles the manuscript with public training snapshots and a source audit of clinical reference records. Of 107 repeatedly accessed development compounds, 73 retain evaluable reference Cmax values. The hybrid prediction has a geometric mean absolute fold error (AAFE) of 2.830 (conditional bootstrap 95% confidence interval 2.30-3.52), with 43.8% of predictions within twofold; engine-only and direct machine-learning AAFE are 3.872 and 3.049. These data do not establish independent generalization or superiority of the hybrid. The user-facing residual band is development-derived and is not valid split-conformal calibration. A selected ten-compound measured-input diagnostic lowers engine AAFE from 6.708 to 5.968, while new same-model synthetic experiments illustrate Bayesian updating with explicit effective-sample-size and interval diagnostics. Neither experiment establishes clinical accuracy. A previously reported temporal cohort has been consumed by repeated analysis, and no untouched external performance estimate is available. The platform's contribution is the integration of topology-compiled simulation, structure-driven parameterization, and experimental observation-informed refinement, together with an auditable account of data provenance and limitations. Negative development experiments identify unsuccessful tested strategies; they do not demonstrate an intrinsic structure-only accuracy ceiling or a verified bioavailability-specific cause of error.
items.authors: Jae Min Yoon

items.title: Dopant-Controlled Gas Adsorption and Electronic Response in AlN-and BP-Doped Two-Dimensional Fullerene Networks: A DFT and Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics Study
items.abstract: Using density functional theory (DFT) and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), we investigated the structural stability, electronic properties, and gas adsorption behaviour of AlN-and BP-doped quasi-2D C60 fullerene networks (C58AlN and C58BP). Both heteroatom-pair substitutions maintain structural and thermal stability. Dopant chemistry strongly governs adsorption preferences: C58AlN exhibits robust binding (CO2:-2.79 eV, H2O:-1.27 eV, N2:-0.50 eV), whereas C58BP shows weak interactions. Charge analysis confirms significant electronic redistribution during adsorption. Crucially, adsorption strength does not dictate sensing performance; N2 triggers the highest conductivity modulation despite weaker adsorption. Overall, heteroatom-pair engineering offers a valuable strategy to tune gas capture and sensing capabilities in fullerene-based 2D materials.
items.authors: Poonam Devi, Neetu Yadav, VIVEK KUMAR YADAV

items.title: What sixty studies of V2O5 supercapacitor electrodes can and cannot tell us: a validated dataset with study-grouped analysis
items.abstract: Vanadium pentoxide (V 2 O 5 ) is one of the most studied electrode materials for supercapacitors. Hundreds of studies report its specific capacitance, but it is not clear whether these data can be combined to predict the performance of a new electrode. To examine this, 974 records from 60 published studies were collected into one dataset, and each record was linked to its source. Within each study, the data behave as expected. Capacitance decreases as the charge-discharge rate increases, and this decrease is well described by a simple power law. Adding a composite partner or a dopant raises the capacitance by about 1.6 times compared with pure V 2 O 5 tested in the same study. Between studies, however, the picture is different. The median capacitance reported for pure V 2 O 5 differs up to 27 times from one study to another. A model trained on some studies could not predict the values reported in others (R 2 = 0.11), although a random split of the same data suggested good accuracy (R 2 = 0.76). One likely reason is that key electrode details, such as mass loading and active mass, are reported for only about one fifth of the records. A short list of details that future studies should report is proposed. The dataset and scripts are openly available.
items.authors: Taha Yasin EKEN

items.title: Reaction-Network Kinetics of Lignin Hydrothermal Liquefaction: Effect of Cu Incorporation Strategy
items.abstract: Cu-based catalysts can enhance bio-oil production during the hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) of lignin; however, the influence of Cu incorporation strategy on individual reaction pathways remains insufficiently understood. In this study, experimental HTL of lignin under direct Cu-assisted and Cu-impregnated conditions was investigated over 200–320 °C and residence times of 5–25 min, together with a five-pathway lumped kinetic model. Apparent kinetic parameters were estimated by nonlinear regression of the experimental product yields. The model captured the principal evolution of residual solid, bio-oil, water-soluble fraction, and gas over the investigated conditions. The maximum bio-oil yield was obtained at 280 °C and 15 min, increasing from 24.87% for the direct process to 28.74% for Cu-impregnated lignin. Kinetic analysis revealed pathway-dependent effects of Cu impregnation. At 280 °C, the apparent residual-solid-to-bio-oil rate constant (k1) increased from 0.0211 to 0.0402 min-1, whereas the fitted contribution of the direct residual-solid-to-gas pathway (k3) was substantially lower following Cu impregnation. The apparent bio-oil-to-gas rate constant (k4) also increased at elevated temperatures, indicating stronger secondary conversion of bio-oil under more severe conditions. Arrhenius analysis further showed differences in the apparent activation energies and pre-exponential factors of the dominant pathways. Overall, the results demonstrate that Cu impregnation modifies the apparent distribution of reaction pathways rather than uniformly increasing all fitted rate constants, providing a quantitative kinetic framework for understanding the influence of Cu incorporation strategy on lignin HTL.
items.authors: Ankit Kumar, Sivamohan N.

items.title: Cation-Deficient Tantalum Oxide–Zinc Tantalate Nanocomposite for Photocatalytic Carbon Dioxide Conversion
items.authors: Kio Kawata, Shoji Iguchi, Shimpei Naniwa, Akihisa Ishikawa, Wataru Ota, Tohru Sato

items.title: Off-line LCxLC-Mass Spectrometry Workflow using CID and EAD for the Quantification and Comprehensive Structural Double Bond Characterization of Glycerophospholipids in Plasma Samples
items.abstract: Here we describe an automated workflow using a PAL Robotic Tool Changer (RTC) system for plasma lipid sample preparation and off-line two-dimensional liquid chromatography (LCxLC) separation. The orthogonal chromatographic platform couples hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC) in the first dimension with rapid reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RPLC) in the second dimension, facilitated by automated fraction collection at 10-second intervals into 96-well plates. Lipid profiling and structural identification strategies were evaluated using collision-induced dissociation (CID) and electron-activated dissociation (EAD) across data-dependent acquisition (DDA), dataindependent acquisition (DIA / SWATH), and high-resolution multiple reaction monitoring (HRMRM) modes. Standard Reference Material NIST SRM 1950 (Human Plasma) was employed for lipid quantification and double-bond characterization of phosphatidylcholines (PCs). By combining automated modified Matyas liquid-liquid extraction, and off-line LCxLC, a total of 115 PC’s lipids could be detected in SRM 1950 plasma sample. For 74 PC’s including isomers, double assignments could be proposed based on the EAD spectra.
items.authors: Laura Gisela González Iglesias, Renzo Picenoni, Guenter Boehm, Gérard Hopfgartner

items.title: SMILES serialization changes activity-cliff annotations in the MoleculeACE benchmark
items.abstract: MoleculeACE is a widely used benchmark that annotates activity-cliff compounds in 30 ChEMBL datasets and reports that machine-learning models predict them poorly. Its “soft consensus” criterion admits a compound pair when any of three similarities reaches 0.9: ECFP4 Tanimoto similarity, Tanimoto similarity of anonymized molecular graphs, or normalized Levenshtein similarity between SMILES strings. The first two are computed after parsing; the third operates on the supplied strings, which the benchmark code does not canonicalize. This study held molecules, potencies, thresholds and code fixed and varied only how the same molecules werewritten. A re-implementation reproduced the distributed labels exactly in 27 of 30 datasets, and canonical round-tripping changed amedian of 0.00% of labels. Re-serializing themolecules with two independent cheminformatics toolkits, with every rewritten string verified to encode the original molecule, changed a median of 8.98% (Indigo) and 9.48% (Open Babel) of compound labels; Kekulé SMILES from RDKit changed 5.23%, and randomized SMILES 17.05%. The graph-derived criteria were invariant across all rewrites. Because MoleculeACE stratifies its train/test split on the cliff label, changing the labels caused split membership to approach that of an independent redraw (31.3% of compounds reassigned, against a 32.21% ceiling). An end-to-end repair, with serialization-invariant labels, re-derived splits and retrained descriptorbased models, moved the pooled cliff penalty by −0.006 to +0.020 log units; every confidence interval included zero against a minimum detectable effect of 0.041–0.057, and for SVM the shift fell within the variability of same-definition split redraws of comparable magnitude. The distributed annotation is therefore reproducible but not invariant to valid serialization. Benchmarks that retain string-based criteria should specify and enforce the canonicalization contract (toolkit, version and output mode); otherwise, labels should be defined on parsed molecular representations. Serialization-invariant labels, splits and per-molecule predictions are released.
items.authors: Phongsakon Sriwicha

items.title: Decoding Polyurethane Breakdown: A QM/MM MD Exploration of UMG-SP3 Urethanase Catalysis
items.abstract: Polyurethane (PU) low-cost production and versatility propelled its widespread daily usage. However, due to a lack of efficient end-of-life waste treatment options, this recalcitrant polymer tends to accumulate, becoming hazardous. Enzyme depolymerization emerged as a promising 2 alternative to tackle this global problem. Accordingly, three metagenome-based urethanases were discovered (UMG-SP1, 2 and 3). Despite several efforts being made to understand their catalysis, none of the studies accounted for full protein sampling. To address this, we employed an umbrella sampling-based quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics methodology to explore UMG-SP3catalyzed urethane bond hydrolysis. Our results revealed that the hydrolytic mechanism occurred in two sequential stages: i) acylation; and ii) deacylation. The first stage was rate-limiting, with an energetic barrier of 21.6 kcal.mol-1, corresponding to the formation of the acyl-enzyme state and the release of an alcohol (leaving group). Remarkably, the energetic barrier was in agreement with the previously reported values for the UMG-SP2 homolog. In addition, the enzyme shown preference for the cleavage of the C-O bond instead of the C-N bond. However, we observed that the overall reaction was endergonic, with a product-state Gibbs free energy of 8.3 kcal.mol-1. UMG-SP3 has previously been shown to be less stable than the other UMG-SPs. As a result, its more mobile active site may be less effective at stabilizing the released product, increasing the associated free energy. Hence, to improve the likelihood of industrial implementation, the mechanistic data should be leveraged to rationally engineer a more stable and efficient enzyme. Altogether, these findings can pave the way for improving enzymatic depolymerization of PU.
items.authors: Luís M. C. Teixeira, Pedro Paiva, Alexander Sandahl, J. Preben Morth, Peter Westh, Daniel E. Otzen

items.title: Decoupling Thermal Kinetics and Structural Evolution in HfO2 RRAM via Broadband Impedance Spectroscopy: A SPICE Model for Analog Applications
items.abstract: The integration of HfO2-based resistive random-access memory (RRAM) into analog circuits and neuromorphic hardware requires accurate, physics-based small-signal models. In this work, we employ broadband impedance spectroscopy to physically isolate the distinct structural and kinetic components governing the alternating current (AC) response of TiN/Ti/HfO2/W memristive devices, thereby providing such a model. Measurements were performed over a wide temperature range (77 K to 350 K), across multiple device areas, and at various resistance states controlled by compliance current. The AC response reveals distinct relaxation processes, which are accurately described by an electrical equivalent circuit that isolates the individual electrical signatures of the filament constriction, the interfacial boundary, and the bulk conductive path. The low-frequency relaxation, attributed to the filament constriction, exhibits a strong exponential temperature dependence, allowing for the extraction of the thermal activation energy associated with trap-assisted charge transport within the oxygen vacancy-rich gap. In contrast, the bulk-related response is temperature-independent but strongly depends on the resistive state. The model is further validated by the scaling of the high‑frequency pole with device area, confirming its geometric origin. As a result, our model decouples the thermal kinetics from the structural evolution of conductive filaments in emerging non-volatile memories. Finally, to demonstrate the practical utility of this model, it is implemented in LTSpice to design all-memristive analog filters and a neuromorphic signal mixer. This approach takes advantage of the properties of both pristine and programmed devices to eliminate the need for conventional passive components.
items.authors: Salvador Dueñas, Guillermo Vinuesa, Héctor García, Helena Castán

items.title: Shaping single crystals through a controlled non-classical crystallization pathway
items.abstract: The ability to program the shape of single crystals through molten-state processing has transformed the manufacturing of inorganic materials, yet this strategy is fundamentally incompatible with most organic-based crystals, which decompose before melting. Here, we show that a non-classical crystallization pathway can overcome this limitation by generating a moldable dense-liquid intermediate during the growth of peptide-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). By engineering a reaction environment in which precursor concentration and reagent diffusion are controlled while suppressing convection, we selectively activate a liquid-liquid phase separation process to produce a confined dense-liquid phase that can be shaped prior to crystallization. Repeated diffusion-limited chemical perturbations subsequently transform this intermediate into single crystals that faithfully preserve the geometry of the confined environment in which they form, enabling non-equilibrium morphologies inaccessible by conventional synthesis. We further show that crystal shape influences mechanical properties, demonstrating that controlling crystallization pathways provides a route to tailor function without altering chemical composition.
items.authors: Thao Nguyen, João Pedro Vale, Oriol Arteaga, Annalisa Calò, James D. Nicholas, Roc Matheu

items.title: An Ion-Pair Complex-Enabled Photoinduced Cleavage of the Trifluoromethyl Thianthrenium Salt
items.abstract: Trifluoromethyl thianthrenium salts represent valuable reagents in photocatalysis; however, their activation traditionally necessitates external one-electron donors, such as photocatalysts, electron-donor-acceptor complexes. Direct photoexcitation can proceed without exogenous one-electron donors, thereby circumventing the stringent redox potential constraints inherent in the ground and excited states of conventional photocatalytic systems. Such direct excitation facilitates a transition of substrates to an electronically excited state, promoting homolytic cleavage to release the CF 3 • radical. Nevertheless, this process typically requires near-ultraviolet excitation (390 nm) to attain the high-energy excited singlet state of the substrate. In this study, we report a pioneering strategy involving the design of an acid-base ternary ion-pair complex utilising trifluoromethyl thianthrenium salts. In contrast to conventional ion-pair complex catalysis, this methodology eliminates the requirement for a photocatalyst and bypasses the single electron transfer process. This conceptual advancement lowers the activation energy to the excited singlet state of TT-CF 3 OTf, enabling the generation of CF 3 • species via homolytic cleavage under industrially preferred 450 nm excitation. As a proof of concept, the ion-pair complex was utilised to facilitate the trifluoromethylative difunctionalisation of diverse alkenes. This method yields pharmaceutically significant compounds and natural products with moderate to high yields. Both DFT calculations and experimental results demonstrate the formation of an ion-pairing complex, with binding constants K a of 4.36 in acetonitrile and 2.28 in chloroform, the latter increasing to 4.20 upon the addition of KOAc. This methodology exhibits substantial potential for future applications within biological and biochemical contexts.
items.authors: Ling Wang, Huda Hassan Dasuki, Mustapha Musa, Xuelong Zhang, Jonathan P. Knowles, Mark A. Fox

items.title: Decoding the Sequence Determinants of DNA Cleavage in Histidine-Containing Copper(II) Metallopeptides
items.abstract: The increasing global incidence of cancer, emerging viral infections, and antimicrobial resistance highlights the urgent need for innovative therapeutics with novel mechanisms of action. Nucleic acids, central to genetic information processing, are promising targets for therapeutic intervention through selective cleavage. Inspired by the biological activity of DNases and RNases, peptide-based metallonucleases—particularly those containing histidine—have emerged as versatile agents with tunable activity and potential applications in treating genetic diseases, including cancer. By analyzing a set of six copper(II) complexes with different histidine-containing tripeptides, this work investigates how peptide sequence influences several factors determining DNA-cleavage efficiency, such as speciation and conditional affinity at physiological pH, coordination mode, DNA binding, and ROS production. These findings offer a new framework for designing peptide-based copper nucleases and possibly identify a non-ATCUN sequence as a promising lead structure.
items.authors: Ana B. Caballero, Olga Iranzo, Patrick Gamez

items.title: Provenance-Aware Quality Control for Heterogeneous Bioactivity Data
items.abstract: Background. Machine-learning models for proteins increasingly train on large, pooled collections of laboratory measurements-binding affinities such as IC50, Ki, Kd and EC50 (numbers that describe how tightly a molecule binds its target), togetherwith biophysical readouts from techniques such as surface plasmon resonance (SPR), bio-layer interferometry (BLI) and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). These measurements arrive in different units, from different assay formats, fitted with different models, and at different levels of quality. Pooling them without care injects substantial noise. The per-record quality flags that some databases attach are incomplete, and they do not travel with the data once records from several sources are combined. What has been missing is an open, model-agnostic layer that turns raw measurements into records a downstream pipeline can consume directly: unit-normalized, quality-checked, and carrying their own uncertainty and provenance. What we built. biophys_interop is an open Python toolkit and data schema. It maps any supportedmeasurement to a single canonical record spanning 24 measurement types (modalities), converts units to a common standard, and runs a registry of 72 deterministic, method-aware quality-control (QC) rules. Every rule cites a reason from the measurement literature, recommends a concrete action, and returns a simple pass / warn / fail flag together with a calibrated uncertainty. The library is small and has few dependencies. We are deliberate about what our validation does and does not cover: two broadly applicable affinity rules (a plausible-value-range rule and an exact-duplicate rule) are tested at scale against an independent curator’s labels; the remaining method-specific biophysical rules are offered as a literaturegrounded, executable registry-useful and auditable, but not claimed as validated here, because no public database publishes the per-record ground-truth flags that would be needed to score them. Results. Using ChEMBL’s own data_validity_comment and potential_duplicate annotations as an independent ground truth, transparent rules on the standardized record reproduce two of ChEMBL’s three curator flag families on 175,387 held-out records across 30 human targets, with no trained model (value-range rule: Matthews correlation coefficient [MCC] 0.61; duplicate rule: MCC 0.65). The thresholds transfer cleanly to a completely separate set of targets (train on 15, test on 15 disjoint targets; 88,443 held-out records; MCC 0.73 and 0.64). Going beyond the curator, the layer flags 929 internally inconsistent records that ChEMBL did not flag, and a comparison against the independent BindingDB database exposes 38 disagreements of 100-fold or more, 89% of them unmarked by either database. A domain expert who checked a 24-record sample against the primary literature confirmed 16 of 24 (67%) as genuine data errors, including 11 of 12 cross-database conflicts. We reproduce the known cross-assay noise regime reported by Landrum and Riniker, and show that a comparability gate based on assay metadata more than halves the median disagreement between records (0.51- 0.21 log units). Finally, feeding the calibrated signal into a downstreammutation-effect (ΔΔG) predictor gave no reliable improvement; we report this negative result in full. The toolkit, the rule registry, the cleaned datasets, and one-command reproduction scripts are released openly. Conclusions. Once heterogeneous public measurements share one representation, simple transparent rules can catch data problems-matching expert curators at scale on the rule families we tested, and catching errors those curators missed. The result is a reusable, auditable data layer for protein machine learning, rather than a new predictive model. Keywords: bioactivity data; data curation; quality control; ChEMBL; BindingDB; data standardization; FAIR data; machine learning; interoperability; reproducibility
items.authors: Xin Gao

items.title: Raman Spectroscopy Reveals Isotope-specific Hydrogen Bond Kinetics in a Spherical Droplet leading to Preferential Evaporation of D2O in H2O-D2O Mixture
items.abstract: The evaporation of a spherical droplet having a pure solvent or a mixture of isotopic forms is fundamental to atmospheric physics, and critical for studying interfacial fluid dynamics, and hydrogen-bond kinetics. Understanding the hydrogen/deuterium bonded structural dynamics at molecular level during evaporation of isotopic water mixture (H2O/D2O) is important for understanding non-equilibrium phase transitions. In this work, we investigated real-time evaporation kinetics of spherical water droplets on superhydrophobic surface by time - dependent Raman spectroscopic method. Specifically, the results give an account for the variation of each H - or D-bonded clusters (ranging from fully tetrahedral ice-like structure to free water molecule) with time in the mixture from the time - dependent intensity change of each distinct vibrational stretching band of O-H or O-D. For pure H2O, the O-H peak intensities for all the clusters were decreasing with time, whereas for pure D2O, the ice-like structures vanished quickly with simultaneous increase in the free D2O molecules. In the mixture of H2O-D2O, based on Raman signal of each species, our experimental measurements suggested that the species having O-D or D2O was evaporating faster in comparison to the species having O-H or H2O. The results were also supported by the molecular dynamics simulation, which revealed that the bulk D2O was moving to the surface, and evaporating faster than H2O molecules.
items.authors: Sujay Paul, Dinesh Sharma, Arun Chattopadhyay

items.title: SCO ATLAS: Mapping Spin-Crossover Thermodynamics across Experimentally Grounded Fe(II)N6 Complexes
items.abstract: Research on the Spin-crossover (SCO) phenomenon has generated extensive experimental and computational data, distributed across hundreds of different sources, limiting systematic comparison and data reuse. Here, we introduce the SCO ATLAS, a data infrastructure that connects experimental sources with quantum chemistry computations and derived analyses, and we demonstrate its use through a first analysis devoted to the gas-phase thermodynamics of transition metal complexes (TMC) based on Fe(II)N6. Currently, the ATLAS includes 723 CSDderived crystallographic systems, from which 602 unique TMCs were retained for analysis. We map the thermodynamic landscape governing their molecular spin-state stability, identify the ranges of electronic and vibrational contributions compatible with SCO near room temperature, and show that ligand denticity modulates both components. Normal-mode analysis traces the denticity dependence of the vibrational entropy primarily to changes in ligand motion and the first coordination sphere. The homoleptic complexes are organized into 96 ligand families, with family identity accounting for approximately one-third of the within-denticity variation in ∆Helec. Across the complete dataset, ∆Helec is most strongly associated with the HS Fe–N distance. The released data, calculations and analysis tools provide a reusable framework for navigating SCO chemical space and developing future extensions of the ATLAS.
items.authors: Sergi Vela

items.title: Interaction effects and droplet dynamics in chitosan-coated nanoemulsions via echo-Diffusing Wave Spectroscopy
items.abstract: In this work, interaction effects and droplet dynamics in chitosan-coated nanoemulsions were investigated via echo-Diffusing Wave Spectroscopy (DWS). Medium-chain triglyceride (MCT) nanoemulsions containing 5–10% (w/w) oil were prepared with and without chitosan. Experimental photon transport mean free paths, were compared with non-interacting, hard-sphere, and excluded-annulus scattering models to evaluate the contribution of inter-droplet correlations. Intensity correlation functions were analyzed against scaled delay time, to account for differences in photon transport, while mean squared displacements (MSDs) were used to characterize inferred droplet motion. Chitosan incorporation produced non-monotonic changes in photon transport and correlation relaxation, while generally reducing the apparent droplet displacement. The excluded-annulus model provided a useful first approximation of selected intermediate-concentration formulations but was not able to capture the full concentration dependence, highlighting the limitations of representing the hydrated chitosan layer as a fixed exclusion boundary. The findings reveal a concentration-dependent interplay between longer-range interactions governing inter-droplet organization and hydrodynamic coupling and shorter-range interactions involving the hydrated polymer layer. This study demonstrates the value of echo-DWS for investigating interaction effects in polymer-coated nanoemulsions and provides a physical framework for their rational design as drug-delivery carriers.
items.authors: Logan-Marie Torry, Foluso Akin-Ige, Jose Huergo, Amy Yang, Leah Knight, Samiul Amin

items.title: Talking to instruments: device-integration standards for self-driving laboratories
items.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are rapidly outgrowing the single-instrument prototype, scaling into multi-instrument and multi-site platforms that run autonomous discovery across chemistry, materials science, biotechnology, pharmaceutical re-search and adjacent domains. What now decides whether an SDL can scale, share its integrations and federate experiments is no longer the algorithms or the robots, but the software layer that orchestrates heterogeneous devices. Today that layer is the bottleneck: a fast-growing ecosystem of open-source orchestrators in which most have built device integration on their own bespoke conventions instead of adopting a formally governed standard. The result is predictable and costly. Integrations do not transfer between laboratories, orchestrators cannot interoperate and many new SDLs rebuild their device-control layer from scratch. Crucially, this is an engineering coordination problem, not a fundamental scientific one and therefore among the most tractable bottlenecks in autonomous science. We map the device-integration standards landscape onto the open-source orchestrator ecosystem, compare the leading options and give scenario-driven guidance on when to use each. We then translate the requirements of autonomous operation into a concrete deliverable: a set of testable engineering criteria and a weighted procurement scorecard that defines an autonomous-ready control interface and gives institutional buyers the leverage to demand it; these requirements do not change as orchestration turns agentic: whether an instrument is driven by a program or by a language-model agent through a model-facing protocol, it is only as safe and reliable as the interface it exposes. Adopted at scale, these requirements turn device integration from a burden repaid lab by lab into shared infrastructure,
items.authors: Willi Gottstein, Lukas Bromig, Matthias Arnold, Sina Barazandeh, Joseph S Brown, Keith A. Brown

items.title: Unveiling the Potential of Biomass-Accessible Bifuran Unit in Conjugated Polymers: Synthesis, Thermal Properties, Photophysics, and Comparative Study with Phenylene and Thiophene Analogues for OLED Applications
items.abstract: The bifuran unit is a biomass-accessible building block for organic electronic materials; however, its application in electroluminescent devices remains largely unexplored. In this study, polycondensation reactions of a bifuran diboronic ester with nine aryl dibromides were examined. The obtained polymers (PBFAr)s showed strongly comonomer-dependent yields and solubilities. Detailed solution-state and device characterization was focused on the soluble fluorene-containing polymer PBFAr1. For comparison, analogous polymers containing phenylene (PSPhAr1), biphenyl (PBPhAr1), and bithiophene (PBTAr1) units were also synthesized. In chloroform solution, PBFAr1 and its bithiophene-based analogue PBTAr1 exhibited photoluminescence quantum yields of 43% and 39%, respectively. Kelvin probe measurements indicated an energy-level alignment with the ITO anode that may facilitate hole injection. Solution-processed OLEDs with an ITO/PEDOT:PSS/emissive polymer/LiF/Al architecture were fabricated, and the PBFAr1-based device exhibited cyan electroluminescence at 484 nm, demonstrating that PBFAr1 can function as an emissive layer in a solution-processed OLED. These results demonstrate the potential of bifuran-based conjugated polymers as emissive materials for further development in organic optoelectronic applications.
items.authors: Shekhar Gupta, Yuya Tanaka, Nobuya Hiroshiba, Takeshi Mori, Hitoshi Saomoto, Ryusei Makiko

items.title: Metal-Free Traceless Directing Group-Assisted Cascade Cyclisation of 2-Alkynylquinazolinones for the Synthesis of Enpyrroloquinazolinones and Their Anticancer Activity
items.abstract: Pyrroloquinazolinones, representing the pharmacological scaffold of the natural product Luotonin A, exhibit significant biological activities. Distinguishing from metal-catalysed methodologies, this study delineates a metal-and photocatalystfree strategy for the synthesis of enpyrroloquinazolinone derivatives via a cascade Michael addition-cyclisation-denitrative aromatisation, involving 2-alkynyl quinazolinones and nitroalkenes, which renders the nitro group into a traceless directing group. The resultant enpyrroloquinazolinone analogues underwent systematic evaluation for their anticancer efficacy and potential to activate caspases 3/7 against A549 (NSCLC) and SW480 (colorectal) cancer cell lines. Furthermore, molecular modelling indicates that these enpyrroloquinazolinones possess substantial potential as effective inhibitors of topoisomerase I, providing a promising foundation for the continued development of topoisomerase I inhibitors for therapeutic interventions.
items.authors: Han-Kui Wu, Ling Wang, Anjana Patel, William Midgley, Mustapha Musa, Ehmke Pohl

items.title: Laser ablation rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry imaging with few-micrometer sampling pixels
items.abstract: Achieving sub-cellular resolution in ambient, matrix-free mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) remains challenging because reducing the sampling area often compromises ion yield and image fidelity. Here, we demonstrate an infrared laser–driven ambient MSI platform that mitigates these limitations through low-fluence, picosecond pulsed, highrepetition-rate laser ablation with a custom 2.94 μm light source with near-diffraction limited beam quality. This approach produces well-confined ablation features with diameters of 5μm to 10 μm. Coupling the laser ablation plume to a rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry (LA-REIMS) interface and a commercial time-of-flight mass analyser provides multiplexed ion maps of metabolites, phospholipids, and other small molecules in a single acquisition. This configuration enables routine 3 μm-pixel size imaging of fresh-frozen tissue sections, as well as imaging of formalin-fixed, paraffin embedded biopsy samples, all without additional preparation steps. Oversampled images preserve sub-cellular morphology and yield molecular distributions that correlate with fluorescence and histological features. Together, these results define a robust operational regime for high-fidelity, matrix-free MSI in the few-μm pixel range, where high infrared beam quality and stable, low-fluence, high repetition rate picosecond laser sampling underpin gentle ablation and efficient ion formation via REIMS, enabling sub-cellular molecular mapping in a clinically compatible, fully ambient format.
items.authors: Yu Wang, Ronan Battle, William Francis, Lucy Noyes, Daniel Simon, Yayue Song

items.title: Efficient Microwave-Enhanced Solid Phase Peptide Synthesis of Secretin Hormones Amenable for Rapid Library Design and Lead Optimization
items.abstract: Microwave-enhanced solid phase peptide synthesis of complex, therapeutically relevant, aspartimide-prone secretin hormones was achieved under optimized conditions with economical and commercially available protected amino acids. In order to determine robust and general methods, standard Fmoc SPPS conditions, Oxyma-buffered deprotection solution, Fmoc-(Dmb)Gly-OH, Fmoc-Asp(OMpe)-OH, and combinations thereof were systematically evaluated for crude purity using LC-MS. Aspartimide formation was significantly reduced, and syntheses were completed in a single run without the need for expensive, commercially inaccessible, or diversity-limiting peptide fragments or pseudoprolines, supplying methods amenable for rapid library generation, hit-to-lead endeavors, and lead optimization.
items.authors: Brenson A. Jassim, Kyle T. Faivre, Severin T. Schneebeli

items.title: Computational assessment, against criteria specified in advance, of a Na+/Ag+ ion-exchange route to Ag2MgSiO4, a predicted wurtzite-derived silver silicate
items.abstract: Many metastable inorganic compounds exist only because a synthetic route delivers them, and database screening is poorly placed to find them. Topotactic ion exchange is such a route: at low temperature it swaps the mobile cation of a known parent for another, ideally while the framework stays intact, yet it is rarely assessed computationally before synthesis. We test whether a simple exchange-energy criterion, specified in advance and checked against independent calculations, can nominate a credible target. Computed with a machine-learned interatomic potential, the criterion reproduced the sign of 42 published DFT exchange enthalpies (36/36 for |∆H| ≥ 10 kJ mol−1) and selected Ag2MgSiO4, to be made from Na2MgSiO4 in molten AgNO3. Density functional theory gives an exchange energy of about −58 kJ mol−1 per Ag, within the ±10 kJ mol−1 window around three reported preparations of silver silicates and germanates from sodium parents in molten AgNO3, and an energy above the hull (0.038–0.042 eV atom−1) like that of known silver silicates. The Pna21 structure is dynamically stable in the harmonic approximation (0 K). Calculated Ag+ hop barriers are comparable to or lower than those of a reported Ag+ conductor, and the HSE06 gap, calibrated on one literature value, is about 3 eV, at the violet edge of the visible range. These are 0 K predictions; no synthesis was attempted, and the closest precedent is Ag2MnSiO4, so a single exchange experiment can confirm or refute them (incomplete exchange or changes in particle size and shape are reported in some precedents).
items.authors: Chulmin Pyo

items.title: Non-Covalent Interactions Directed Azobenzene Crystals: Photoisomerization-Induced Melting and Melt-Mediated Polymorphism
items.abstract: Azobenzene molecular crystals have emerged as a compelling class of stimuli-responsive materials, yet the structural factors that determine whether a given crystal bends, melts, or remains entirely inert under UV irradiation are far from understood.
