Here, we investigate a series of eight structurally homologous 2,2′-dihydroxyazobenzene derivatives (Azo-0 to Azo-7) in which terminal functional groups (‒OH vs. ‒OMe) and pendant alkyl spacer length are independently varied, allowing the contributions of intramolecular conformation, intermolecular packing topology, and lattice compliance to be disentangled. Single-crystal Xray diffraction (SCXRD), UV-vis spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), together with thermal-stage polarized optical microscopy, reveal two mechanistically distinct melting pathways. The central finding is that an intramolecular O-H···N hydrogen bond, present in four derivatives (Azo-0, Azo-1, Azo-3, Azo-5), forms a pseudo-six-membered chelate ring that locks the azobenzene core in its planar trans conformation, fully suppressing photoisomerization in both solution and solid state. Removal of this intramolecular constraint through ‒OMe substitution liberates the azobenzene core in Azo-2, Azo-4, Azo-6, and Azo-7, enabling efficient and fully reversible cis-trans photoisomerization with visible-light-driven recovery. Critically, irradiation of these unlocked crystals below their equilibrium melting points (Ts Tm) triggers rapid, cooperative crystal-to-liquid transitions that are absent in the dark and under 456 nm light irradiation, establishing photoisomerization-induced lattice strain—not photothermal heating—as the operative mechanism. The sole outlier, Azo-5, melts under intense UV irradiation through a purely photothermal pathway, consistent with its locked conformation and strong 370 nm light absorption. Additionally, Azo-7 undergoes a thermally driven solid, liquid, solid polymorphic transformation: melt-recrystallization converts the high-melting polymorph Azo-7α (Tm ≈ 59 °C) into a structurally distinct, lower-melting polymorph Azo-7β (Tm ≈ 42 °C), demonstrating that thermal history is itself an independent handle for programming crystal packing. These findings translate directly into three molecular design principles for photomechanical organic crystals: phenolic OH gates the photoisomerization switch via intramolecular hydrogen bonding; alkyl chain length tunes lattice compliance and packing dimensionality; and melt-mediated crystals provide access to structurally and thermally distinct polymorphic forms.
items.authors: Ritika Kadiyan, Saptarshi Datta, Jagan Rajamoni, Nicholas Johnson, Jinjia Xu

items.title: A Biobased Epoxy Resin with Sequential Thermoplastic-to-Thermoset Curing Enables Removable-to-Permanent Adhesive Bonding
items.abstract: Adhesives are commonly designed either as reworkable thermoplastics or permanently crosslinked thermosets. Here, sequential thermoplastic-to-thermoset curing enables a simple two-component formulation based on a bio-based epoxy resin to function first as a removable hot-melt adhesive and subsequently as a permanent structural adhesive. Reaction of diglycidyl ether of vanillyl alcohol (DGEVA) and anilinium methanesulfonate at 110 °C produces a thermoplastic intermediate that is solid at room temperature but flows upon reheating and dissolves in selected solvents. This intermediate forms load-bearing joints that can be thermally debonded and rebonded or disassembled by dissolution. Further heating induces crosslinking and converts the same adhesive layer into a permanent epoxy network, increasing the apparent lap-shear strength nearly eightfold and rendering the joint resistant to disassembly under the same solvent conditions. This curing sequence therefore assigns reworkability and high-strength permanent bonding to successive adhesive states within the same formulation.
items.authors: Izabela Kurowska, Kaan Yorganci, Nora Aranburu, Itxaso Calafel, Amaia Agirre, Leire Unanue

items.title: Membraneless microdroplets generate thermodynamically distinct states of water under fully hydrated conditions
items.abstract: Water is indispensable for life, yet aqueous environments can thermodynamically disfavor dehydration-driven condensation reactions relevant to prebiotic polymer formation. Whether hydrated, dynamically reorganizing compartments can establish hydration thermodynamics distinct from the surrounding solution remains unclear. Here, we show that membraneless polyester microdroplets derived from prebiotically plausible α-hydroxy acids sustain spatially organized hydration environments during thermal structural reorganization. Combining high-speed scanning ion conductance microscopy, spatially resolved Raman spectroscopy and temperature-dependent wide-angle X-ray scattering, we resolve dynamic interfaces, spatial hydration gradients and reversible polymer organization. Crucially, Raman-derived average hydrogen-bond coordination within the droplets remains lower and markedly less temperature-dependent than in the corresponding aqueous solution. Van’t Hoff analysis of intact versus broken hydrogen bonds reveals attenuated apparent enthalpic and entropic contributions to redistribution. Together, these findings demonstrate that dynamically reconfiguring polymer-rich compartments can maintain distinct hydration thermodynamics during thermal perturbation, linking the physical chemistry of water with soft compartmentalization under hydrated conditions.
items.authors: Chen Chen, Shinji Watanabe, Linhao Sun, Kiyohiro Adachi, Priyanka Sharma, Tony Z. Jia

items.title: Thickness dependent HER activity of individual MXene flakes revealed by SECCM
items.abstract: MXenes, 2D transition metal carbides, provide unique properties for a large range of applications including electrocatalysis and energy storage. Specifically, Ti 3 C 2 T x , has shown activity for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). MXenes are conductive, present a rich surface chemistry and do not contain rare and expensive elements. They are promising for next generation catalyst materials. Here, we study the HER activity of individual single-layer and multilayer Ti 3 C 2 T x flakes, using SECCM and ex situ AFM. Our results show that multilayer flakes have a much larger overpotential, revealing that the reaction proceeds more slowly in the interlayer volume compared to the open basal plane of a single layer. This opens avenues of optimization for MXene catalyst layer formulation that have not been considered before.
items.authors: Maryam Alihosseini, Samaneh Salek, Joshua Byers, Guillaume Goubert

items.title: Guiding chromatographic purification through data-driven condition recommendations
items.abstract: Purification is essential for isolating compounds for reliable characterization and subsequent experiments; however, suitable chromatographic conditions are often still selected through trial and error. Herein, we present a data-driven framework that recommends a stationary phase or separation mode, solvent, and solvent ratio to support thin-layer chromatography (TLC) screening and column chromatography (CC) purification. Using purification records from publications and laboratory notebooks, we developed models to predict TLC and CC conditions. Models using product structures alone or in combination with reactant and agent information were compared across prediction tasks and data sources. Experimental evaluation of 11 previously unreported compounds demonstrated that ranked recommendations could guide TLC screening and the selection of CC purification conditions. Additionally, a web application was developed to provide users with flexible access to the prediction models. The proposed framework supports the selection of practical purification conditions and provides a foundation for integrating purification planning into future autonomous experimental workflows.
items.authors: Yuki Murakami, Nobuo Cho, Kosei Egami, Hiroto Yamazaki, Shoichi Ishida, Aoi Hirano

items.title: Reductive Deoxygenation of Benzylic Alcohols by Low-Valent Titanium Alkoxides
items.abstract: 2 ABSTRACT: Reductive deoxygenation of benzylic alcohols is a valuable transformation that yields alkylated aromatic compounds. Even though hydroxyl group in these substrates is considered as activated, general mild methods for their reduction remain elusive. While many existing protocols require acidic reagents or additives detrimental for functional groups, milder alternatives are efficient only with 1° benzylic alcohols and diarylmethanols. Here we report that low-valent titanium alkoxides promote deoxygenation of 1°, 2° and 3° benzylic alcohols under basic conditions compatible with acetal, alkene, ester, amide, nitrile, aryl halides and benzyloxy groups. The low-valent titanium reagents were generated in situ by the reduction of Ti(OiPr)4 either with a dihydrobenzimidazol derivative under irradiation with blue light or with pieces of sodium metal. Mechanistic studies revealed that the deoxygenation step is promoted by Ti(III) alkoxides, while OH-groups of the substrate serve as a source of H-atoms.
items.authors: Dziyana Atroshchanka, Yahor Rusakovich, Antanina Shtytsko, Mark Senkevich, Gleb Kakouka, Vitaly Syakhovich

items.title: Single-Polynucleotide Encapsulation in Lipid Nanoparticles via Single-Step Assembly at Physiological pH
items.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading nonviral platform for polynucleotide delivery, but structural heterogeneity and poorly controlled loading states limit quantitative structure–function analysis and rational formulation design. Standard protocols use rapid mixing under acidic conditions followed by buffer exchange, reflecting the assumption that ionizable lipid protonation is required for nucleic acid complexation. Here, we show that lipid–polynucleotide nanoparticles can instead be assembled directly at near-physiological pH through a single rapid micromixing step. Under near-stoichiometric lipid-to-polynucleotide conditions, rapid solvent exchange yields a homogeneous nanoparticle population without acidic formulation or post-assembly pH adjustment. Small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering (SAXS and SANS), together with cryogenic transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM), reveal a common core–multishell architecture consistent with encapsulation of one polynucleotide strand per particle. In situ SAXS shows that the final structure is established within submillisecond timescales during solvent exchange, indicating rapid cooperative coassembly rather than postmixing restructuring. Systematic variation of mixing conditions, stoichiometry, PEGylated lipid content, ionic strength, and pH demonstrates that this structural regime is selected by the assembly pathway rather than composition alone. The nanoparticles remain structurally stable over extended periods and retain intracellular delivery activity, while providing a constrained system for probing formulation-dependent effects. These results establish physiological-pH assembly as a route to pathway-selected single-polynucleotide nanoparticles and identify loading state as a design variable alongside composition, size, and surface chemistry. More broadly, they highlight assembly history as a determinant of nanoparticle structure and pathway-directed assembly as a strategy for controlling soft nanomaterial heterogeneity at its origin rather than after formation.
items.authors: Maxime Guichonnet, Johanna Mirande-Ney, Anne-Sophie Kirstetter, Martine Meireles, Sébastien Teychené, Kevin Roger

items.title: Cu(II) complexes based on morpholine-substituted thiosemicarbazones show reduced toxicity in normal cells
items.abstract: Three novel Cu(II) complexes with 3,4-dimethoxybenzylidene-substituted thiosemicarbazones were synthesized and evaluated for anticancer, antibacterial, and antioxidant activities. Our recent structure-activity relationship studies showed that Cu(II) complexes containing 3,4-dimethoxybenzylidene-substituted ligands can display potent anticancer activity, reaching single-digit IC 50 values, which prompted further investigation of this structural motif. The complexes examined here showed moderate antibacterial activity and distinct antioxidant profiles in the ABTS, DPPH, and ORAC-FL assays. Among them, the morpholine-containing complex Cu(dm-TSC-morph) 2 showed the most favorable anticancer selectivity, retaining low-micromolar activity against SK-MEL-28 and A-375 melanoma cells (IC 50 = 6.58 ± 0.71 and 9.20 ± 1.52 μM, respectively) while exhibiting lower toxicity toward BJ, HUVEC, and HEK-293 cells, with selectivity indices up to 4.88. Studies of mechanism of action revealed that Cu(dm-TSC-morph) 2 induced intracellular oxidative stress in melanoma cells. These findings identify the morpholine-containing derivative as the most promising compound in the analyzed series and support further development of selective Cu(II) thiosemicarbazone complexes.
items.authors: Bartłomiej Rogalewicz, Marcin Świątkowski, Magdalena Iwan, Joanna Kubik, Agnieszka Korga-Plewko, Monika Pitucha

items.title: The assembled catalytic triad of Ideonella sakaiensis PETase is metastable in apo molecular dynamics simulations across multiple control conditions
items.abstract: Active-site geometry is routinely reported from molecular dynamics of engineered variants of Ideonella sakaiensis PETase (IsPETase) as evidence that a design preserves catalytic capability. We simulated wild-type IsPETase and six length-matched linker fusion constructs, four replicates each, for 350 ns at 343 K under a preregistered analysis plan. Twenty-six of 28 trajectories began with the Ser133 OG to His210 NE2 distance inside the competent range, below 0.35 nm, and two began marginally above it. All 28 ended outside that range without recovery. The median time to crossing, from the onset of free dynamics, was 4.06 ns, with a range spanning more than four orders of magnitude. Triad loss was not generally accompanied by global destabilisation. The loss persisted when the system was built from the crystal structure rather than a predicted model, when both native disulfide bonds were present, and at 300 K. Changing the catalytic histidine protonation state did not restore persistent catalytic geometry. A post hoc control under a second protein and water parameter set also left the competent range in all four replicates, but reached separations of 0.48 to 0.90 nm rather than the 1.9 to 2.1 nm seen under CHARMM36m. Because the endpoint failed in the wild-type control, the intended comparison of linker family and length could not be completed. Active-site distances from apo IsPETase simulations should not be interpreted as evidence of catalytic competence without a wild-type control and replicate sampling.
items.authors: Amarechi Okorafor, Aryan Atri, Ayushmaan Singh

items.title: TiO2 as active site and protective layer on Sn doped spinel cobalt oxide for acidic OER
items.abstract: Green hydrogen is expected to play a major role in the decarbonisation of hard-to-electrify sectors such as shipping, aviation, steel, and fertiliser. Cost effective acidic water electrolysis to produce green hydrogen requires active, stable non-noble metal oxide catalysts, however non-noble metal oxides tend to be unstable at oxidative potentials in acidic media. In this work we show that Sn doped Co 3 O 4 exhibits improved activity, while using an ultrathin TiO 2 overlayer improves stability greatly without hindering activity. The maximal activity, at 5% Sn content, was comparable to the state-of-the-art for non-noble PEM anode catalysts, while the maximal stabilising effect produced by the overlayer was more than eightfold.
items.authors: András Kozák, Georgios K. Stavroglou, Julie B. Koefoed, Albin Mustafi, Gustav Stausbøll Hedemark, Charalampos Lampadaris

items.title: Developing An Entirely Mechanochemical Synthesis of Cram’s Cavitands and Carcerands
items.abstract: We report the development of an entirely mechanochemical synthesis of a set of iconic and complex supramolecular targets, Cram’s carcerands and cavitands, using a sequence of mechanochemical, liquid-assisted steps. By demonstrating how mechanochemical methods can be adapted to each segment of carcerand synthesis, this work highlights the benefits and opportunities mechanochemistry offers for simpler, high-yielding synthesis of complex targets. This work exploits grinding based on dual asymmetric centrifugal motion, which provides high autogenous frictional heating to drive chemical reactivity and, in some cases, permits thick and resinous reaction systems to mix without solidifying. The analogous media-free approach provided efficient mixing when heating was not required. Using these methods, we show that a set of phenolic cavitands, which are crucial precursors to a wide set of carcerands and hemicarcerands, can be synthesized rapidly, in high yields, using minimal organic solvent, and with improved operational simplicity, and that the final capsule-like carcerands can also be assembled mechanochemically, despite the common expectation that effectiveness of such supramolecular transformations requires high dilutions.
items.authors: Joseph M. Marrett, Hatem M. Titi, Tomislav Friscic

items.title: Directional Control of Droplet Motion via Geometric Gating
items.abstract: We explore new methods for inducing the movement of water droplets on elastomeric substrates, such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Our approach builds upon the well-known phenomenon that water droplets move easily across these substrates when swelled with silicone oil. While designing shallow open channels and traps on a PDMS film offers a simple way to control a droplet's trajectory by tilting the substrate in two orthogonal directions, this method is poorly suited for manipulating multiple droplets simultaneously. To address this limitation, we introduce two new methods. The first method utilizes a piano-concave PDMS platform with a radius of curvature significantly larger than the size of the droplet and its translation distance. When the system's configuration is altered, this curved substrate consistently guides the droplet along a curved geodesic. The second method incorporates diode-like gates on the PDMS. These gates are created on either flat or piano-concave PDMS films by embedding thin, rigid plates into the elastomer prior to crosslinking, followed by swelling in silicone oil. This process generates sigmoidal steps that restrict droplet motion to a single direction. Finally, we demonstrate how combining these two strategies enables various forms of directed motion for both single and multiple droplets.
items.authors: Manoj K. Chaudhury, Vanessa Elias, Michelle Fruge

items.title: Light-Driven Dissolution of Ultrasmall Maghemite Nanoparticles: The Role of Ligand and Photon Energy
items.abstract: Light-controlled conversion of iron oxide nanoparticles into redox-active soluble iron offers a route toward externally triggered, image-guided ferroptosis strategies, but the physicochemical factors governing this process remain poorly understood. Here, visible-light-driven dissolution of ultrasmall citrate-stabilized maghemite nanoparticles (3.4 ± 0.8 nm) is shown to arise from a competition between iron release and nanoparticle aggregation. The process involves iron oxide reduction, ferrous iron release, citrate detachment and oxidation, and subsequent nanoparticle aggregation. The effects of citric acid and photon energy are systematically examined, revealing their key roles in regulating dissolution and aggregation. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and spatially resolved diffuse reflectance are used to monitor these changes in biologically relevant environments, including tissue-mimicking phantoms. MRI contrast evolves predictably with irradiation time, supporting the use of these particles as responsive imaging probes. In glioblastoma cells, green-light irradiation of internalized maghemite nanoparticles induces mitochondrial cytochrome oxidation. Cell-viability assays further reveal a non-monotonic concentration dependence under blue and green light, with lower nanoparticle concentrations producing stronger cytotoxic effects. These results establish a light-controlled, ligandassisted dissolution/aggregation strategy in which photon energy and ligand availability govern iron release, colloidal stability, imaging response, and light-induced cellular toxicity.
items.authors: Dmitrii Tsiurko, Ekaterina Moiseeva, Sergei German, Daria Terentyeva, Arsen Zotov, Alina Platonova

items.title: Photoresponsive Dynamics in HABI-Carbamate-Silsesquioxane Hybrid Polymer Networks with Tunable Thermomechanical Properties and Shape-Memory Behaviors
items.abstract: Photoresponsive polymer networks that reversibly modulate their mechanical properties under light irradiation are promising materials for advanced actuators and shape-memory systems. Herein, we report the synthesis of a new family of hexaarylbiimidazole (HABI)-carbamate-siloxane hybrid polymer networks containing methyl, phenyl, vinyl, acrylate, methacrylate, and isooctyl organotrialkoxysilane structures. The polymers were prepared through simultaneous urethane formation and siloxane condensation. We characterized all synthesized compounds by ATR-FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, solid-state 13C NMR, 29Si NMR, LC-HRMS, UV−Vis spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and dynamic mechanical analysis. Chemical characterization confirmed successful incorporation of HABI moieties, formation of carbamate linkages, and cross-linked siloxane networks. The organotrialkoxysilane substituents significantly influenced the thermal and mechanical properties of the polymer networks. Methacrylate- and acrylate-containing polymers showed the highest thermal stability (Td5% = 237 °C and 207 °C, respectively), while ceramic yields increased from 7% for the pristine network to 15%- 19% for the modified systems. Dynamic mechanical analysis revealed pronounced, reversible light-induced changes in storage and loss moduli arising from reversible HABI C−N bond cleavage and recombination, with the vinyl-containing polymer exhibiting the largest storage modulus variation (8 × 103 MPa). Several polymers also demonstrated reproducible light-assisted shape-memory behavior, with the acrylate-, methacrylate-, methyl-, and isooctyl-containing systems showing the most distinct responses. These HABI-carbamate-siloxane hybrid networks provide a versatile platform for developing mechanically tunable, photoresponsive materials for smart polymer and shape-memory applications.
items.authors: Mehdi Erfani Jazi, Ethan T. Chandler, Fatemeh Aghabozorgi, Buddhima Rupasinghe, Joseph C. Furgal

items.title: Integrating Ion Mobility–Resolved Tandem Mass Spectrometry and Microcrystal Electron Diffraction for Structural Elucidation
items.authors: Aleyna Lumsden, Amalia-Sofia Piticari, Amar Rai, Artemy Novokhrost, Timea Pálmai-Pallag, Yufeng Li

items.title: Isolation and bonding analysis of copper(I)-xenon complex stabilized by weakly coordinating alkoxyaluminate anion.
items.abstract: The first crystalline Cu(I)-Xe complex, Xe-Cu[Al(OR F ) 4 ], 1 , (R F = C(CF 3 ) 3 ), forms as a salt of the weakly coordinating perfluorinated alkoxyaluminate upon ligand exchange between elemental xenon and Cu(I)-N 2 complex, Cu(N 2 )[Al(OR F ) 4 ]. Despite the lack of relativistic character of the copper ion, 1 is obtained under ambient Xe pressure and at room temperature. The crystal structure reveals that it is a molecular compound where xenon is a terminal ligand to copper with steric factors causing a Cu-Xe bond elongation in comparison with known gas-phase Xe-Cu(I) species. Extensive computational analysis facilitates the interpretation of spectral properties and gives insight into the nature of the bond between Xe and Cu[Al(OR F ) 4 ]. EDA-NOCV and NPA indicate that electrostatic forces between Xe and Cu[Al(OR F ) 4 ] have the largest share of its energy, though orbital interactions between the 5p orbital of Xe and the hybridized 4s/3d orbital of Cu as well as dispersive forces are also significant. Though the Xe-Cu[Al(OR F ) 4 ] bond is fairly weak in comparison with Au + -Xe in the known [Xe-AuAsF 3 ] complex, the isolation of 1 is possible thanks to the use of the weakly coordinating anion and solvent, which are worse ligands to copper than Xe atom.
items.authors: Przemysław J. Malinowski, Vadim Zhuravlev

items.title: Spatially programmed MOF-coated microchannels for capillary-driven microvolume analysis
items.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer chemically and geometrically programmable pore environments that have been exploited as coatings for capillary- and fiber-based microextraction. However, most formats still rely on discrete adsorbent handling or external fluid actuation, poorly suited to the microliter sample volumes typical of biological specimens. Here we report glass microcapillaries bearing a spatially programmed, nanometer-thick MOF film that simultaneously drives fluid uptake by capillary action and performs localized analyte enrichment within a single, self-contained channel. Retaining the adsorbent as a conformal film rather than a particulate phase removes the need for separate adsorbent handling. It also concentrates chemical functionality at the fluid-contacting surface, enabling efficient enrichment from a few microliters without external pumps. We demonstrate this approach by enriching and quantifying the inflammation-associated metabolites kynurenine and quinolinic acid from microliter volumes of mouse blood serum, achieving clear discrimination between inflammatory and control conditions. These MOF-coated microcapillaries offer an integrated route to low-volume biofluid analysis in settings where sample availability and external fluid handling are limiting.
items.authors: Tilottoma Baisakhi, Archana Yadav, Rajarshi Ghosh, Shruthi Rajaram, Aneesh Tazhe Veetil, Ritesh Haldar

items.title: DNA binders based on the integration of duocarmycins into minor groove-targeting polyamides have potent and selective anti-trypansosomal activity
items.abstract: Duocarmycins are attractive DNA alkylating agents due to their high potency; however, increasing their selectivity has always been a challenge. Here, we describe the integration of the duocarmycin subunits DSA and CI into minor groove-targeting polyamides, compounds that can ‘read’ DNA sequences. The synthesis of a CI analogue suitably substituted for solid phase synthesis using Fmoc-chemistry is described. The synthesis of the hybrid compounds is achieved using solid phase methods on chloro-trityl resin. The resulting hybrids display sequence-selective DNA alkylation, depending on the enantiomer and position of the duocarmycin unit as might be expected, except for the compounds with a central DSA alkylation subunit, which act more similarly to reversed analogues. The CI hybrids with a central unit are relatively unreactive with DNA and modelling studies suggest that the CI subunit is sub-optimally located for alkylation in these structures. Investigations against the parasite T. brucei, responsible for African trypanomiasis, highlight compounds with nanomolar potency and high selectivity (SI 300), showing that the integration of duocarmycins into the backbone of polyamides has promise for developing gene-targeting small molecule anti-parasitic agents.
items.authors: Zoë R. Goddard, Bethany R. Hood, Michael Brazzill, Deanne Hayward, Dietmar Steverding, Victoria Kamperi

items.title: A robust multiwell workflow for quantitative and nontargeted chemical exposomics at cohort scale
items.abstract: Chemical exposomics enables comprehensive profiling of environmental substances and their metabolic perturbations, providing new opportunities to uncover environmental drivers of disease. To realize its full potential in human exposome initiatives, more reproducible high-throughput workflows are needed that combine sensitive quantitative targeted analysis with nontargeted molecular discovery in small serum volumes. We describe a 96-well phospholipid depletion workflow using 100 µL of serum and liquid chromatography – high-resolution mass spectrometry to quantify 247 priority pollutants, drugs and metabolites while confidently annotating hundreds of additional exogenous and endogenous molecules. In contrast to evaporation-to-dryness workflows, adding a small volume of dimethyl sulfoxide retained more analytes and improved recovery (99% median target recovery), with negligible effect on sensitivity (0.5 ng/mL median method limit of quantification), resulting in robust within-laboratory reproducibility across four operators over 1.5 years (18% median relative standard deviation). Application to 718 human serum samples confirmed scalability while maintaining reproducible quantitation and molecular discovery (761 annotated substances) at the cohort scale.
items.authors: Solveig Thiele, Bénilde Bonnefille, Sophia Harlid, Stefano Papazian, Jonathan W. Martin

items.title: Features of the Gibbs Equation (∆G = ∆H - T∆S) Applied to Solvation, Vaporization, and Complexation Thermodynamics
items.abstract: The Gibbs equation (∆ G = ∆ H – T ∆ S ) remains a cornerstone of chemical thermodynamics. Yet the scope and origins of the widely observed correlations between the enthalpies (∆ H ) and entropies (∆ S ), or Gibbs energies (∆ G ) and enthalpies, have long been debated. This study systematically analyzes over 4,500 experimental thermodynamic values at 298.15 K to establish quantitative principles governing the ∆ G vs. ∆ H relationship across solvation, vaporization, and molecular complexation processes. By classifying systems according to hydrogen-bonding capabilities, we demonstrate that non-associated solute–solvent pairs universally follow a baseline linear correlation (the Barclay–Butler line). Systematic deviations from this baseline are quantitatively attributed to distinct physical contributions: conformational flexibility in long-chain aliphatics (hindered internal rotation), a constant entropic penalty per directional hydrogen bond, and predominantly entropic solvophobic effects in associated solvents. Through thermodynamic transformations, these solvation/vaporization rules are extended to yield a universal linear ∆ G –∆ H relationship with an invariant slope of 0.660 for both solution- and gas-phase molecular complexation, encompassing hydrogen bonding, charge transfer, and dispersion interactions. The framework is successfully applied to α -cyclodextrin host–guest systems, where it can be used as a diagnostic tool for detecting anomalous or non-inclusion binding modes and for deeper analysis of the complexation mechanism. Ultimately, this work transforms the Gibbs equation into a predictive instrument, enabling accurate estimation of enthalpies from single-temperature Gibbs energy measurements and providing a unified, mechanism-independent foundation for analyzing intermolecular interactions in systems of varying complexity.
items.authors: Boris N. Solomonov, Mikhail I. Yagofarov

items.title: Growth and crystallization of solution-processed TIPSpentacene on ultra-thin ferroelectric HZO gate dielectrics
items.abstract: The solution processed organic thin film growth on the ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2(HZO) thin films was investigated using the most commonly used TIPS-pentacene toward memory device applications. The molecular orientations, surface morphologies, and crystallinity of TIPS pentacene deposited on HZO were comparable to those of fabricated thin films on SiO2. In particular, 2D-GIXD results showed that TIPS-pentacene on HZO crystallized by annealing at 150°C exhibited higher crystallinity and molecular orientation than that on SiO2. Preliminary electrical measurements revealed that TIPS‑pentacene/HZO stacks exhibited strong channel conduction with negligible gate modulation, indicating that interfacial electronic states at the HZO surface dominate charge transport.
items.authors: Towa Nakazawa, Daiji Kitamura, Ryoga Takemoto, Kazuto Koike, Shingo Maruyama, Shunsuke Yamamoto

items.title: Phase-Controlled Efficient Nitrate-to-Dinitrogen Electroreduction on an α-Co/NC@CNT Electrified Membrane Platform
items.abstract: Selective electrochemical conversion of nitrate (NO 3 - ) to dinitrogen (N 2 ) is attractive for nitrate remediation but remains challenging because competing hydrogenation pathways often yield reduced nitrogen products. Here, we develop a self-supported flexible electrified membrane (α-Co/NC@CNTFEM) by integrating phase-defined hexagonal close-packed (HCP) α-Co/nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) into a conductive carbon nanotube (CNT) framework. The resulting membrane combines a uniformly integrated catalytic phase with a thin, interconnected porous architecture suitable for flow-through electrochemical operation. At an initial nitrate concentration of 10 mg L -1 , α-Co/NC@CNT-FEM achieves 96.5% nitrate conversion, 81.5% N 2 Faradaic efficiency, and 97.9% N 2 selectivity, exceeding the corresponding mixed-phase Co NP /NC@CNT-FEM and bare CNT-FEM. The enhanced N 2 selectivity is associated with the coupled effects of the phase-defined α-Co, N-doped carbon matrix, and flow-through CNT microenvironment, which may favor N–N coupling while suppressing excessive hydrogenation. Moreover, our results also reveal that stable nitrate removal on this platform is maintained over 10 consecutive cycles. This work demonstrates crystal-phase engineering coupled with electrified membrane design as a materials strategy for selective nitrate-to-N 2 conversion.
items.authors: Jiantao Xu, Ruxin Han, Jifa Zhang, Dawei Li, Feihu Li

items.title: Analytic Nuclear Gradients and Derivative Couplings for SA-QED-CASSCF
items.abstract: Exploring the potential energy surfaces of molecules in optical cavities requires analytical derivatives. We present analytical nuclear gradients and nonadiabatic derivative couplings for state-averaged quantum-electrodynamics complete-active-space self-consistent field theory (SA-QED-CASSCF) forthe coherent-state Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian, including the coupledperturbed response of the QED-Hartree–Fock reference and the photon contribution to the coupling that arises because the coherent-state displacement depends on the geometry. The derivatives agree with finite differences to within 10−6 atomic units (5×10−6 for the state of smallest weight in an unequal average) for equal, unequal and zero-weight state averaging, and with independent codes without the cavity. With them we locate a polariton-induced conical intersection in LiH, where the cavity makes the molecular orientation a second coordinate and a reflection combined with photon parity makes the crossing symmetry-allowed. In ethylene, the S0/S1 conical intersection persists under coupling and keeps its twisted–pyramidalized geometry, and it becomes more accessible from the Franck–Condon point, because the dipole self-energy raises the diffuse π → 3s state more than the crossing pair. Capturing the partial return of this penalty through the bilinear coupling requires the polarization-axis partner orbital in the active space, a rule for polaritonic CASSCF in general.
items.authors: Nam Vu, Jonathan J. Foley

items.title: N-aminated N-heterocycle based hydrazones as widely tunable photoswitches
items.abstract: Photoswitches based on E/Z isomerism around a C=N bond have found wide-reaching applications in materials science and biology. Herein, we report a new class of hydrazone photoswitch based on aminated nitrogen heterocycles, the N-aminated N-heterocyclic hydrazones (NaNs). These photoswitches can be synthesised in a single step, achieve near quantitative photoswitching, offer visible light (470 nm) response, have thermal half-lives of up to 958 hours at room temperature and quantum yields of up to 70%. We have investigated the impact of different structural features on switch properties by studying a library of 30 derivatives with varied N-amino N-heterocyclic components and varied aldehyde components. These have been extensively studied in the solution and solid state, towards understanding structure-activity relationships for rational NaN photoswitch design. The stability of the metastable state facilitated the growth of the Z-isomer crystals for an anthracene derived NaN, and we observed both E/Z isomerisation and dimerisation of the anthracene, depending on irradiation duration. Furthermore, we demonstrate a member of the library undergoes E→Z photoisomerisation in the solid state, displaying single crystal to single crystal switching. We anticipate that the simple synthesis of these compounds, combined with their tuneable properties, will ensure that they find widespread application across numerous fields.
items.authors: Alex Buchanan, Rebecca Kerridge, Jorn Steen, Alexander M. Wilmshurst, Daniel Rainer, Finlay Williams

items.title: Mousanes: Convergent Synthesis and Diversification of Serially Spiro-Fused Cyclobutanes
items.abstract: Connecting cyclobutanes through successive spiro junctions offers a way to restrict the relative positions and orientations of functional groups along a saturated framework. Here we describe a convergent synthesis of mousanes, dispirodecane scaffolds comprising three cyclobutanes. A functionalized methylenecyclobutene is prepared on decagram scale by elimination of an iodo-bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanederived precursor. This 1,3-diene undergoes regioselective, triplet-sensitized [2+2] homodimerization to construct the central cyclobutane and both spiro junctions. Hydrolysis and stereoconvergent hydrogenation provide a bifunctional mousane on multigram scale, from which amino acid, diamine, diol and differentially functionalized derivatives are prepared. Calculations suggest that regioselectivity is established during the initial C–C bond-forming step and show that mousane stereochemistry controls terminal geometry. The exo,exo framework has dimensions comparable to short hydrocarbon linkers but displays a narrower calculated range of terminal-vector orientations. We illustrate the use of these building blocks through incorporation into drug analogues and a BRD4-targeting heterobifunctional ligand directed degrader.
items.authors: Manivel Pitchai, Sankar Ulaganathan, Nanjundaswamy K.C., Mohammad Javeed, Pavan Srinivas, Sourav Roy

items.title: Super-Reaction Enhancement of Polariton-Mediated Electron Transfer
items.abstract: We investigate the enhancement of polariton-mediated electron transfer (PMET) using a general super-reaction mechanism where multiple donor sites locally couple to individual acceptors. We demonstrate that this enhancement extends to the collective light-matter coupling regime with a large number of acceptors and cavity-coupled donors. We use analytic rate theory and quantum dynamics simulations to show that the local super-reaction mechanism serves as an additional enhancement to the delocalized driving force enhancement of PMET. We further incorporate bath-induced disorder in the donors to investigate precisely how collective light-matter coupling protects the coherent super-reaction enhancement against disorder. The results show that ET from bright polariton states, that are separated enough from the dark state manifold, is enhanced by the super-reaction mechanism in any ET regime, offering another avenue to realize cavity modification of photochemistry.
items.authors: Eric R. Koessler, Todd D. Krauss, Pengfei Huo

items.title: Hydrogen-Assisted Reduction of Metal Oxides: Reaction Mechanisms, Process Optimization, and AI/ML-Enabled Pathways for Sustainable Materials Processing
items.abstract: Hydrogen reduction of metal oxides has been identified as a promising approach for producing some engineering (metallic) materials, both through primary production and the reprocessing of waste materials. Such an approach offers a viable promise for the production of value-added materials in a sustainable manner. Unlike in other reduction processes, where obnoxious gases get 2 released as byproducts, hydrogen reduction, on the other hand, generate water vapor as the clean principal byproduct. Such an approach renders the overall mcheaping process inexpensive because of the use of metal oxides as the cheap feedstocks. However, the manufacturing process offers several challenges, upscaling being one of the major ones. In the present review, an attempt has been made to assess the overall reduction process in an integrated manner, which relates thermodynamic principles, reduction mechanisms, reactor-scale phenomena, and specific application requirements. The principles of thermodynamic constraints related to oxide reducibility are described in relation to the role of reduction temperature, gas compositions, and the gas-solid reaction mechanisms to determine rate-controlling processes, diffusion coefficients, and the role of catalysis for the production of metallic materials by primary manufacturing processes and environmental remediation. There is also the consideration of an enabling role of automation, modeling, and digital twin technologies. The manuscript describes practiced hydrogen reduction processes to produce some of the specific metals, such as iron, nickel, cobalt, and refractory metals, but also the need to improve hydrogen access, efficiency, scalability, and ensure catalyst longevity. Enhanced research in hydrogen, renewable power coupling, AI-assisted process control and reactor design are some of the aspects that have been observed to be the major enablers. The manuscript not only describes the status and future projections but also provides a roadmap for improving the status quo.
items.authors: Kunal Mondal, Rigoberto C. Advincula, Prabhat K. Tripathy, Nagaraj P. Shetti

items.title: When Philicity Fails: Mechanistic Control of Ambiphilic Metal–Superoxo Reactivity
items.abstract: A fundamental challenge in oxygen activation chemistry is understanding the factors that govern the switch between electrophilic and nucleophilic reactivity in metal–superoxo intermediates. Notably, only four ambiphilic metal–superoxo systems have been reported to date, yet the origins of their ambiphilic behavior remain poorly understood, limiting the rational design of catalysts with predictable and tunable reactivity. Here, we systematically investigate these four reported complexes, [(L 1 ) •+ Co II –O2 •⁻ ] – ( 1b ) (where L1 = (N • ( o -PhNC(O) i Pr) 2 ) 2– ) , [(L 2 )Mn III –O 2 •– ] ( 2b ) (where L 2 = BDP Br P = 2,6-bis((2-( S )-di(4-bromo)phenylhydroxylmethyl-1-pyrrolidinyl)methyl)pyridine) 2– ), [(L 3 )Fe III (O 2 •⁻ )] 2− ( 3b ) (where L 3 = TAML = Tetra Amido Macrocyclic Ligand) 4- and [(L 4 )Co III –O 2 •⁻ ] ( 4b ) (where L 4 = BDPP = 2,6-bis((2-(S)diphenylhydroxylmethyl-1-pyrrolidinyl)methyl)pyridine) 2– ) , using density functional theory to elucidate their O 2 activation and reactivity toward electrophilic and nucleophilic substrates. O 2 activation preferentially proceeds through inner-sphere pathways, in which electron transfer and M–O 2 bond formation occurs concomitantly, with ligand-to-O 2 electron transfer for 1a and metal-to-O 2 electron transfer for 2a – 4a . For PPA deformylation, coordinatively saturated complex 2b favor α-hydrogen atom abstraction, whereas the open, four-coordinate 1b preferentially undergoes nucleophilic addition. In contrast, oxygen-atom-transfer reactivity toward triphenylphosphine does not follow electrophilicity alone: despite the higher intrinsic electrophilicity of [(L 5 )Cu II –O 2 •– ] + (L 5 =TMPA = tris(2-pyridyl methyl)amine); ( 5b ), 1b exhibits a lower activation barrier (68.4 vs 81.4 kJ/mol) owing to stronger orbital interactions and reduced deformation requirements. Collectively, these results establish that metal–superoxo reactivity is governed by the interplay of coordination environment, philicity, orbital interactions, steric effects, and deformation energy. These insights provide a framework for rational catalyst design in which reactivity can be tuned by optimizing the complete electronic and structural reaction landscape rather than maximizing philicity alone.
items.authors: Chandrasekhar Nettem, Abitha Periyasamy, Manjeet Kumar, Gopalan Rajaraman

items.title: Consecutive hydrodefluorination for the regioselective synthesis of partially fluorinated arenes
items.abstract: Fluorinated arenes are critically important motifs in drug discovery, often exhibiting superior bioactivity compared to their non-fluorinated counterparts. While advances in fluorination methods have improved access to monofluoroarenes, the synthesis of di- and trifluoroarenes remains challenging. Here, we present a powerful method for access to partially fluorinated arenes via consecutive hydrodefluorination of perfluoroarenes, executed in one ‘pot’. This method utilises hydridosilicates as the reducing species, which are formed in situ by the combination of phenylsilane and cesium carbonate in dimethylsulfoxide. These conditions avoid precious metal catalysts and exotic reagents, exhibiting exceptional regioselectivity and control over the degree of defluorination. Through an in-depth mechanistic study, we found that hydridosilicates can perform hydrodefluorination by two distinct mechanisms, one thermal and one photochemical. These mechanisms are complementary in substrate scope—together, they enable a method with notable generality.
items.authors: Yanxian Tan, Howard Toh, Chieh-Yu Chang, Phillip S. Grant

items.title: Treatise on Present Practice and Perspectives of MDGC
items.abstract: The state of affairs of multidimensional gas chromatography (MDGC) at present is no more than an implementation of a two-dimensional form (2D-GC) reducing the domain to the setup known as GCxGC. Introduced in 1991 with great expectation, however, GCxGC still happen to fall short of realizing the anticipated capabilities despite continuous efforts made over the elapsed 35 years. This got quantitative formulation in regard of separation performance as early as 2008, proving that it failed to be competitive with a well-governed 1D-GC. The present paper highlights further limitations of GCxGC: inadequate operation burdened with shortcomings are presented via examples taken from GCxGC literature; crowning the list with the inability to meet fundamental requirement that if a compound can be analyzed by 1D-GC it must remain analyzable by MDGC. The repertoire of the intertwining issues, each of which unavoidably rigs or even hamstrings the others, highlights that GCxGC has a built-in self-limiting feature. Attempts to overcome confinements via loosening the binding conditions turned GCxGC back to the form it emerged from decades ago, yet without getting rid of the hampering curbs. The unfavorable overall picture forces to consider viabilities of other concepts, with focus on avoiding errors and pitfalls of GCxGC while fulfilling basic requirements of MDGC. In our view, there are two alternatives. One is ZGC, principle of which was introduced in 1989, requirements and potential of which are presented here in more detail; the other is a concept called Quantum-GC, which is presented as an introductory approach.
items.authors: Endre Fuggerth

items.title: Photocatalytic performance of silver clusters on anatase TiO2 for bisphenol A degradation in water under solar light
items.abstract: The increasing occurrence of bisphenol A (BPA) in water sources raises significant environmental and health concerns, demanding efficient and sustainable remediation strategies. In this work, we investigate the photocatalytic degradation of BPA using silver metal clusters (Ag5) supported on anatase TiO2 under simulated solar irradiation. The deposition of Ag5 clusters significantly enhances visible-light absorption, promotes charge separation and improves photocatalytic performance, achieving an apparent rate constant (kobs) of 0.0142 min-1, corresponding to a ~43% improvement compared to bare TiO2. In addition, the Ag5@TiO2 catalyst exhibits higher photocatalytic activity, demonstrating the beneficial effect of Ag5 clusters incorporation. HPLC-MS analysis enabled the identification of intermediate degradation products. Compared to literature reports on modified TiO2-based photocatalysts, the present system demonstrates competitive performance even at significantly lower catalyst loadings. These results highlight the potential of Ag5@TiO2 photocatalysts as highly efficient alternatives for removing endocrine-disrupting compounds from water.
items.authors: María Moreno-Pérez, José Manuel Ageitos, Iria R. Arias, José Manuel Blanco Trillo, M. Arturo López-Quintela, Carlos Vázquez-Vázquez

items.title: A Stereochemical Blueprint for Thermoresponsive Polymers
items.abstract: Predicting polymer structure-property relationships is challenging due to the vast chemical expanse of polymer design space and the limited availability of high-quality datasets that effectively span the design space. Here, we present a physics-informed framework that integrates high-throughput molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with machine learning to predict the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) of stereochemically diverse poly(Nisopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) systems using 5632 MD simulation trajectories, corresponding to a cumulative simulation time of 2816 µs. We use validated MD simulations to generate descriptors that capture local hydration and conformational environments, enabling the extraction of molecular features directly linked to thermoresponsive behaviour. The resulting model accurately reproduces subtle experimentally observed LCST variations arising from changes in tacticity, demonstrating that sequence derived features and simulation-derived hydration descriptors encode the molecular information required to resolve compositiondependent phase behaviour. Beyond LCST prediction, the framework provides mechanistic insight into the molecular origins of thermoresponsive behaviour of PNIPAM, revealing that meso and racemic dyads undergo distinct backbone rotational mediated collapse pathways, with meso dyads requiring backbone rotation through partially hydrated intermediates, whereas racemic dyads collapse within a fixed backbone rotational conformation through closure of the isopropyl-isopropyl distance. These findings establish a transferable simulation-machinelearning strategy for linking polymer structural information to macroscopic properties and accelerating the discovery of functional polymer materials.
items.authors: Rangika Munaweera, Martin Stroet, Megan L. O'Mara

items.title: Lookahead Bayesian Optimisation for Molecular Growth in Self-Driving Laboratories
items.abstract: Self-driving laboratories can autonomously execute iterative design-make-test-analyse cycles, but molecular optimisation presents a distinctive challenge: selecting which compound to elaborate determines not only the next experiment, but also the chemical space accessible in subsequent rounds. Conventional molecular Bayesian optimisation typically evaluates compounds without considering how their selection changes what can subsequently be synthesised. Here, we introduce Lookahead Bayesian Optimisation (LABO), which instead values candidate molecules according to the predicted value of the synthetically accessible chemical space they unlock, enabling optimisation to account for future experimental opportunities. We evaluate LABO in simulated five-round molecular optimisation campaigns across 30 lead-like starting compounds and five kinase targets. LABO outperformed established molecular optimisation strategies from the literature across all 30 optimisation landscapes, as well as random, greedy and Bayesian optimisation controls. LABO was shown to improve ligand-lipophilicity efficiency by 1.25 units over random selection, equivalent to approximately 18-fold greater potency at equal lipophilicity, and by 0.34 units (2.2-fold) over greedy elaboration. These results demonstrate a general principle for autonomous molecular optimisation: under synthetic constraints, the value of a molecule depends not only on its predicted properties, but on the future experiments that selecting it makes possible. By explicitly incorporating this future experimental value into molecular selection, LABO provides a framework for planning successive rounds of molecular growth in self-driving laboratories.
items.authors: Connor J. Taylor

items.title: Nucleus-Independent Chemical Shifts in disordered nanoporous carbons are governed by the long-range magnetic response of the carbon framework
items.abstract: Nanoporous carbons are widely used in energy storage, gas storage, and separation technologies due to their high surface area, porosity, and electrical conductivity. Understanding atomic-scale structure is critical for interpreting performance, yet disorder greatly complicates characterization. NMR chemical shifts of adsorbed molecules have emerged as a probe of structural disorder, but how nucleus-independent chemical shifts (NICS) relate to structure in realistic, disordered carbons remains poorly understood. Here, we generate realistic nanoporous carbon structures using molecular dynamics simulations and compute pore-averaged NICS using density functional theory, reproducing experimentally observed negative values across commercial nanoporous carbons. We find a moderate correlation between sp 2 domain area and NICS, indicating that domain size alone is a poor predictor of the observed shifts, while NICS value also weakly correlate with heteroatom content and 6-membered ring fraction. Instead, decomposing local shielding from non-local contributions shows that the framework's bulk magnetic susceptibility, which implicitly encodes domain size, packing arrangement and defects, dominates the pore-averaged response. These results reframe NICS as a reporter of the framework's collective magnetic susceptibility, rather a local probe of isolated aromatic environments. This position NMR as a quantitative tool for characterizing functional disorder in nanoporous carbons and will help establish a link between framework architecture and performance.
items.authors: Thomas Kress, Xinyu Liu, Alexander C. Forse

items.title: Fusion-Number-Dependent Emergence of 16π-Electron Antiaromatic Circuits in Thienocyclopenta-Fused Pyrenes
items.abstract: Antiaromatic 4nπ-electron circuits provide a powerful strategy for narrowing the HOMO–LUMO gaps of π-conjugated molecules, yet their contribution is often attenuated or obscured in stable polycyclic frameworks by competing local aromatic stabilization. Here we report a systematic series of thienocyclopenta-fused pyrenes containing one ( 1TP ), two ( trans -2TP and cis -2TP ), or four ( 4TP ) fused thienocyclopentadiene units, designed to evaluate the stepwise contributions of embedded 16π-electron circuits. The molecules were synthesized through Suzuki–Miyaura coupling followed by palladium-mediated annulation. Notably, 4TP was isolated as an air- and ambient-light-stable green solid, and its structure was confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Comparative 1 H NMR analysis revealed a progressive upfield shift of diagnostic protons upon increasing the number of fused thienocyclopentadiene units, indicating the emergence and amplification of a paratropic ring-current effect. Theoretical calculations supported the emergence and strengthening of 16π-electron antiaromatic contributions in the two 2TP isomers and 4TP . Frontierorbital calculations and cyclic voltammetry further showed that the LUMO level is substantially stabilized whereas the HOMO level remains nearly unchanged, resulting in a systematic decrease in the HOMO–LUMO gaps. These results establish thienocyclopenta fusion as an effective molecular design strategy for controlling the antiaromatic contribution of 16π-electron circuits within a stable carbon-rich π-framework.
items.authors: Kenji Tsukamoto, Koji Takagi, Yasutomo Segawa

items.title: A Silica-Supported Tungsten-Iridium Hydride Catalyst with Enhanced Arene H/D Exchange performances
items.abstract: Despite extensive exploration of reaction conditions, the direct synthesis of a molecular tungsten-iridium complex from Cp*IrH 4 and W(≡C t Bu)(Np) 3 remained elusive. However, we discovered that the silica-supported tungsten alkylidyne species, (≡SiO)W(≡C t Bu)(CH 2 t Bu) 2 , readily reacts with Cp*IrH 4 , enabling the formation of heterobimetallic surface species, (≡SiO)W(CH 2 t Bu) 2 (H) n IrCp*. This result demonstrates the power of Surface OrganoMetallic Chemistry (SOMC) as a unique synthetic method for assembling heterobimetallic architectures that are otherwise inaccessible or unstable under homogeneous conditions. Preliminary catalytic evaluations in H/D exchange of arenes reveal that this silica-supported W–Ir material shows the best performance within the series, exhibiting higher activity than Hf–Ir and Ta–Ir analogs.
items.authors: Andrey V. Pichugov, Oussama Fayafrou, David Gajan, Laurent Veyre, Chloé Thieuleux, Camp Clement

items.title: Assessing the state of the art in ADMET prediction: Lessons from the OpenADMET-ExpansionRx community blind challenge
items.abstract: Computational blind challenges are essential for advancing drug discovery, especially in research areas with limited public data, such as absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity (ADMET) prediction. In this paper, we present the results of our latest community blind challenge, organized in collaboration with Expansion Therapeutics (ExpansionRx). Participants were tasked with predicting nine distinct ADMET endpoints routinely evaluated during lead optimization of compounds in drug discovery programs. Following unprecedented engagement from the global community, this challenge provided valuable insights into the state of the art in machine learning for ADMET modeling. Evaluating submissions against a realistic, challenging dataset from active ExpansionRx drug discovery programs revealed that message-passing neural networks and chemical foundation models dominated among the top performers. Furthermore, the results highlighted the power of proprietary industry datasets and a critical need to optimize predictive workflows for different endpoints independently via multitasking and task-affinity grouping. We also demonstrate how hosting our open-source blind challenge infrastructure on a flexible platform like Hugging Face was pivotal for driving community engagement and visibility. Ultimately, blind challenges supported by robust infrastructure, widespread dissemination, and rigorous post-challenge analysis are fundamental to maximizing the utility of public data releases. We anticipate that these community benchmarks will continue to drive the advancement of ADMET models, enabling their deployment in both early- and late-stage drug discovery.
items.authors: Maria A. Castellanos, Hugo MacDermott-Opeskin, Jon Ainsley, Jonathan A. Swain, Sean Colby, Devany West

items.title: Mathematical Modeling of Coupled Electronic and Ionic Transport Mechanics in Flow-Electrode Capacitive Deionization
items.abstract: Flow Capacitive Deionization (FCDI) is an electrochemical ion removal technology well-suited for continuous desalination of brackish waters, as well as ion-specific removal. Despite over a decade of research into FCDI, few researchers have probed the transient and spatially dependent mechanisms of ion transport and electro-adsorption within flow electrodes. In this study, transport equations describing the advection of overpotential along with the flowing electrode are coupled with the Nernst-Planck equations governing ion transport within the ion exchange membranes, water channel, and slurry electrolyte. The effect of flow velocity on electrical potential profiles and active regions of capacitive electro-adsorption are illustrated using 2-dimensional Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulations. The model is then validated against a representative experimental cell using experimentally determined slurry properties and membrane properties as model inputs. The model shows general agreement with experimental data despite a high variability in experimental results. Finally, an empirical correlation for slurry conductivity, capacitance, and velocity, is fitted to non-dimensionalized simulation results, yielding power model correlations analogous to the Nusselt number and Peclet numbers in conductive heat transfer, Nu c ∝Pe c 0.258±0.002 . The result is a useful tool for predicting FCDI cell performance based on material inputs and operating parameters. This model serves as valuable groundwork for the expansion of FCDI modeling capabilities and subsequent optimization of operational parameters and cell geometries.
items.authors: Garrett Pohlman, Floria Li, Emna Aidi, Bilen Akuzum, Ertan Agar, Lukas Hackl

items.title: Harnessing π-d magnetic interactions in Co porphyrins by metal-ligand coordination
items.abstract: π-Multiradicalic compounds fabricated by on-surface synthesis have emerged as a powerful platform to interrogate spin interactions at the atomic scale. However, the introduction and role of unpaired d-electrons on such systems, and the study of π-d electronic interactions, are still incipient. In this context, a crucial point is the tunability of the inherent magnetic properties of such π-d architectures by incorporation of peripheral metal-organic coordination, which at the same time allows creating self-assembled architectures. Herein, to this aim we exploit an ex-professo synthesized Zn-porphyrin (1) equipped with two carbonitrile-dimethyl-phenyl moieties at its trans-meso positions, which forms π-extended metallo-organic nanostructures featuring unpaired π-electrons through cyclodehydrogenation and concomitant carbonitrile-gold coordination. Transmetallation of such Zn-based nanoarchitectures with Co atoms gave rise to the several Co-based porphyrin multiradicalic species featuring both unpaired π and d electrons, including porphyrin monomers (CoPor M) and dimers (Co-Por D) as well as one-dimensional porphyrin nanochains (1D CoPor NC) and nanotapes (1D CoPor NT). Scanning probe spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveal that the carbonitrile-gold coordination environment dramatically alters the magnetic structure of the cobalt center as compared to analogue porphyrin species lacking the CN group. On the one hand, in both CoPor M and 1D CoPor NC the cobalt atom presents a S=3/2 ground state versus the S=1/2 case for Co porphyrins analogues lacking the nitrile moiety. Additionally, no Kondo interactions are detected at the metal center, as a consequence of a diminished magnetic interaction of CoPor M and 1D CoPor NC with the Au(111) substrate. On the other hand, CoPor D presents two radical electrons distributed between the cobalt atoms and the carbon π-system which interact ferromagnetically yielding a S=1 ground state. Our findings demonstrate how metal-ligand coordination can be used to harness the magnetic interactions within surface-supported multiradicalic molecular systems.
items.authors: María Tenorio, Lenka Cerna, Marco Lozano, Ana Barragán, Miguel Martínez García, Aurelio Gallardo

items.title: A field-deployable method for measuring picomolar mercury levels in natural waters
items.abstract: Measurements of mercury (Hg) at sub- to picomolar concentrations in natural waters often rely on cold vapor atomic fluorescence spectrometry (CVAFS), which provides the sensitivity required for trace detection. However, CVAFS instruments are not well suited for routine field deployment and require compressed high-purity argon or helium gas to operate, limiting their use in remote regions and locations without established analytical infrastructure. Cold-vapor atomic absorption spectrometry (CVAAS) offers a robust alternative but generally lacks the sensitivity required for low-level natural waters. Here, we optimized and tested the Nippon Instruments EMP Gold+, a purge-and-trap preconcentration system coupled to a portable CVAAS detector, to address this analytical challenge. We developed protocols for total Hg (THg) and dissolved gaseous Hg (DGM) and evaluated their performance in seawater during field deployments in Monterey Bay, California, USA and the Gulf of Guinea, Ghana. The optimized methods achieved detection limits of 0.97 pM for THg and 0.25 pM for DGM. THg measured in the Gulf of Guinea agreed closely with laboratory CVAFS measurements (R 2 = 0.953, slope = 1.11), with field matrix-spike recoveries of 90.6-96.2%. In Monterey Bay, portable DGM measurements reproduced the vertical structure observed independently for dimethylmercury using gas chromatography coupled to CVAFS. We demonstrate that this new approach can support direct measurements in regions where compressed gases and specialized analytical infrastructure are unavailable and provide rapid screening to guide subsequent sampling for more detailed Hg speciation.
items.authors: Roland P. Ovbiebo, Johannes West, Abril Hernandez, Hannah M. Adams, Ziheng Kuang, Gabriella A. Yeboah

items.title: Solving density-of-states occupation in disordered systems using neural networks
items.abstract: Describing density-of-states occupation with high precision in disordered systems is crucial for modeling charge transport and understanding doping mechanisms or interfacial energy-level alignment. Beyond fundamental insight from a mechanistic understanding of these physical phenomena, accurate modeling is pivotal for optimizing technological applications in optoelectronic and thermoelectric devices. However, the required calculations are computationally demanding and inherently complex, preventing systematic computational-experimental approaches. Here, we leverage neural networks to perform these calculations precisely and efficiently. We first demonstrate this approach for the Fermi-Dirac occupation of Gaussian densities of states, achieving accelerations of up to three orders of magnitude, a substantial advantage for advanced modeling workflows that require repeated evaluation of the underlying integrals. We then introduce a neural network for doped molecular materials, such as organic semiconductors, that directly predicts doping levels and Fermi level shifts, circumventing conventional recursive schemes and accelerating computations by nearly five orders of magnitude.
items.authors: Melissa Berteau-Rainville, Emanuele Orgiu, Ingo Salzmann

items.title: Glycine specifically labelled proteins to enhance solution NMR of methylene groups
items.abstract: Specific isotopic labelling of proteins has greatly advanced biomolecular NMR. Protein domains, individual residues or certain chemical groups with specific patterns of isotopes can be incorporated to optimize the use of NMR pulse schemes. Here, we describe a novel cell-free protein expression protocol that allows specific isotopic labelling of glycine residues, whilst all other amino acids are independently labelled. This technique enables us to prevent amino acid scrambling and cross-protonation from the solvent resulting in high labelling selectivity of glycine residues as attested by quantification of 15N amide scrambling and residual Ca protonation. We then highlight the potential applications of these samples in the field of biomolecular NMR. We produced a 1 H, 13 C glycine specifically labelled sample of a subunit of the heavy metal ATPase HMA8, in a completely perdeuterated 2 H background and demonstrate how the CH 2 -TROSY experiment recorded on such a sample improves the spectral quality of glycine residues.
items.authors: Rachel Lenoir Capello, Lionel Imbert, Jérôme Boisbouvier, Emeric Miclet

items.title: Hybrid Organosilicon Polymers Integrating Latent Si–Si Chromophores and Orthogonal Si–O–C Reactivity
items.authors: Bercis Pektas, Cuong Minh Quoc Le, Kenshiro Hitoshio, Hideki Yorimitsu, Jun Shimokawa, Hatice Mutlu

items.title: Surface hydroxyls act as key intermediates in the selective oxidative dehydrogenation of 2-propanol on Co3O4
items.abstract: Transition-metal oxides typically catalyze aerobic oxidation reactions with high activity even at low temperatures, but rarely with high selectivity. Owing to the complexity of competing surface processes on such catalysts, the rational design of selective low-temperature catalysts still requires a deeper mechanistic understanding of the active surface and reaction intermediates. In this work, we combine operando modulation-excitation infrared spectroscopy with density functional theory and molecular dynamics to mechanistically investigate 2-propanol oxidation over Co3O4 with a focus on surface hydroxyls, acting as hydrogen acceptors during alcohol adsorption. We identify two chemically distinct hydroxyl populations: linear hydroxyls, which actively participate in acetone formation and can be considered part of the active surface ensemble, and bridged hydroxyls, which behave largely as spectators. Together, these results provide a molecular-level mechanistic picture of alcohol oxidation on Co3O4 and establish the dynamic role of surface hydroxyl species as active players in heterogeneous oxidation catalysis.
items.authors: Pierfrancesco Ticali, Stephane Kenmoe, Hamidreza Hajiyani, Amir Omranpour, Nicolas Cosanne, Hauke Scheele

items.title: Sulfilimine benziodoxolones: stable electrophilic bifunctional reagents for nitrogen incorporation
items.abstract: We report the design and scalable synthesis of novel sulfilimine-based hypervalent iodine reagents (INSert, based on the I-N=S motif), that are bench-stable, non-explosive and can act as bifunctional electrophilic nitrogen donors. Their distinctive architecture combines a benziodoxolone moiety to induce electrophilicity at the nitrogen atom, with a sulfilimine group as a versatile, latent synthetic handle for downstream diversification. We first demonstrate the utility of this reagent class through the formal anti-Markovnikov hydrosulfilimination of alkenes via alkyldimethylborane intermediates, followed by subsequent transformation of the resulting N-alkylsulfilimine into various nitrogen-containing scaffolds. We also report preliminary N-insertion reactions with an indole and an imidazole. These results clearly show that the reagents’ modular iodinane-sulfilimine architecture can open new avenues for the incorporation of nitrogen into organic molecules through multiple distinct reaction manifolds.
items.authors: Andrii Suponytskyi, Patrick W. Fritz, Mykola Avramenko, Lucia Invernizzi, Gian Carmine Conigliaro, Lara Kirchberg

items.title: Deoxygenative Dialkylation of Vinylic Epoxides to Chiral Alkanes by Double SN2’
items.abstract: Chiral alkanes bearing two contiguous tertiary all-carbon stereocentres are important motifs in bioactive molecules, natural products and functional compounds, yet their stereocontrolled synthesis remains challenging. Here we report their modular preparation through the formal deoxygenative dialkylation of enantioenriched vinyl epoxides. Two consecutive organocopper-mediated S N 2′ substitutions enable stereospecific transfer of the starting stereochemical information followed by diastereoselective installation of the adjacent stereocentre. The sequence can be performed in one pot, providing densely substituted hydrocarbon frameworks with high regio- and stereocontrol. The method accommodates diverse, including sterically demanding, alkyl substituents, extends to cyclic substrates, and leaves a terminal alkene for downstream diversification. Vinyl epoxides thus provide a stereochemically encoded platform for straightforward access to complex chiral alkanes.
items.authors: Nicolò Rossi, Gwilherm Evano

items.title: Basis-Set Limit Wavefunction Energies of Massive Water Clusters: Resolution of a Challenge for Many-Body Expansion
items.abstract: The many-body expansion (MBE) offers a route to high-level wavefunction energies of systems beyond the reach of conventional calculations, but its practical convergence is entangled with basis set superposition error (BSSE), electrostatic embedding, and the scarcity of direct supersystem benchmarks at large size. Here, we show that as the complete-basis-set (CBS) limit is approached, electrostatically embedded three-body MBE, EE-MBE(3), provides accurate absolute and relative HF, RI-MP2, and CCSD(T) energies across water clusters of varying sizes. Critically, the largesystem conclusions are tested against direct same-level supersystem references rather than lowerlevel or extrapolated benchmarks. A distributed canonical RI-MP2 implementation enables a systematic HF/RI-MP2 campaign for 64 and 128 waters with cc-pVXZ and aug-cc-pVXZ basis sets (X = D, T, Q), with three configurations at each cluster size/basis set point. The largest calculation, (H2O)128/aug-cc-pVQZ, contains 22,016 spherical primary basis functions and, to our knowledge, is the largest reported MP2 calculation performed without a local-correlation approximation. At augcc-pVQZ, EE-MBE(3) maintains per-water errors within the 0.09 kcal mol-1 dynamical-accuracy
items.authors: Yuhong Jiang, Jiarui Wang, Giuseppe M. J. Barca, Junming Ho

items.title: From Rotor to Motor: Dissecting Design Principles for Light-Driven Directional Motion
items.abstract: Research on molecular motors continues to expand as increasing attention is devoted to dynamic and out-of-equilibrium chemical systems. Among the different classes of artificial molecular machines, light-driven motors are the most extensively present, yet the fundamental principles governing their directional motion remain difficult to disentangle, particularly for non-specialists. This work applies these concepts in a tutorial setting by gradually implementing molecular features to a base scaffold that turns it from a bistable system into an experimentally observable light-driven molecular motor. In doing so, it demonstrates how directional bias emerges as soon as relaxation of a high-energy state is coupled to a mechanical movement (a power stroke), while the motor performance can be addressed through modification of the underlying energy landscape. In addition, we show a practical workflow for benchmarking new motor candidates along with the experimental determination of their kinetic and thermodynamic parameters. To complement this study, we provide procedures for undergraduate students to synthesize and operate a molecular motor in practical courses.
items.authors: Nils C. Jansen, Romain Jamagne, Johannes Wega, Ludmilla Sturm, Aya Lebrazi, Marion Pupier

items.title: Drawing the Bow: Bending Peropyrene for Singlet Fission
items.abstract: Singlet fission (SF) can overcome efficiency limits in solar cells by converting one photon into two triplet excitons. Only a few organic chromophores, however, possess triplet energies compatible with Si- and GaAs-based semiconductors commonly used in photovoltaic devices. Peropyrene fulfills these energetic requirements, but excimer formation in its unsubstituted form stabilizes the singlet excited state. This lowers its energy below the threshold required for SF, necessitating control over intermolecular interactions. Contorting chromophores reduces their ability to achieve effective π-surface overlap with neighboring molecules, but the most common strategy, twisting, comes at the cost of a lower triplet energy. We overcome this trade-off by bending peropyrene into a bow via selective π-radical cascade reactions. This approach enables progressive deformation to the limit attainable with this method, a regime hitherto inaccessible by strategies developed for shorter and longer homologs. Bending reorganizes the solid-state crystal packing and reduces the extent of red-shifted emission in concentrated solution and in the solid state, consistent with reduced excimer stabilization. Calculations show a slight increase in triplet energy, desirable for improved compatibility with relevant semiconductors.
items.authors: Paula L. Widmer, Daniel Čavlović, Tara Matic, Olivier Blacque, Michal Juríček

items.title: Dynamic Flow Experimentation for Data-Rich Polymer Synthesis
items.abstract: Growing global challenges in healthcare, energy, sustainability, and technology have motivated increased automation and robotics to accelerate material discovery and development. Continuous droplet flow chemistry has provided a solution to non-uniform mixing and transport phenomena and provides the advantages of batch reactions for screening individual reaction conditions and reagent compositions. Dynamic experimentation in flow chemistry enables the exploration of a broad design space while minimizing the use of reagents and time by continuously varying reaction parameters (such as temperature, concentration, reaction time). Here, an automated polymer synthesis platform with dynamic experimentation capabilities was implemented. The platform leveraged syringe pumps, a custom uniform irradiance photochemical reactor with tunable temperature control, inline Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and an online benchtop nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometry (NMR) at 80 MHz for automated and data-rich polymer synthesis. The combination of inline FTIR, online NMR, and offline (500 MHz) NMR enabled cross-validation between analytical techniques, and parity plots comparing data between the techniques had an R 2 value greater than 0.99 for the dynamic experiment exploring the PET-RAFT homopolymerization of methyl acrylate. Dynamic experimentation was also used to explore the copolymerization of methyl acrylate and dimethylacrylamide. The obtained rich data were used to generate accurate Gaussian process regression models for the polymerization reactions with R 2 values greater than 0.9 for parity plots of the model vs experimental monomer conversion values. The Gaussian process regression model of the copolymerization was used to understand copolymerization reaction kinetics by determining reactivity ratios under various light intensity and temperature conditions.
items.authors: Dylan J. Walsh, Katharina A. Fransen, Alexander Bentley, Federico Florit, Klavs F. Jensen, Bradley D. Olsen

items.title: Resolving Water-Oxidation Kinetics by Combining Operando Spectroscopy with O2 Evolution Rates over Seven Orders of Magnitude
items.abstract: Electrocatalytic water oxidation is central to renewable energy conversion, yet the origin of its potential–current response remains challenging to define. Classical electrode kinetics attributes the empirical exponential increase in current with potential to the linearly lowering of the activation barrier with applied potential, as described by Butler–Volmer formalisms, while potential-dependent coverage of active surface states has also been considered as an important factor in electrocatalytic kinetics. However, direct quantitative experimental links between the state evolution, activation-energy changes, and the macroscopic potential-current response remain limited. Here, by combining temperature-dependent electrochemistry with operando optical spectroscopy, we show that the apparent activation energy decreases approximately linearly with the coverage of electrophilic *O active states on iridium oxide catalysts. Potential-current data across more than 7 orders of magnitude, obtained from microelectrode and electrochemical mass spectrometry, reveal a continuously evolving Tafel slope from ~20 to 160 mV dec-1, which is not captured by the simplest version of Butler-Volmer equation. In contrast, a second-order coverage-dependent barrier model, employing *O active state densities determined from optical spectroscopy, is found to give a good fit to the global potential-current response, with the coverage dependence of the activation barrier being in good agreement with that measured directly from temperature-dependent data. More complex models are also discussed.
