These results link water oxidation kinetics to the accumulation and interaction of active states, providing a framework for understanding kinetics of multistep electrocatalytic reactions.
items.authors: Caiwu Liang, Jack Kirk Pedersen, Reshma Rao, Jan Rossmeisl, Ifan E.L. Stephens, Soren B. Scott

items.title: Pore-network homogeneity for mechanically reliable powder-compacted solid-electrolyte separators
items.abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) with alloy anodes require solid-electrolyte (SE) separators that sustain ion transport while accommodating repeated electrode-derived mechanical loads. However, the mechanical state of powder-compacted separators is commonly inferred from bulk porosity, averaged mechanical properties, or cell-level stack pressure changes, obscuring spatially heterogeneous local responses. Here, we show that pore-network homogeneity is a key determinant of the mechanical reliability of sulfide solid-electrolyte separators by governing local mechanical heterogeneity and stress localization. FIB-SEM tomography and spatially resolved nanoindentation reveal that a highly densified separator with a broad particle-size distribution (PSD) retains clustered pore-rich and mechanically compliant regions, whereas a narrower-PSD separator exhibits a more homogeneous pore network and local mechanical response. Despite comparable cell-level pressure evolution, the two separators show markedly different cycling stability. Post-cycling microscopy reveals cracking and interfacial delamination in the heterogeneous separator, while microstructure-resolved simulations reveal stronger local stress amplification consistent with these observations. Controlled digital structures with identical D50 and porosity further isolate PSD-dependent changes in pore architecture and stress distribution. These findings establish pore-network homogeneity as a key design criterion for mechanically reliable solid-electrolyte separators beyond ionic conductivity and bulk densification.
items.authors: Hyeok-Rae Cho, Hyeong-Jong Kim, Jae-Seung Kim, Beom Jin Park, Youngkyung Kim, Daeyeon Lee

items.title: Polymorph Influence on Sequential Anion Exchange Doping and Charge Transport in Poly(didodecyl-quaterthiophene) (PQT) for Organic Thermoelectrics
items.authors: Jie-Hao Chen, Naisong Shan, Yunhao Zhao, Alexander Filatov, Sihong Wang, Shrayesh Patel

items.title: Transition-State Steric Fields Capture Geometric Signatures Associated with Electronic Perturbations in Asymmetric Catalysis
items.abstract: In data analysis of molecular catalysis, molecular shape can be represented by voxel descriptors generated by mapping molecular structures onto a three-dimensional grid according to atomic van der Waals radii. Such voxel representations of molecular shape can be treated as steric molecular fields and are generally used as steric descriptors. However, because electronic perturbations can lead to systematic changes in molecular geometry, steric fields constructed from transition-state (TS) structures may also capture geometric signatures. We therefore examined whether steric fields derived from TS geometries can capture such structural changes associated with electronic perturbations in asymmetric catalysis. Using DFT-calculated TS structures from three asymmetric Michael addition systems, we generated two voxel-based molecular-field representations, steric fields and NPA-charge fields, for the major and minor TS pathways and used them to construct regression models with calculated enantioselectivity (ΔΔ G ‡ ) as the target variable. The resulting steric- and NPA-charge field models showed similar pathway-dependent trends in cross-validated coefficients of determination (q 2 ). The NPA-charge fields revealed distinct charge responses across the three reaction systems, and the associated changes in TS geometry were captured by the steric fields. These results indicate that TS-derived steric fields can encode not only molecular shape but also the geometric changes associated with electronic perturbations, providing simple and interpretable descriptors for data analysis in asymmetric catalysis.
items.authors: Shigeru Yamaguchi

items.title: Plasmonic Coupling Within Atomically Precise Nanocluster Dimers for Engineering Hot-Carrier Generation and Molecular Activation
items.abstract: Activating the exceptionally strong N≡N remains a fundamental challenge due to the chemical inertness of molecular nitrogen (N2). Plasmonic nanoclusters offer a promising approach by generating localized electromagnetic fields and energetic hot carriers that can drive bond activation at ambient conditions. Here, we combine real-time time-dependent density functional theory with Ehrenfest molecular dynamics to reveal how plasmonic coupling between tetrahedral Ag20 nanoclusters governs N2 activation and dissociation. Systematic variation of the intercluster separation shows that a 6 Å nanogap maximizes near-field enhancement and hot-electron transfer to the adsorbed N2, accompanied by N-N activation. Consequently, N2 dissociation is achieved at incident field strengths as low as 0.5 VÅ–1, whereas larger-gap dimers exhibit substantially lower activity. Similarly, isolated N2 remains intact under comparable conditions. These findings establish nanogap engineering as an effective strategy for optimizing plasmon-driven N2 activation and provide design principles for developing efficient plasmonic catalysts.
items.authors: Khushboo Bhardwaj, Samir Kumar Nayak, Pramod K. Verma, Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala

items.title: Carboxyl–Group Removal and Return: Mechanistic and Strategic Advances in Decarboxylation–Carboxylation
items.abstract: Carboxylic acids are ubiquitous functionalities and indispensable synthetic linchpins in organic chemistry. In recent years, strategies involving the removal, exchange, or recycling of the carboxyl group, particularly decarboxylation and carboxylation have gained remarkable momentum, partly driven by the imperative to valorize carbon dioxide generated in chemical transformations. Beyond simple CO2 extrusion, tandem decarboxylation–carboxylation and related cyclic processes have emerged as powerful yet underexplored approaches for constructing carboxylic acids in a single operation. This review highlights recent advances (2000–2026) in decarboxylation–re-carboxylation chemistry, with an emphasis on mechanistic understanding, reactive intermediates, and the strategic use of CO2 as a transient functional handle. We introduce a unified conceptual framework that classifies carboxyl–group transfer based on the identity of the carbon shuttle, the timing and mode of carboxyl reintroduction, and the nature of reactive intermediates. Subsequent sections discuss three major mechanistic archetypes: CO2–cycling decarboxylation–re-carboxylation, ester–cycling decarboxylation–re-esterification, and non-in situ carboxyl transfer using exogenous CO2 or alternative carboxyl sources. By delineating key developments and conceptual trends, we aim to inspire further innovation in exploiting carboxyl–group recycling as a platform for sustainable molecular synthesis.
items.authors: Yujuan Xie, Liliang Huang, Huangdi Feng, Erik V. Van der Eycken

items.title: A quantitative roadmap from catalyst benchmarks to commercial hybrid electrolysis
items.abstract: Hybrid water electrolysis replaces the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction with the oxidation of an organic substrate, producing hydrogen alongside another value-added chemical. In its most efficient form, the electrochemical oxidative dehydrogenation (EOD) of aldehydes, hydrogen evolves at both electrodes with specific electricity consumption down to 4 kWh kg−1 totalH2 , tenfold lower than conventional water electrolysis. Yet whether such efficiency gains translate into commercial viability has never been tested, as the field lacks standardized performance metrics, limiting catalyst comparability and industrial viability assessment. We propose three performance metrics: Anodic Hydrogen Productivity (AHP), Specific Electricity Consumption (SEC), and Deactivation Rate (DR), and benchmark all reported EOD systems as a case study. A techno-economic analysis links these metrics to net present value and reveals a roadmap to commercial viability: (i) Feedstock selection is the primary economic determinant; (ii) Catalyst stability is the foremost bottleneck, with DRs exceeding tolerable values by three orders of magnitude; (iii) Current density is a linear lever on economics; (iv) Energy efficiency, the property most intensively optimized by the field, matters least, contributing under 1% of net present value for high-value products. This offers quantitative benchmarks for catalyst and process development toward commercially viable EOD. Because the metrics depend only on measurable cell performance, benchmarks and roadmap transfer directly to other hybrid electrolysis concepts.
items.authors: Katharina M. Ebeling, J. Raphael Seidenberg, Benni Zou, Dominik Bongartz, Alexander Mitsos, Regina Palkovits

items.title: DeMiR: Density-Matrix-Informed Representations for Molecular Property Prediction
items.abstract: The Hohenberg–Kohn theorem, which states that all physical quantities in the ground state are functionals of the electron density, suggests that much of a molecule's behavior is encoded in its electronic structure. This study proposes DeMiR, a model that treats electron density matrix prediction as a pretraining task. DeMiR reconstructs cc-pVDZ/B3LYP density matrices for molecules ranging in size from QM9-scale molecules to drug-like molecules with up to 146 atoms, achieving median NMAE values of 1.0% and 2.16%, respectively. At the atomic level, the model's embeddings contain electronic structure information: per-atom electronic observables are predicted with an R² of 0.94 by a linear probe, whereas Uni-Mol reaches 0.84 and a randomly initialized model of the same architecture only 0.63. The embeddings also remove 44.9% of the residual error left by a geometry-based descriptor, showing that this information is not linearly accessible from an explicit geometric descriptor. At the molecular level, transfer depends on the label type. Where electronic structure directly determines the property, transfer holds: on an external experimental pKa test set, fine-tuned DeMiR achieves an MAE of 1.143, significantly outperforming a randomly initialized control with the same architecture and training budget (1.397), and performing on par with or better than chemical foundation models pretrained on far larger datasets. In contrast, for labels such as pIC50 and ADMET, DeMiR shows no consistent advantage over existing general-purpose foundation models, as two-dimensional substructures and physicochemical descriptors have already saturated predictive performance. This study presents the scope within which a connection between electron density prediction capability and molecular property prediction capability holds, along with its boundaries.
items.authors: Donghyeon Kim, Dongsup Kim

items.title: Fourteen-Membered Macrocyclic Copper Complex for Highly Selective Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
items.abstract: The selective electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO3−) to ammonia (NH3) represents a promising route for sustainable NH3 production. However, achieving high NH3 selectivity remains challenging due to competing reactions. Additionally, many reported catalysts rely on noble metals and often require relatively elevated catalyst loadings to achieve high apparent activity, while most systems operate only at relatively low current densities. Herein, a fourteen-membered macrocyclic copper complex supported on Ketjenblack (Cu-14MR/KB) is reported as a cathode catalyst for the highly selective electrochemical reduction of NO3− to NH3. With a low Cu loading of 1.34 μmol cm−2, Cu-14MR/KB delivered a high Faraday efficiency for NH3 synthesis of up to 94.8% at a current density of −26.3 mA cm−2 and maintained high NH3 selectivity over a wide current density range from −26.3 to −150 mA cm−2. Notably, at −150 mA cm−2, Cu-14MR/KB achieved an NH3 yield rate of 604 μmol cm−2 h−1 with an NH3 Faraday efficiency of 86.4%. Furthermore, a more contracted Cu–N4 coordination environment was revealed in Cu-14MR than in CuPc, with a shorter Cu–N bond distance, suggesting relatively stronger Cu–N interactions. This work provides an efficient strategy for high-performance NO3− electroreduction using a low-loading and non-noblemetal catalyst.
items.authors: Yuantao Yang, Ryotaro Iwata, Shoji Iguchi, Ritsu Hibino, Koyata Nishiyama, Makoto Moriya

items.title: Light Intensity Switches Photocurrent Polarity via Surface States in Single-Component Semiconductors
items.abstract: Understanding and regulating photocurrent generation in semiconductors, particularly the control of polarity, is central to photoelectrochemical (PEC) system design. While engineered heterojunctions enable wavelength-dependent polarity switching, they require complex architectures. Light intensity, by contrast, is far more readily tuned but has long been limited to modulating photocurrent magnitude. Herein, we report that surface states, which participate in photoinduced carrier transfer, can mediate light-intensity-dependent photocurrent polarity reversal in single-component semiconductors of both n- and p-type (e.g., carbon nitride, CdTe quantum dots, and BiOI). Mechanism studies reveal that in the photocurrent switching potential (E ps ) region, where the built-in potential is attenuated, surface state occupation, dictated by illumination intensity, governs the direction of charge transfer. This surface-state-mediated mechanism establishes light intensity as an orthogonal dimension for adaptive photoresponsivity, bypassing the need for heterojunction engineering. As a proof of concept, a dopamine PEC biosensor built on this principle achieves exceptional selectivity without conventional biorecognition units, where photocurrent polarity itself serves as the recognition dimension.
items.authors: Wang Li, Kaiqing Wu, Hong Yang, Qiushi Ruan, Sicheng Liang, Kaiyuan Wang

items.title: A review on foundation models for polymer informatics
items.abstract: Foundation models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning transferable knowledge from broad, heterogeneous data and adapting them to diverse downstream tasks, driving a growing interest in AI-accelerated scientific discovery. In polymer science, this paradigm offers a promising route beyond conventional machine learning methods that are often confined to isolated tasks and struggle to generalize under data scarcity and across heterogeneous downstream settings. Polymer foundation models (PFMs), however, are not merely general scientific foundation models applied to polymer datasets. They must address representation, generation, transfer, and evaluation challenges specific to polymer informatics. This review synthesizes recent progress in PFMs for representation learning and generative modeling, spanning models designed for polymer systems and those adapted from general foundation models. We organize this review around two stages: (1) polymer modeling as the foundation, covering representations, datasets, model architectures, and pretraining objectives; and (2) downstream applications, evaluation, and adaptation. By synthesizing recent progress, open challenges, and future directions, this review outlines a roadmap toward robust and generalizable foundation models for polymer informatics.
items.authors: Yihan Zhu, Eric Inae, Yuhan Liu, Weijiang Li, Sobin Alosious, Renzheng Zhang

items.title: Wavelength-Sequential Generation of Multi-Emissive Fluorophores for Site-Selective Fluorescence Nanoscopy
items.abstract: Photoactivatable fluorophores are indispensable tools for super-resolution microscopy, but their performance is often hindered by the need for caging group chemistry, ultraviolet activation, interfering triplet-state photochemistry, and most importantly resulting in a single emissive scaffold. Here, we report a hydroacridine-based fluorophore that addresses the often encountered limitations by providing caging-group-free activation using visible light. A heteroatom-engineering strategy enables rapid singlet-state proton-coupled electron transfer, converting a blue-emissive precursor into two highly fluorescent acridinium states with distinct green (ΦF ≈ 0.80) and red (ΦF ≈ 0.78) emission by a two-step photoconversion using blue and green light sequentially. The process operates efficiently under physiological conditions without involving triplet biradical intermediates, enhancing compatibility with live-cell imaging. The fluorophore architecture further supports organelle-targeted imaging and photoinduced intracellular redistribution, enabling multicolour visualization from a single molecular scaffold, serving both spatial and temporal control over the photoactivation. These findings provide new strategies for heteroatom-controlled visible-light photoactivation and fluorophore design, providing a new platform for next-generation super-resolution imaging.
items.authors: Saugat Mondal, Tapas Bera, Debjit Maity, Sayan Paul, Swapnamoy Sahoo, Bhaskar Rao Pinninti

items.title: Energy ordering of singlet and triplet excitedstates in s-indacene, Pentalene,Cyclobutadiene derivatives in singlet fission : A model exact and density matrixrenormalization group study
items.authors: Ramen Patra, Mousumi Das

items.title: Minimum Knowledge Collaboration enables joint materials development through protected optimization
items.abstract: Materials companies must jointly develop products that meet competing requirements while keeping their formulations, processes and models private. Sample exchange alone can leave their searches poorly coordinated. We introduce Minimum Knowledge Collaboration (MKC), which connects private Bayesian optimizers through bounded candidate descriptions and company-specific search directions. Mathematical analysis links representation error, feasible private responses and information-limited search. In 256 controlled synthetic programs, all methods pursued the same reachable product target, defined as 100%. After 64 complete-product tests, MKC reached 92.4%, the information-rich reference 93.8%, and reusable better, neutral or worse feedback 6.0%. By 2,048 tests, ternary feedback reached MKC's result in 30 of 32 simplest bilateral programs; attainment across all 1,024-candidate programs was 12.5%. A cross-study scenario calculation gave a 0.0063% complete-state reconstruction index. This assumption-based design screen complements the measured reconstruction results. MKC demonstrates coordinated product development with bounded disclosure and supports industrial evaluation.
items.authors: Yakov Kutsovsky

items.title: Mechanochemical Activation of Strontium for the Selective Cross-Coupling of Chlorosilanes
items.abstract: Silicon-containing compounds are important in both academic and industrial settings, and the reductive coupling of chlorosilanes is a widely used approach for the formation of Si–Si bonds. However, despite its long history, this strategy for the formation of Si–Si bonds has remained largely limited to homocoupling, while a general synthetic method for selective heterocoupling has yet to be established. Previous strategies have relied on the stepwise generation of silicon nucleophiles or electrochemical methods. Here, we demonstrate that mechanochemical activation of strontium metal by ball milling enables the one-pot, cross-selective coupling of a broad range of chlorosilane pairs. Notably, after screening group 1 and group 2 metals, strontium was found to exhibit higher reactivity under mechanochemical conditions than commonly used metal reductants such as lithium and sodium. Importantly, no reaction occurs when strontium is employed under conventional solution conditions, highlighting the crucial role that mechanical activation plays in the reaction. Finally, this method is also applicable to the cross-coupling of chlorosilanes with chlorogermanes, thus establishing a practical and operationally simple protocol for the formation of E–E (E = Si, Ge) bonds.
items.authors: Hyehwang Kim, Koji Kubota, Hajime Ito

items.title: A Charge-Directed Electrocyclic Ring Opening of Azomethine Ylides as a Route to 2-(N-Acylamino)-1,3-dienes
items.abstract: The electrocyclic ring opening of azomethine ylides driven by charge neutralization leads to 2-N-acylamino-1,3-diene products. The requisite azomethine ylide is formed by deprotonation of an oxazolinium ion, which is formed by O-silylation of a readily available oxazolidinone starting material. Computational studies indicate that the deprotonation event is the rate limiting step of the sequence providing a short-lived ylide intermediate that opens spontaneously via a low-barrier (1.7 kcal/mol) transition state leading to an enecarbamate product that is about 48 kcal/mol lower in energy than the ylide intermediate. Charge minimization biases the equilibrium position of the electrocyclization reaction leading to the ring-opened product. This transformation provides a straightforward route to 2-Nsubstituted-N-acylamino-1,3-dienes which were used in subsequent Diels-Alder cycloaddition reactions to give cyclohexenecarbamate products.
items.authors: Yash Punjabi, Tarun Roy, Roland Tóbiás, Bill Poirier, Matthias Brewer

items.title: Herzberg–Teller eﬀect as a phonon-assisted optical transition in molecules
items.abstract: This study derives expressions for the photophysics of a molecule exhibiting the Herzberg–Teller (HT) effect. The derivation is based on Fermi’s golden rule, and the Longuet-Higgins representation, where the electron–photon and vibronic couplings are treated as perturbations, is used. All the vibrational modes are included, thus enabling the assignment of vibronic progressions in the spectrum originating from Franck–Condon factors. A forbidden transition is regarded as the photon absorption or emission accompanied by phonon absorption or emission, clarifying the contribution of vibronic structures to the transition. The derived expressions are applied to the absorption from S0 to S1 and fluorescence from S2 to S0 for azulene, a molecule known to exhibit the HT effect. Using the S4 state as an intermediate state, the calculated fluorescence spectrum and rate constant agree well with the experimental results. The in-plane stretching vibration of the five-membered ring contributes to phonon emission, whereas that at the junction of the five-and seven-membered rings contributes to the acceptance of the excess excitation energy. Furthermore, the vibronic coupling density analyses reveal that the vibronic couplings originate from the five-membered ring. This study presents a theory that allows for a detailed assignment of vibronic structures involved in the HT effect, providing design guidelines for HT molecules.
items.authors: Takeaki Zaima, Wataru Ota, Takumi Yagi, Tatsuhisa Kato, Tohru Sato

items.title: Extending Hertzian Contact Area Theory to Plastic Deformation of Glassy Polymer Particles
items.abstract: Quantifying the mechanical response of polymer particles under compression is fundamentally hindered by a deceptively simple problem: the contact area between the particle and compression plate can rarely be directly measured during deformation. Since Hertz formulated his contact theory in 1881, widely used Hertzian and adhesive contact models have remained largely confined to the elastic regime, leaving the plastic deformation behavior of polymer particles fundamentally out of reach. Here, we extend the original Hertzian contact area relation from elastic deformation to plastic deformation by combining it with the Boyce–Parks–Argon constitutive model. The contact area predicted by the model agree well with those obtained directly from all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of poly(methyl methacrylate) and poly(methyl acrylate) particles. When the framework is applied to experimental compression data of polystyrene and acrylic particles, it identifies clear yield points and shows that crosslinking density and particle-size effects can be understood within the established framework of bulk polymer mechanics. The framework provides a route to the intrinsic mechanical properties of polymer particles beyond the yield point without direct measurement of the contact area, supporting the rational design of particles with tailored mechanical properties.
items.authors: Ikki Takahashi, Yusuke Yasuda, Minoru Kato, Kazushi Fujimoto

items.title: Checkmate for CHK2: Discovery of First-in-Class Covalent CHK2 Inhibitors with High Potency and Selectivity
items.abstract: Checkpoint kinase 2 (CHK2), a serine/threonine kinase encoded by CHEK2, plays a key role in the DNA damage response (DDR), acting downstream of ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) kinase in the ATM–CHK2–p53 signaling axis. Despite considerable interest in CHK2 as a potential therapeutic target, our understanding of its biological functions and therapeutic potential remains constrained by the limited availability of potent and selective chemical probes. While several non-covalent CHK2 inhibitors have been developed, their utility for interrogating CHK2 biology is often limited by suboptimal kinase selectivity. Moreover, selective covalent inhibitors that enable robust and sustained pharmacological perturbation of CHK2 have not been reported. To address this gap, we developed the covalent CHK2 inhibitor (R)-12b, which selectively targets Cys231 at the P3 position of the glycine-rich loop (P-loop). Covalent binding of (R)-12b induces a repositioning of the P-loop, leading to an outward displacement of the N-lobe and expansion of the ATP-binding pocket. (R)-12b exhibits nanomolar biochemical and cellular potency, good in vitro metabolic stability, moderate covalent bond-formation kinetics, and a highly favorable kinome-wide selectivity profile. Together, these properties establish (R)-12b as a first-in-class selective covalent CHK2 inhibitor and a valuable chemical tool for exploring CHK2 biology and further elucidating its therapeutic potential.
items.authors: Xiaojun Julia Liang, Janosch Rheinganz, Fabian B. Kraft, Sven R. Aldea, Benedikt Masberg, Alexander Rasch

items.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of the Outer-Sphere Reorganization Energies of Aqueous Oligothiophenes
items.abstract: The outer-sphere reorganization energy (λout) contributes directly to the activation barrier for hole transfer in aqueous organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors, yet it is usually estimated from dielectric continuum models rather than computed explicitly. Here, λout is computed for doped oligothiophenes in explicit aqueous electrolyte by all-atom molecular dynamics with an electronic continuum correction, using vertical-energy-gap fluctuation estimators and thermodynamic integration. Increasing the degree of polymerization from one to six decreases λout from 0.84 to 0.55 eV owing to hole delocalization; λout saturates beyond the trimer and remains comparable to the inner-sphere reorganization energy (0.48 eV for the hexamer). Across side-chainfunctionalized thiophene monomers, λout varies by ≈0.2 eV and scales with the square of the doping-induced change in molecular dipole moment, whereas for trimers and hexamers it converges to ≈0.53 eV irrespective of whether the side chain is neutral, cationic, or anionic. These results identify backbone delocalization as the principal determinant of λout for aqueous conjugated oligomers.
items.authors: Huihang Qiu, Nicholas E. Jackson

items.title: Probing local structure and hydrogen incorporation in solution-processed thin-film solid electrolytes
items.abstract: Solution processing of functional thin films offers significant benefits, yet characterising their local structure and bulk composition remains challenging. Here, we investigate the composition-structure-property relationships of nanocomposite Na-Al-P-O (NAPO) thin-film solid electrolytes using impedance spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and time-of-flight elastic recoil detection analysis (ToF-ERDA). An invariant activation energy of ≈0.8 eV across NAPO compositions was observed despite a ≈20-fold variation in ionic conductivity, suggesting that these differences arise primarily from changes in the concentration of mobile Na⁺ in the amorphous matrix. NMR measurements revealed highly disordered Al environments that were correlated with increased conductivity, evidence for multiple Na environments with differing mobilities, as well as a reduced local energy barrier to Na + hopping of ≈0.5 eV for two compositions. ToF-ERDA measurements showed that the elemental distributions were homogeneous, alongside significant H incorporation, identified as hydroxyl groups bound to Al and P via NMR. The H content increased as the ionic conductivity decreased in the NAPO system. Comparison with related, but ionically insulating compositions showed that H is a universal component of solution-processed materials. Although the protons were not mobile in these systems, H is proposed to occupy mobile sites within the framework that would otherwise host mobile ions such as Na + . Thus, our work suggests that promoting local disorder and minimising H incorporation are key design strategies for enhancing ionic conductivity in solution-processed amorphous solid electrolytes.
items.authors: Thomas E. Gill, Leon Hensmann, Jędrzej Kondek, Matthew K. Sharpe, Callum D. McAleese, Michael Ryan Hansen

items.title: Protein Language Model-Boosted Prediction of Isoelectric Point
items.abstract: pH plays a key role in many biological processes. When the solution pH equals the isoelectric point (pI) of a protein, the protein carries zero net charge, which minimizes its solubility and thus promotes aggregation. Here we present ESMpI, a sequence-based protein pI predictor that combines optimized pKa values of seven ionizable residue types and two terminals with embeddings from a pre-trained protein language model. Benchmarked against experimental protein pI values, ESMpI outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, including structure-based approaches that derive the pI of a protein from residue-specific pKa calculations. Finally, ESMpI requires only sequence information, making it well suited for high-throughput proteomescale analyses and protein engineering.
items.authors: Fangfang Luo, Xiangxiang Lu, Zhitao Cai, Hongyu Lin, Yandong Huang

items.title: A Blood–Brain Barrier-on-Chip Approaching In Vivo Tightness for Quantitative Ultrasound-Mediated Opening
items.abstract: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) remains one of the greatest obstacles to the treatment of neurological diseases, preventing the delivery of nearly all large therapeutics and most small molecules to the brain. Although ultrasound-activated microbubbles offer a promising strategy for transient BBB opening, quantitative in vitro models capable of reproducing physiological barrier properties while allowing controlled ultrasound studies remain scarce. Here, we report a human BBB-on-chip that combines near-physiological barrier tightness with real-time quantitative permeability measurements under ultrasound exposure. We identify the key physical parameters governing barrier formation, demonstrating that microenvironment geometry and hydrogel confinement play a decisive role in establishing a functional endothelial barrier. The optimized platform exhibits permeability coefficients for 10 and 70 kDa dextran that approach in vivo values despite relying on a simple endothelial monoculture under static conditions. To quantitatively characterize barrier integrity, we compare three permeability formulations commonly used in the literature and introduce a complementary impermeability index describing barrier dynamics. Finally, we demonstrate that ultrasound-activated microbubbles increase barrier permeability by more than sixfold, enabling the extravasation of fluorescent tricaprylin nanodroplets into the hydrogel compartment.
items.authors: Mathis Martin, Mame-Diarra Sylla, Agathe Neukelmance, Pascal Dargent, Wladimir Urbach, Stéphane Desgranges

items.title: d10 Coinage Metal Organic Chalcogenolates: Tuning Dimensionality and Properties through Phenylthiolate Functionalization
items.abstract: Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates (MOCs) based on d 10 coinage metals constitute a versatile class of coordination polymers combining anisotropic structures with diverse functional properties. In this review, we examine a series of 23 Cu(I), Ag(I), and Au(I)-based MOCs obtained from eight functionalized thiophenolate ligands. The systematic comparison of these compounds highlights how the metal identity, ligand functionalization, steric hindrance, and secondary interactions govern the coordination modes and, most importantly, the dimensionality of the resulting networks. The 1D and 2D MOCs provide a particularly relevant platform to establish relationships between network dimensionality and physical properties. Their photoluminescence and electrical properties reveal distinct trends across the Cu, Ag, and Au series, with dimensionality playing a key role in both light emission and charge transport. The review further discusses the dynamic behavior of these materials, including ligand-exchange processes and reversible transformations between different structural and physical states. Their ability to form fibers, thin films, glasses, and composite materials further illustrates the versatility of MOCs beyond their crystalline structures. Selected examples of optical thermometry, optoelectronics, phase-change materials, sensing, and catalysis demonstrate their emerging functional potential. Overall, this review emphasizes dimensionality as a central structural parameter for understanding structure–property relationships and guiding the design of functional MOCs.
items.authors: Alexis Giraudon, Buqin Xu, Chloé Andrade, Nathalie Guillou, Régis Debord, Gilles Ledoux

items.title: Spin-dependent thermoelectric transportproperties of DPH-based molecular device
items.authors: Ramen Patra, Mousumi Das

items.title: A bipartite quantum-acoustic architecture stabilizes multi-exciton solitons at 323 K
items.abstract: A fundamental thermal paradox has constrained the physical viability of quantum coherent Davydov solitons in protein α-helices for over 50 years. At 323 K (0.0278 eV), ambient thermal noise disrupts the localized amide I self-trapping resonance, rapidly scattering multi-quanta excitations into delocalized thermal states on femtosecond timescales. This long-standing decoherence gap is resolved by a non-equilibrium, bipartite quantum-acoustic stabilization matrix which induces a transverse acoustic viscoelastic phonon gap, extending exciton coherence lifetimes from 6.5 fs to 42.6 fs by acting as a macroscopic low-pass filter. Utilizing non-Markovian open quantum system simulations, we demonstrate that a highly polarizable variable-dipole linactant at the lipid raft interface induces localized electrodynamic Stark defects, breaking lattice translation symmetry to anchor the wave packet. Sustaining this protective boundary against passive diffusive loss mandates a strict kinetic equilibrium that arrests uncoupled proton leaks, directly coupling the continuous, hydrogen-bonded α-helices of eukaryotic F/V-type rotary c-rings to a hyper-rigid viscoelastic membrane locked in a far-from-equilibrium state. Finally, we present a definitive pathway to bypass thermal decoherence by establishing three physical boundary conditions to translate these biological principles into a predictive blueprint for synthetic quantum-acoustic metamaterials.
items.authors: Doris Loh, Russel J. Reiter

items.title: A Framework for Quantifying and Attributing Molecular Standardization Reproducibility in Cheminformatics Pipelines
items.abstract: Molecular structure standardization, which normalizes salts, charge states, tautomers, isotopes and stereochemistry to a canonical form, is mandatory in essentially every cheminformatics pipeline. The protocols used to perform it nonetheless vary across tools, databases and configurations. Disagreement between standardization pipelines is documented at production scale, but existing analyses compare one pipeline against one reference, so they cannot identify which normalization decision produced a given disagreement. We present a measurement framework that treats standardization reproducibility as a quantifiable property of a dataset. Given an arbitrary set of protocols, the method determines whether they agree on each molecule's standardized identity, then attributes each disagreement to a specific normalization operation by systematic ablation. Agreement is evaluated under two identity conventions, canonical SMILES and InChIKey, which we show are not interchangeable. We applied the framework to a seeded random sample of 4,972 ChEMBL structures using three protocols that bracket the plausible range: a minimal one, one approximating the ChEMBL curation pipeline, and a deliberate upper-bound stress case. They agreed on 54.1% of molecules under canonical-SMILES identity (95% CI 52.8–55.5%) and 57.7% under InChIKey identity (56.3–59.0%). Ablation attributed divergence mainly to stereochemistry handling (66.6% of divergent molecules) and tautomer canonicalization (22.1%). Disabling stereochemistry removal, a step no major public pipeline performs, raises agreement to 75.5% and leaves tautomer canonicalization responsible for 87.4% of what remains. The cause spectrum is thus a property of the protocols compared and the dataset audited, not an intrinsic ranking of operations. A hand-assembled benchmark inverts it entirely, which argues for auditing the dataset actually in use instead of relying on published rates. Extending the comparison to the pipelines databases actually run, namely ChEMBL's own curation code and MolVS in two configurations, yields two further results. Our composed ChEMBL-like protocol reproduces ChEMBL's production pipeline on 99.8% of structures, so conclusions drawn from the composed protocols transfer to the real one. And two configurations of a single standardizer agreed with each other on only 56.0% of structures, while two independently developed standardizers agreed on 77.2%. Configuration choice within one tool spans a wider range of outcomes than the choice between tools, so naming the software used is not sufficient provenance. To test whether such divergence carries a practical cost, we applied the same protocols to 27,152 IC50 measurements across four targets. Grouping by standardized identity is what deduplication does, so protocol choice silently changes a dataset. The most aggressive protocol removed up to 9.5% of compounds by merging, fusing into single training labels compounds whose measured activities differed by up to three log units, a thousandfold difference in potency on a cardiac-safety endpoint. Cross-validated model performance was nonetheless statistically indistinguishable across protocols on all four targets, under both random-split and generalization-stressing scaffold-split cross-validation.
items.authors: Sree Vasthav Upputoori, S. Madhav Varma

items.title: High-Resolution 3D Laser Printing of Microalgae-Derived Materials for Photodynamic Therapy
items.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers localized, controllable cancer treatment through reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated by light-activated photosensitizers. Three-dimensional (3D) printing of PDT-active materials has emerged as a powerful tool for fabricating customized structures with controlled architecture and composition. However, conventional PDT materials often require complex, multi-step syntheses with low yields. Consequently, integrating natural photosensitizers into biocompatible matrices represents a crucial step towards sustainable PDT. Here, microalgae-derived materials are investigated to fabricate high-resolution scaffolds via 3D laser printing while retaining the intrinsic photoactive properties of chlorophyll. Within these matrices, native chlorophyll derivatives fulfill a triple light-induced function: driving microalgal lipid biosynthesis, initiating additive-free 3D laser printing, and acting as immobilized photosensitizers. Fluorometric assays confirm robust ROS generation upon red-light irradiation of the 3D printed microalgae-derived material. The photodynamic efficacy of these scaffolds is evaluated in melanoma cells to demonstrate their therapeutic potential. In vitro studies reveal significantly reduced cell viability upon irradiation, while maintaining cytocompatibility under dark conditions. Furthermore, the microalgae-derived materials enable the fabrication of scaffolds with varied complex geometries and feature sizes while retaining photodynamic activity. These findings demonstrate a highly versatile, biobased strategy combining natural photosensitizers with 3D laser printing to produce functional platforms for precision PDT.
items.authors: Clara Vazquez-Martel, Sandra Clara-Trujillo, Carla Arnau del Valle, Lea Sielaff, Juan Luis Gomez Pinchetti, Ramon Martinez-Mañez

items.title: Quantum Subspace Expansion for Molecular Excited States: Representability, Stability, and Practical Considerations
items.abstract: Accurate treatment of excited states remains challenging for classical electronic-structure methods, motivating quantum algorithms that may provide more favorable resource scaling. We systematically assess the practical performance of Quantum Subspace Expansion (QSE) for low-lying electronic states across 28 organic molecules from the Thiel benchmark set. Statevector simulations reveal that QSE representability depends strongly on the target state, active space, and molecular electronic structure, with multiconfigurational character emerging as an important factor. In several cases, the one-body QSE subspace cannot adequately represent the target states, while explicit double-excitation operators improve representability at the cost of a larger operator space. Analysis of the QSE overlap matrix shows that although eigenmodes with small eigenvalues drive numerical instability, they cannot be discarded indiscriminately without compromising spectral accuracy. Under finite-shot sampling, energy errors exhibit an empirical scaling of approximately n_{\mathrm{orb}}^2/\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{shots}}} , which, combined with the growth in measurement groups, yields a total measurement cost of approximately \mathcal{O}(n_{\mathrm{orb}}^{11}) for constant accuracy under our direct-estimation protocol. These results expose a central tension between representability, numerical stability, and measurement cost. Encouragingly, we find that the projected matrices exhibit recurring structural patterns, while the finite-shot perturbations in the Hamiltonian and overlap matrices show nontrivial covariance, suggesting opportunities for more efficient structure-aware measurement and reconstruction strategies. Overall, our results provide an assessment of QSE across chemically-relevant organic molecules, identifying present limitations while highlighting potential routes toward more practical future implementations.
items.authors: Naythan Z. X. Yeo, Shi Jun Ang

items.title: Selective Operando Visualization of Ultrathin Lithium in Li-Metal Batteries by Neutron Capture Imaging
items.abstract: Operando visualization of ultrathin lithium is essential for understanding plating and stripping in lithium-metal batteries, but existing neutron imaging techniques lack sufficient sensitivity for ultra-thin lithium layers formed at crucial early stages. Here we introduce neutron capture imaging (NCI), which selectively detects tritons generated by neutron capture in 6 Li. Ex situ measurements of electrochemically plated and thermally evaporated 6 Li demonstrate sensitivity around 10 nm for a 1.5 h acquisition and two-dimensional imaging with around 100 μm lateral resolution. Simulations indicate that the resolution could approach 25 μm through optical optimization. Operando measurements in an asymmetric Cu|| 6 Li cell reveal spatially heterogeneous lithium plating and stripping in agreement with electrochemical data. Our results establish NCI as a high-sensitivity, near-zero-background tool for operando studies of lithium metal batteries, opening new possibilities for resolving early-stage deposition, dead lithium formation, and interfacial dynamics with broad applicability to ultrathin reactive lithium layers in electrochemical systems.
items.authors: Xiaolong Zhang, Leon Skarjan, Ricardo Carreon, Jongmin Lee, Andreas Borgschulte, Thomas J. Schmidt

items.title: Ultra-Low CoNi Alloy Nanoparticle Loaded Polypyrrole Nanospheres as Oxygen Electrocatalysts in Alkaline to Near-Neutral Zinc-Air Batteries
items.abstract: Dearth of a wide-range pH-adaptable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalyst is a bottleneck in the advancement of efficient metal-air batteries as catalysts optimized for alkaline media often lose effectiveness under near-neutral conditions. Herein, we report an ultralow (~1 atomic%) amount of CoNi alloy loaded polypyrrole-derived graphitic nanoparticle (CoNiPpy) system as a pH-adaptable oxygen electrocatalyst for high energy density and durability in near-neutral zinc-air batteries (ZABs) with 100% coulombic efficiency. The efficient activity of CoNiPpy towards oxygen reduction and oxygen evolution reactions (ORR and OER) is established, with CoNiPpy showing a lower overpotential than the benchmarked Pt-IrO2 catalyst combo in both alkaline and near-neutral electrolytes. When employed as the air cathode in rechargeable ZABs, CoNiPpy outperforms Pt/C benchmarks, sustaining 650 cycles in alkaline electrolyte and 1100 cycles for ~200 h in near-neutral electrolyte. Stable operating voltages of 1.435 V and 1.235 V are achieved in alkaline and near-neutral ZABs respectively. Series connected cells further power a 33 mW lighting load for more than 1 h and operate portable sensors, demonstrating functionality beyond conventional electrochemical benchmarking. Detailed full-cell analysis demonstrates that, rather than relying on high metal loadings, trace CoNi incorporation into a conductive N-containing carbon framework can enable a single bifunctional air cathode to operate across both alkaline and near-neutral ZAB chemistries. The findings further emphasize that appropriate electrolyte selection plays an important role in full-cell performance and guiding the development of scalable zinc-air battery systems.
items.authors: Subhra R. Pattanayak, Pallavi Thakur, Saswata Goswami, Hyoju Park, Arun Devaraj, Chandra Sekhar Tiwary

items.title: Chiral Intramolecular Ether–Borane FLPs for Asymmetric Ketone Hydrogenation
items.abstract: Asymmetric hydrogenation of ketones remains challenging in frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) catalysis, largely because the low basicity of ketones places stringent demands on both H 2 activation and stereocontrol. Here we introduce binaphthyl ether–boranes (BINEBs), a new class of chiral intramolecular FLPs featuring a bis-ether Lewis base tethered to a strongly Lewis acidic borane on an axially chiral binaphthyl scaffold. BINEBs catalyze the asymmetric hydrogenation of a broad range of aromatic ketones, delivering chiral secondary alcohols with high enantioselectivities. This platform also enables the first metal-free kinetic resolution of cyclic α-haloketones using H 2 as the reductant, providing enantioenriched cis-halohydrins with selectivity factors (s) exceeding 200. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support a multifunctional role for the key intramolecular bis-ether motif: it mediates heterolytic H 2 cleavage and, following proton transfer to the ketone, remains engaged through hydrogen bonding, orienting the substrate for stereoselective hydride transfer. This study illustrates how covalent Lewis acid–base preorganization can enhance substrate recognition and stereocontrol, providing catalyst design principles that may open opportunities in asymmetric FLP hydrogenation and Lewis acid catalysis.
items.authors: Nikolay V. Shcherbakov, Julius K. Kräutle, Josep Mas-Roselló

items.title: Predicting Thermophysical Properties of Halide Salts Using On-the-Fly Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials Across Multiple Exchange-Correlation Functionals
items.abstract: In silico modeling of molten salts is pivotal for the development of emerging carbon-free energy technologies, where accurate knowledge of thermophysical properties is essential for understanding and predicting material behavior under operating conditions. However, the accurate prediction of these properties using first-principles methods remains computationally intractable because of the large length scales and long timescales required to adequately describe molten-salt systems. In addition to these computational limitations, the choice of exchange-correlation (XC) functional is crucial for accurately predicting thermophysical properties. Here, we employ machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) to investigate the thermophysical properties of NaBr, KCl, and AgCl, which represent alkali- and transition-metal halides, across their solid and liquid phases. We systematically benchmark ten XC functionals for NaBr over a temperature range of 600–1400 K and subsequently assess the transferability of the best-performing functional to KCl and AgCl. The MLIPs enable simulations at length and timescales beyond the practical limits of conventional ab initio molecular dynamics, thereby facilitating the prediction of key thermophysical properties, including density and ionic self-diffusion coefficients. In addition, the simulations capture the first-order solid–liquid phase transition, allowing the behavior of these salts to be examined across both phases within a unified computational framework. Our results show that the BEEF-vdW functional provides accurate predictions of the optimized lattice constants of NaBr and KCl and consequently reproduces their experimental solid- and liquid-phase densities. For molten NaBr, the predicted Na⁺ and Br⁻ self-diffusion coefficients agree with experimental measurements to within approximately 6%, demonstrating the ability of the MLIP-based approach to reproduce experimentally relevant transport properties. However, the transferability of an XC functional is found to be system-dependent. Although BEEF-vdW performs well for NaBr and KCl, it inaccurately predicts the density of AgCl, which is associated with its inaccurate prediction of the lattice constant. In contrast, PBE-D3 provides excellent agreement with the experimental density of AgCl, with deviations of approximately 5% across both the solid and liquid phases. This work establishes a foundation for the high-throughput generation of reliable molten-salt thermophysical databases using general machine-learning potentials, enabling simulations beyond the computational limitations of first-principles methods.
items.authors: Pritam Rudra, Sudarshan Vijay, Ojus Mohan

items.title: Discovery of new octadecanoids in γ-linolenic acid rich oils
items.abstract: 17 novel hydroxy fatty acids derived from LA, ALA, and GLA were characterized in evening 2 primrose, borage and hemp oil. Structural characterization was based on semi-synthetic 3 standards generated by autoxidation, photoxidation and enzymatic conversions, combined 4 with LC-MS and GC-MS analysis with multiple derivatization strategies. Novel oxylipins 6-5 HODE and 7-HODE, presumably formed as site-products of Δ6-desaturase, showed 6 characteristic patterns in GLA-rich oils: 6-HODE occurred at high levels in in evening primrose 7 oil (23 ± 1 mg/100 g) and in borage oil (84 ± 7 mg/100 g), whereas 7-HODE (28.7 ± 8 0.6 mg/100 g) was abundant in hemp oil. These novel oxylipins occurred in similar 9 concentrations in both cold-pressed and refined oils and did not relate to the oxidation status. 10 Although, the occurrence of autoxidatively formed hydroxy-LA, ALA and GLA correlated with 11 peroxide value. Overall, these findings highlight novel oxylipins as promising markers of oil 12 quality and authenticity. 13 14 15 16
items.authors: Ariane Löwen, Lia Warja Musielak, Kathrin Plitzko, Nils Helge Schebb

items.title: Hypoboric Acid Catecholate (HAC) Catalysis for Stereoselective Decarboxylative Borylation of Redox-Active Esters
items.abstract: The Hypoboric Acid Catecholate (HAC) is a new class of diboron reagent bearing a borylcatecholato and a boronic acid moiety. Herein, we demonstrate that HACs can also be expontaneously formed in situ from collections of catechols and hypoboric acid. These HACs catalyze the decarboxylative borylation of redox-active esters, providing superior reactivity and selectivity. Equilibrium and kinetic NMR experiments indicate that the catalytic turnover is enabled by the high affinity of catechols for hypoboric acid and their low affinity for boronic acids that is uncovered herein. The catalytic system operates in mild conditions and is robust towards air and moisture, demonstrating its utility in the synthesis of important medicinally-relevant boronates. The enhanced selectivity is sourced in the regioselective radical capture by HAC intermediates at their customized borylcatecholato moiety, which can easily be stereoelectronically tailored for specific applications. These features of the catalytic approach with unsymmetrical HACs presented herein contrast with current state-of-the-art methods based on stoichiometric symmetrical diboron reagents.
items.authors: S. V. Kohlhepp, M. Costantini, B. Meana-Baamonde, Abraham Mendoza

items.title: Synthesis and Reactivity of Fluorene-Bridged Cyclic Diaryliodonium Salts
items.abstract: Spirocyclic organic compounds play a significant role in organic materials, particularly in the field of optoelectronics. In this study, novel spiro-bridged cyclic diaryliodonium salts were synthesised in yields of up to 78%. The structure of the parent salt was confirmed by X-ray crystallography, and the salt was functionalised in iodine-chalcogen exchanges towards highly valuable xanthene derivatives in up to 88% yield.
items.authors: Jan Rick Koch, Mattis Damrath, Jannis Diekmann, Oliver Fincke, Boris J. Nachtsheim

items.title: High-resolution mass spectrometry revealed that amino acid-based surfactants as a potential contributor to bacterial regrowth in tap water
items.abstract: Microbial regrowth in tap water poses a potential threat to public health. Although biodegradable organic matter (BOM) supports microbial proliferation, specific BOM components remain largely unknown. This study evaluated the bacterial growth potential and explored BOM components in tap water samples collected from a hospital and a university. In the hospital sample, indigenous microbial communities grew up to 107 cells/mL after several days of incubation. Amplicon sequencing revealed that abundance of Methylotenera mobilis increased significantly. By solid-phase extraction followed by liquid chromatography high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC/HRMS), 36 putative BOM components were screened from 5,787 dissolved organic matter components. Tandem mass spectrometry and co-chromatography identified C18H36N4O3 as lauroyl arginine, an N-acyl amino acid and amino acid-based surfactant. N-lauroylglycine, and N-myristoylglycine were identified as BOM components from the university tap water sample. Further incubation experiments revealed that some bacterial species can use these three compounds as sole carbon sources. Our findings demonstrate that compound-level characterization using LC/HRMS can reveal previously unrecognized contaminants, with potential implications for biological stability and drinking water distribution system management.
items.authors: Yutaro Uehara, Yuta Shinfuku, Ikuro Kasuga, Futoshi Kurisu

items.title: Thioalkyltetrazines Synthesis from Aldehyde Precursors and Application in Ag-Mediated Liebeskind-Srogl Coupling
items.abstract: Tetrahydrotetrazines are readily prepared from aldehydes, but have minimal precedent as precursors to tetrazines of value to bioorthogonal chemistry applications. Formaldehyde and glyoxylate esters undergo condensation with ([1,1'-biphenyl]-4-ylmethyl)thiocarbohydrazide bromide to give practical access to new thioalkyltetrazines as crystalline solids. 3-(([1,1’-biphenyl]-4-ylmethyl)thio)-tetrazine (h-Tz) was used for the synthesis of monosubstituted tetrazines via silver-mediated Liebeskind-Srogl coupling. Tetrazine-3-carboxylic esters were also synthesized using this method, further expanding the library of functional tetrazines for bioorthogonal chemistry applications.
items.authors: HyunJune Jun, Chuanqi Wang, Stephanie Tsang, Remzi Duzguner, John D. Weaver, Shawn LaCasse

items.title: pH-responsive nanopores enable programmable transmembrane potential
items.abstract: Biological ion channels achieve highly selective, ultrafast ion transport through stimulus-responsive gating, in which conformational changes triggered by chemical cues such as pH that modulate channel permeability with exquisite precision. Replicating this coupled chemical-structural functionality in synthetic membranes remains a fundamental challenge, particularly for scalable platforms relevant to energy harvesting, desalination, and chemical sensing. Here, we report a bioinspired polymer-metal-organic framework (MOF) composite membrane in which an amino acid (histidine) functionalized MOF nanopores serve as synthetic proton-gated anion channel. The histidine modified, spatially confined ion transport pathway exhibited selective Cl- diffusion at pH 4, enabling pH programmable control of transmembrane potential. Micrometer-scale percolated transport networks within the composite membrane, architecturally inspired by ion channels embedded in lipid bilayers, translate localized αNH2(histidine)-anion specific interaction into macroscopic, anion selective transmembrane potential output. This work establishes a generalizable design strategy for coupling chemical gating with macroscopic ion transport in synthetic membrane systems, with direct implications for ion separations, sensing and osmotic energy generation.
items.authors: KM. Archana Yadav, Ritupan Sarmah, Bibhab Bandhu Majumdar, Renjith B. Nelliyil, Jaideep Mor, A R Ramya

items.title: Electrochemically Controlled Crystallization Using Selective Bipolar Membrane Electrodialysis
items.abstract: Nitrogen and phosphorus nutrient recovery from wastewater represents a critical frontier for circular fertilizer manufacturing and effective water treatment. Conventional chemical precipitation remains hindered by the need for expensive reagent consumables. Here, we examine an integrated, chemical-free electrochemical mixer (ECM) system that leverages selective bipolar membrane electrodialysis (SBED) to achieve precise struvite (MgNH4PO4 · 6H2O) crystallization. We furthermore demonstrate how control over current density (1–5 mA cm−2), specific charge loading (20–40 C m−3), and hydraulic retention time (τ = 2.3–6.9 s) enhances downstream crystallization yield, purity, and morphology. Shortening retention promotes boundary-layer convection, reducing in-cell scaling energy penalty (∆E) by 86% and total stack energy consumption by 22%. Operating within an optimized pH window (7.7 pH 9.0) governs crystal morphology and allows for 91% yield of highly pure struvite ( 97%), bypassing competitive newberyite crystallization. We unify the ECM transport kinetics and crystallization thermodynamics into a single dimensionless descriptor—the crystallization index—which establishes a linear correlation to predict the product yield based on upstream transport dynamics. Steady specific energy consumption of 9.38 ± 0.9 kWh kg−1 − struvite through autonomous in-situ acid flushing confirms system stability with minimal scaling. Finally, techno-economic analysis evaluates the levelized cost of struvite produced as $996 t−1, which is a reduction in operating expenditures by a maximum of 89% compared to commercial phosphorus recovery installations. Ultimately, the ECM eliminates crystallization chemical dependencies and reduces membrane scaling bottlenecks, establishing a highly tunable and efficient separations reactor with precise control of crystal products.
items.authors: Hyuck Joo Choi, Spandan Mondal, Mohammed Tahmid, Marta C. Hatzell

items.title: Bonding, Biradicaloid Character, and Real-Space Topology of the Dinitrosyl Beryllium Dimer Be2(NO)2: A Multiconfigurational and Energy-Decomposition Study
items.abstract: The structural, vibrational, thermodynamic, multiconfigurational electronic structure, biradicaloid character, charge-transfer bonding, and real-space topological properties of the dinitrosyl beryllium dimer, Be2(NO)2, are investigated using density functional theory (DFT) at the TPSS/def2-TZVP-D4 level, complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) coupled with N-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (NEVPT2), STEOM-DLPNO-CCSD, and multi-wavefunction topological analyses via Multiwfn. Energy Decomposition Analysis combined with Natural Orbitals for Chemical Valence (EDA-NOCV) and Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) reveal that the stability of this unique main-group cluster is governed by strong electrostatic interactions, pronounced charge-transfer components, multi-centre core bonding, and synergistic orbital back-donation channels. Natural orbital occupation numbers and narrow singlet–triplet gaps further confirm significant biradicaloid character.
items.authors: D. K. Jha, M. Pathak, Dhananjay Kumar Jha

items.title: Additive Manufacturing of Polyvinylidene Fluoride (PVDF) Toward High Performance with AI-Driven Workflows
items.abstract: Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a high-performance fluoropolymer known for its chemical resistance, mechanical strength, thermal stability, and piezoelectric and dielectric behavior, making it an ideal material for additive manufacturing (AM). The first part of this paper provides an overview and demonstration of this potential, with the first section reviewing PVDF materials, crystallographic phases, and fused deposition modeling (FDM) processing. This perspective provides practical guidance for optimizing PVDF AM for engineering applications, as well as the potential for artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) workflows to inform future research.
items.authors: Rigoberto C. Advincula, John Ryan C. Dizon, Tabitha D. Burch, Xiang Cheng, Alejandro H. Espera, Erick L. Ribeiro

items.title: Excitonic Coupling Suppresses Phonon-Induced Polariton Group Velocity Renormalization
items.abstract: Exciton-polaritons can transport electronic excitation energy ballistically over distances far exceeding those accessible to bare excitons, yet their measured group velocities are often substantially lower than those predicted from the bare polariton dispersion. Recent experiments have shown that excitonic transfer coupling of the materials coupled inside the cavity can reduce the magnitude of group velocity renormalization, even though it does not impact the measured optical dispersion relation of polaritons. We derive an analytical, finite-temperature theory for the phonon-renormalized lower polariton group velocity that explicitly considers the impact of exciton transfer coupling. Our theory suggests that phonon-mediated virtual scattering of polariton states into dark states and back makes the magnitude of the group velocity renormalization sensitive to the dark exciton dispersion at large momentum. We use mixed quantum–classical dynamics simulations to corroborate the analytical predictions, capture experimental trends in layered halide perovskites, and show that stronger excitonic coupling helps preserve the ballistic character of polariton propagation. These results identify the excitonic transfer integral as a molecular design variable for preserving fast, coherent polariton transport under strong light–matter coupling.
items.authors: Alejandro Montilla-Ortega, Santanu Poddar, Milan Delor, Pengfei Huo

items.title: A Fragment-Based Mechanistic Potential for Noncovalent Systems: Combining Conceptual DFT and Quantum Chemical Topology Domains
items.abstract: Within a framework combining conceptual Density Functional Theory (cDFT) with the computational efficiency of the quantum chemical topology (QCT) description of matter, we introduce a mechanistic potential designed for the fast exploration of intermolecular potential-energy surfaces between rigid molecular fragments. The proposed strategy deliberately retains only a minimal set of physically interpretable contributions, namely electrostatics, charge transfer, and dispersion. All electronic properties are evaluated once for the isolated rigid fragments and subsequently propagated using the Kabsch algorithm during their relative translations and rotations, so that the potential energy depends only on the six intermolecular degrees of freedom. The proposed workflow is illustrated using a set of noncovalent and donor-acceptor complexes displaying different degrees of directionality and intermolecular overlap. In the long-range regime, the effective potential mimics a substantial part of the orientational selectivity and correctly identifies the main low-energy regions and interaction-energy minima. This behavior is illustrated for weakly bound systems, hydrogen-bonded and donor–acceptor complexes, σ-hole interactions, the guanine–cytosine pair, and the CO2 molecule confined within a (H2O)20 clathrate cage. Deviations from reference DFT profiles become more pronounced at shorter intermolecular separations, where Pauli repulsion and polarization contributions, which are not explicitly included in the model, become significant. The resulting approach therefore provides a fast, computationally inexpensive, and physically interpretable tool for the prescreening and exploration of intermolecular potential-energy surfaces, allowing favorable orientations and low-energy structures to be identified prior to more demanding electronic-structure calculations. More generally, this mechanistic strategy may provide a useful route for the modeling and exploration of increasingly complex non-covalent molecular and supramolecular systems.
items.authors: Julien Pilmé, Julien Pilme

items.title: Resolving Kinase Resistance Landscapes via Antisymmetric Siamese Graph Networks and Co-Folding Ensembles
items.abstract: Acquired clinical resistance to small-molecule kinase inhibitors arising from single-point mutations within the ATP-binding cleft presents a critical challenge in precision oncology. Conventional computational modeling relies either on rigid docking—which overlooks induced structural alterations—or computationally demanding alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) methods that cannot scale across wide mutational panels. In this work, we present an end-to-end computational methodology integrating multi-state conformational ensemble generation via the generative biomolecular co-folding engine Boltz with a continuous distance-aware Siamese Graph Neural Network (GNN). Crucially, we introduce an unconstrained bias-free difference head that strictly enforces thermodynamic antisymmetry (f (0) ≡ 0.0 kcal/mol), eliminating trivial baseline drift. Under rigorous 5-fold cross-validation on experimentally characterized kinase resistance pairs, the model achieves an out-of-fold root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 1.637 kcal/mol (MAE = 1.459 kcal/mol, Pearson R = 0.239, Spearman ρ = 0.260). Across a prospective panel of 52 clinical kinase-inhibitor complexes, the architecture structurally rationalizes key resistance patterns, resolving the steric disruption of the ABL1 T315I gatekeeper mutation circumvented by ponatinib and the covalent ablation of EGFR C797S against osimertinib.
items.authors: Sharif Ahmad Naikoo

items.title: Overcoming the Density Limitation of Polyhydroxyurethane Self-Blown Foams through Sol–Gel Chemistry
items.abstract: Non-isocyanate polyurethane foams (NIPUFs), particularly polyhydroxyurethane (PHU) foams prepared by cyclic carbonate aminolysis, are promising safer alternatives to conventional polyurethane foams. Although water-induced CO 2 self-blowing can now be achieved from room-temperature formulations within minutes, access to foams with densities below 150 kg·m -3 remains a significant challenge. Herein, we introduce alkoxysilanes as additives for the fabrication of NIPUFs with ultra-low densities (30–50 kg·m -3 ). The strategy synergistically combines CO 2 generation from cyclic carbonate hydrolysis with in situ alcohol formation through alkoxysilane hydrolysis and condensation. Without external physical blowing agents, surfactants, or foam stabilizers, hybrid foams with densities of 28–35 kg·m -3 were obtained, entering the range of conventional lightweight foams. The resulting open-cell foams showed high porosity, complete cyclic carbonate conversion, and tunable mechanical properties depending on amine structure. Their rebound resilience was also strongly and reversibly modulated by humidity, increasing from 0–9% in the dry state to 37–56% at 90% RH and recovering upon drying. This work demonstrates a simple and versatile alkoxysilane-assisted self-co-blowing strategy toward low-density NIPU cellular materials with humidity-responsive mechanical functionality.
items.authors: Maksim Makarov, Laetitia Urbanczyk, Maxime Bourguignon, Sébastien Calvo, Alexandre Léonard, Bruno Grignard

items.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Aquatic Ecotoxicity Prediction
items.abstract: Aquatic ecosystems are threatened by thousands of chemicals whose hazard is often unknown. Laboratory tests of individual chemicals on individual species establish, for example, the Lethal Concentration for 50% of test individuals (LC50), but for most chemicals in use such data exist for only a small fraction of species. A growing body of research applies machine learning to bridge these gaps. Before such models can be relied on in regulatory and environmental management contexts, they must not only be accurate in general, but also quantify how far individual predictions can be trusted. We address this by training a Bayesian Factorization Machine (BFM) on ecotoxicity test data. The BFM matches the accuracy of the current state of the art in predicting LC50 values, and additionally quantifies the uncertainty of every prediction, separating the part arising from a lack of data (epistemic) from the part that is irreducible, reflecting inter-test and biological variability (aleatoric). We then show how this uncertainty propagates into environmental quality assessment: Species Sensitivity Distributions (SSDs) become ensembles of plausible curves rather than single fits, and the hazardous concentrations derived from them carry credible intervals that are widest for the data-poor chemicals where conventional SSDs are least reliable.
items.authors: Tadeusz Price, Oliver Urs Lenz, Markus Viljanen, Leo Posthuma

items.title: Highly Luminescent Alkyl- and Alkoxy-Terminated Silicon Quantum Dots via Aging Following Single-Step Plasma Synthesis and Functionalization
items.abstract: Nonthermal plasma synthesis enables the continuous production and immediate surface functionalization of silicon quantum dots (Si QDs) in a single, flow-through reactor. While this process occurs on a millisecond timescale, the resulting nanocrystals are often limited by low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY) due to persistent surface defects. In this work, we demonstrate that a minimal post-treatment, aging the Si QDs in specific solvents, can enhance the PLQY to ~50%, approaching the performance of much more complex solution-phase methods. We find that the choice of the surface ligand and solvent is critical: hexanol-terminated Si QDs exhibit significantly higher initial and final PLQYs than decene-terminated particles, likely due to the faster reaction of alcohols with electrophilic surface sites in the gas phase. Among the solvents investigated, chloroform consistently yields the highest PLQY. Furthermore, we show that light irradiation at 400 nm and 633 nm drastically accelerates the Si QD aging process, reducing the aging time from hundreds of hours to under 20 hours. This practical “synthesize and forget” strategy offers an efficient pathway for optimizing high-PLQY Si QDs for applications in optoelectronics and bioimaging.
items.authors: Masoumeh Amirifard, Zhaohan Li, Uwe Kortshagen

items.title: Structure-Based Design of Potent Pan-YTHDF Ligands
items.abstract: N6-Adenosine methylation (m6A) is the most abundant post-transcriptional modification of mRNA. The reader proteins YTHDF1, YTHDF2, and YTHDF3 recognize m6A-RNA in the cytosol. Here, we present a protein structurebased medicinal chemistry campaign that resulted in the pan-YTHDF inhibitor 34, which shows for YTHDF2 an equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) of 0.14 µM determined by calorimetry. Compound 34 binds the three YTHDF paralogs with comparable affinity, while being selective against YTHDC1 and YTHDC2. The high-resolution crystal structures of the complex of YTHDF2 with six members of the series validate the structure-based design. Using the structural information, we designed the advanced compound 31 (IC50 = 0.22 μM for YTHDF2, according to TR-FRET) and a negative control, i.e., its methylated analogue 31b (IC50 100 μM for the three YTHDF paralogs, according to TR-FRET). The cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) provides evidence of YTHDF2 target engagement in cells for the advanced compounds 34 and 31, while the negative control 31b is inactive in CETSA. Compounds 34 and 31 at low-µM concentration inhibit the proliferation of the acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cell lines MOLM-13 and THP-1. Importantly, the inhibition of the YTHDF readers by 31 increases the level and stability of the transcript of tumour necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 1B. This renders THP-1 cells more sensitive to tumour necrosis factor-α-induced toxicity. Thus, ligand 34 and the pair 31 and 31b are tool compounds for studying the biological roles of the cytosolic YTHDF readers and their involvement in AML.
items.authors: Francesco Errani, Francesco Nai, Elena Bochenkova, Marcin Herok, Annalisa Invernizzi, Rajiv Kumar Bedi

items.title: Accuracy in Homonuclear Distance Determinations by Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy: The Benefits of Fast Magic-Angle Spinning up to 100 kHz
items.abstract: Homonuclear distance measurements by solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy under magic-angle spinning (MAS) conditions are key to structural analysis in complex materials. While a wide variety of dipolar recoupling techniques involving the excitation of double quantum (DQ) coherences is available, the excitation efficiency is critically affected by the chemical-shift anisotropy (CSA) and the (often unknown) relative orientations between chemical-shift and dipolar-coupling tensors of the involved nuclei. Here, we demonstrate that a previously reported DQ-based sequence, Constant-Time Dipolar Recoupling Effects Nuclear Alignment Reduction (CT-DRENAR), enables robust and highly accurate homonuclear distance determinations for 19F and 31P nuclei under fast MAS conditions up to 100 kHz. We establish a numerical simulation approach to investigate the uncertainties in such distance measurements arising from the orientational effects and show that they become negligible when the MAS frequency exceeds approximately twice the spectral dispersion due to the CSA. Using this numerical simulation approach for data analysis, 31P–31P and 19F–19F effective distances in crystalline model systems with shortest internuclear contacts of 3–5 Å and CSA magnitudes exceeding 100 ppm are determined with accuracies of 0.1–0.5 Å. The experiment is applied to probe the conformational change of a phosphine ligand upon ruthenium coordination in a heterogeneous solid molecular ruthenium-polyphosphine catalyst. These results demonstrate the suitability of CT-DRENAR as a reliable strategy for precise homonuclear distance measurements in complex functional materials.
items.authors: Yufei Wu, Julius Schlüter, Felix J. Byn, Janine C. Baums, Jonas Koppe, Tom Gabler

items.title: Small-Angle X-ray Scattering and Rheology Reveal the Onset of Interparticle Correlations during Nanoparticle Immobilization in Polystyrene
items.abstract: The immobilization of nanoparticles in polymer matrices is a key strategy to suppress Brownian motion while preserving nanoparticle functionality. In this work, monodisperse iron oxide nanoparticles with mean diameters of 6.4, 7.1, and 8.8 nm were synthesized via thermal decomposition of an iron–oleate complex and immobilized in a styrene matrix by radical polymerization. TEM and SAXS confirm that particle size and morphology remain unchanged, whereas interparticle correlations and larger-scale clusters develop during immobilization. Combined in-situ SAXS and rheological measurements reveal that the timing of structure formation is governed by polymerization kinetics. At 80 °C, rapid polymerization leads to the early development of structure factor contributions and a steep viscosity increase. At 60 °C, polymerization proceeds substantially more slowly, allowing the early stage of structure formation to be resolved in which interparticle correlations develop before the viscosity increases steeply. Larger nanoparticles follow the same sequence of structural changes with a progressively earlier onset, indicating that particle size affects the timing of structure formation. These findings indicate that interparticle correlations form as the medium surrounding the still mobile nanoparticles changes during polymerization, with polymerization kinetics setting the time scale until the solidifying matrix freezes in the structure.
items.authors: Nahal Rouzbeh, Eui-young Shin, Niklas Berndt, Jochen S. Gutmann, Sabrina Disch

items.title: Substituent-Controlled Divergent Photocyclization of Aza-1,5 Dienes to Access Three Distinct Cyclic Frameworks
items.abstract: Rigid, three-dimensional cyclic scaffolds are highly valued in medicinal chemistry, yet selectively accessing dis tinct cyclic frameworks from a common class of simple acyclic precursors remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a precious-metal-free photochemical cyclization of aza-1,5-dienes that enables the substituent-controlled, divergent synthe sis of three distinct cyclic frameworks: bridged bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes, fused bicyclo[2.2.0]hexanes, and six-membered lac tams. N-Aryl-substituted substrates preferentially undergo 5-exo-trig cyclization to afford bridged bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes, whereas substrates bearing electron-withdrawing N-substituents such as acetyl or tosyl groups favor the 6-endo-trig pathway to furnish fused bicyclo[2.2.0]hexanes. Notably, this strategy was further extended to the synthesis of six-membered lactams from N-methyl-substituted aza-1,5-dienes under photosensitizer-free conditions. This work establishes a mild, substituent controlled strategy for skeletal divergence, enabling the selective synthesis of structurally diverse cyclic scaffolds of potential value in medicinal chemistry.
items.authors: Jun-Wei Zhang, Cui-Lian Zeng, Wei-Jun Dou, Yun-He Xu

items.title: Peptide-Directed Ligand Design Enables Chemical Disruption of the Nrf2/MafG Coiled-Coil Transcription Factor Complex.
items.abstract: Transcription factor protein interactions remain among the most challenging targets in chemical biology, particularly those driven by leucine zipper coiled coil assemblies.
