Based on in silico primer screening and gradient PCR optimization, IS1081 and IS900 were selected as target sequences for the detection of MTBC-associated M. bovis and MAP, respectively, with an optimal annealing temperature of 60 °C. The assay was subsequently assessed using 114 blood and fecal specimens from 57 clinically suspected weak cattle under pilot field conditions, providing a preliminary proof-of-concept evaluation. Sensitivity analysis using spiked fecal samples (101–106 CFU/g) demonstrated a detection limit of 102 colony-forming units per gram (CFU/g) for both pathogens with no cross-reactivity; amplification at 10 CFU/g was inconsistent, indicating the lower sensitivity threshold of conventional PCR. When compared with single-target IS900 and IS1081 PCRs, the duplex assay achieved 63.6–100% sensitivity and 95.8–100% specificity, respectively, with substantial Cohen’s kappa agreement and statistically significant p-values. The developed assay showed potential as a molecular diagnostic tool for pathogen detection, with future application in herd-level screening warranting multicenter validation.
items.authors: Saurabh Gupta, Samiksha Agrawal, Swadha Pandey, Shoor Vir Singh

items.title: Retrieving “Natural Religion” in Aquinas: Giving Religion Its Due in the Theology of Religions
items.abstract: This study reintroduces the Christian theology of religions to Thomas Aquinas’s understanding of religion as an acquired moral virtue. Aquinas’s treatment of religion as a moral virtue challenges the norm of revelation-centric theological methods across the positional spectrum. The category of natural religion and a religiosity acquired through reason has been cited either as a negative contrast for supernatural theologies of universal religious origins, or utilized in support of apologetical arguments to promote Christian uniqueness. This study, on the other hand, will retrieve Aquinas on natural religion in order to support appropriate autonomy in theological discourse about other religions. Following a review of problematics in theological method in the theology of religions and a consideration of recent, salient scholarship on Aquinas and religion, the argument will turn toward an exposition of religion in the Secunda Secundae. A retrieval of Aquinas’s theory of acquired religious virtue highlights the corrective meaning of appropriate autonomy in natural religion as a strategy for doing rhetorical justice to the reality of universal religious acts, and as a metaphor for the exigent task of a theology of religions that does not absorb religion into a supernatural monism. The relevance of this study for practical theology will be considered in the concluding section.
items.authors: Erik John Ranstrom

items.title: LSTM-Driven Predictive Mobility Management with Dynamic UAV Deployment for Air–Ground Integrated IoV Networks
items.abstract: Ultra-dense networking (UDN) in air–ground integrated Internet of Vehicles (IoV) networks promises substantial gains in network capacity. However, the mobility of both unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) base stations and ground vehicles makes handovers increasingly frequent and drives up signaling overhead, which compromises the low-latency and high-reliability requirements of IoV applications. To address this issue, this paper proposes an active mobility management scheme based on virtual air–ground cells (VAGC) for air–ground integrated IoV networks. We construct a long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network to predict vehicle trajectories, and we enhance the prediction accuracy by incorporating distance and azimuth information. Within the software-defined networking (SDN) controller, we design a multifunctional coordination module that creates VAGCs according to the prediction results and optimizes UAV deployment, thereby enabling timely updates of vehicle-specific UAV activation sets. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme reduces handover latency and lowers signaling overhead by approximately 35% compared with conventional passive mobility management schemes. The handover failure rate (HFR) decreases as the capacity-tolerance parameter δ increases. The performance metric reaches its maximum value of 0.53 when the prediction period is 3 s.
items.authors: Jing Ye, Fanghui Huang, Linna Pang, Ruixin Feng, Junbin Lou, Dawei Wang

items.title: Public Transit as a Catalyst for Emission Mitigation and Air Pollution Reduction: A Case Study in India
items.abstract: Rapid motorization and urbanization have made the transport sector a dominant contributor to air pollution in developing economies such as India. In this study, vehicular emission trends were investigated in Bhubaneswar, a Tier-II smart city, using a combination of questionnaire surveys, video graphic traffic analysis, and IPCC estimation methodologies during October–December 2025. A roadside survey was conducted with a sample size (N = 385), passenger car sample size (N = 520), bus trips (N = 85), and functional unit (g⋅person−1⋅km−1). Primary data regarding vehicle age, emission standards, mileage, and traffic volume were compiled to evaluate average fuel usage and total pollutant loads under estimated field-level traffic conditions. The empirical results indicate that emissions are fundamentally characterized by vehicle configuration, passenger occupancy, and fuel efficiency. Four-wheelers exhibit the highest per capita emissions (1.44 g⋅passenger−1⋅km−1 CO and 0.24 g⋅passenger−1⋅km−1 HC+NOx), primarily due to low occupancy rates. In contrast, buses demonstrate the lowest per capita emissions (0.13 g⋅passenger−1⋅km−1 CO and 0.07 g⋅passenger−1⋅km−1 HC+NOx). The study concludes that transitioning from private modes to public transit could mitigate vehicular emissions from as low as 8–15% (shift from 2W to buses) to as high as 61–80% (all shifting to bus), highlighting the need for strategic planning for sustainable public transportation infrastructure.
items.authors: Rashmi Ranjan Samal, Satya Ranjan Samal, Malaya Mohanty, Madhu Lisha Pattanaik, Kundan Samal, Jagdeep Kumar Nayak
items.title_zh: 公共交通作为减排和空气污染降低的催化剂：印度案例研究
items.summary_zh: 快速的机动车化和城市化使交通部门成为印度等发展中国家空气污染的主要来源。本研究调查了印度布巴内斯瓦尔（Bhubaneswar）这座二级智能城市的车辆排放趋势，采用问卷调查、视频交通分析和IPCC估算方法，数据收集时间为2025年10月至12月。进行了一项路边调查，样本量为385，乘用车样本量为520，公交车出行85次，功能单位为(g⋅人−1⋅公里−1)。收集了有关车辆年龄、排放标准、里程和交通量的初步数据，以评估在估算的现场交通条件下的平均燃料使用和总污染物排放。结果表明，排放主要受车辆配置、乘客占用率和燃油效率的影响。四轮车的人均排放最高（1.44 g⋅乘客−1⋅公里−1 CO和0.24 g⋅乘客−1⋅公里−1 HC+NOx），主要由于低占用率。相比之下，公交车的人均排放最低（0.13 g⋅乘客−1⋅公里−1 CO和0.07 g⋅乘客−1⋅公里−1 HC+NOx）。研究结论是，从私人交通模式转向公共交通可以减少车辆排放，减少幅度从8-15%（从两轮车转向公交）到61-80%（全部转向公交），强调了这一转变的必要性。

items.title: Light Therapy Effectively Treats Onychomycosis and Promotes Healthy Nail Growth in Toenails with Severe Infections: A Longitudinal Cohort Study
items.abstract: Background: Onychomycosis is a stubborn fungal infection of the nail bed that impacts millions of people worldwide. Severe infections, such as those exhibiting deep dermatophytomas or total dystrophy, are particularly challenging to treat, and are often neglected in clinical studies of onychomycosis therapies. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a novel light therapy suitable for severe cases of distal-lateral subungual onychomycosis. Methods: All infected nails received a photodisinfection regimen that entailed exposure of the whole dorsal foot surface to light, following application of a topical formula, as well as careful debridement to reduce hyperkeratosis. The protocol was administered every 2 weeks over 6 months. The length of clear healthy nail from the matrix was measured at baseline and after 6 months to evaluate new clear growth. Results: In total, 165 great toenails were treated in 101 patients (mean age: 61.0 ± 11.0 years, range 33–98); 153 of these nails (92.7%) had severe infections, including total dystrophy or dermatophytomas, the clinical forms most resistant to therapy. After 6 months, 120/165 nails (72.7%) showed at least a 3 mm increase in clear nail or total clearance, and 88 (53.3%) showed an increase ≥6 mm or clearance. The overall mean growth (±standard deviation) was 5.9 ± 4.5 mm, with the highest growth in the group with total dystrophy (6.6 ± 4.5 mm). No side effects were reported throughout the study. Conclusions: Light therapy is a safe and effective treatment for severe onychomycosis, including nails with total dystrophy and dermatophytomas.
items.authors: Alexander Rabinovich, Judy Wismer, Francesca Sarzetto, Lijun Liu, Jianping Xu
items.category_raw: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association
items.title_zh: 光疗法有效治疗严重甲癣并促进健康趾甲生长
items.summary_zh: 背景：甲癣是一种顽固的指甲床真菌感染，影响全球数百万人。严重感染（如深部皮肤癣或完全营养不良）治疗困难，临床研究中常被忽视。本研究旨在评估一种适用于严重远端侧下甲癣病例的新型光疗法的安全性和有效性。方法：所有感染的指甲接受光消毒方案，包括在涂抹局部药物后将整个足背表面暴露于光下，并仔细清创以减少角化过度。该方案每两周实施一次，持续6个月。基线和6个月后测量新生健康指甲的长度。结果：共治疗165个大趾甲，101名患者（平均年龄61.0 ± 11.0岁，范围33-98岁）；其中153个指甲（92.7%）为严重感染。6个月后，120个指甲（72.7%）显示至少3毫米的健康指甲增长或完全清除，88个（53.3%）显示≥6毫米的增长或清除。总体平均生长为5.9 ± 4.5毫米。

items.title: A Feasible Machine Learning Approach to Improve Cognitive Screening in Multiple Sclerosis
items.abstract: Background: Cognitive impairment is a frequent manifestation of multiple sclerosis (MS). Although the Brief International Cognitive Assessment for Multiple Sclerosis (BICAMS) is the recommended screening battery, the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) is more commonly used in routine clinical practice. The ability of published MoCA cutoffs to detect MS-specific cognitive impairment remains unclear. Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of published Italian MoCA cutoffs for MS-specific cognitive impairment and develop a machine learning (ML) pipeline to improve screening accuracy. Methods: We prospectively enrolled 222 people with MS who underwent both MoCA and BICAMS assessment. Cognitive impairment was defined as performance below the 5th percentile on at least one BICAMS test. The sensitivity, specificity, and balanced accuracy of four published Italian MoCA cutoffs were calculated. An elastic-net penalized logistic regression model incorporating age, education, and raw MoCA score was trained using nested five-fold cross-validation to predict cognitive impairment. We additionally evaluated the impact of disability and fatigue on cognitive impairment and model performance. Results: Cognitive impairment was identified in 62 (27.9%) participants. Raw MoCA scores were significantly lower in cognitively impaired participants than in cognitively preserved participants (22.68 ± 4.29 vs. 25.77 ± 3.67; p 0.0001). Published MoCA cutoffs, however, showed extreme specificity (0.92–0.99) but below-chance sensitivity (0.10–0.44), yielding low balanced accuracy (0.54–0.68). The ML model achieved good discrimination (ROC-AUC = 0.787, 95% CI 0.717–0.852), with sensitivity = 0.69, specificity = 0.72, and balanced accuracy = 0.71. Conclusions: Published Italian MoCA cutoffs have insufficient sensitivity for screening MS-specific cognitive impairment. An ML-based scoring approach substantially improves sensitivity while maintaining acceptable specificity, offering a practical tool to enhance cognitive screening in MS.
items.authors: Michelangelo Dini, Letizia Turchi, Giulia Gamberini, Alessandra Caporali, Giovanna Lucchini, Marta Tacchini

items.title: Influence of Particle Size Fractionation via Pulse Spray Drying on the Physicochemical and Functional Properties of Fruit Smoothie Powders
items.abstract: Fractionation of powders by Pulse Spray Drying (PSD) may improve drying behaviour in fruit smoothies prepared with apple, orange, banana, and whey protein. The objective of this study was to determine whether cyclone-based fractionation via PSD yields smoothie powder fractions with distinct physicochemical and functional properties. The obtained fine and coarse powder fractions (FP and CP) and their quality differences were compared after rehydration (FPS and CPS). Most product was obtained as FP in the cyclone owing to its better fluidization behaviour, while CP was retained in the drying chamber due to its larger particle size, higher density, higher moisture content, and lower glass transition temperature. Both powder fractions could be readily rehydrated for consumption. CPS and FPS reached similar oxidation levels for 5-(Hydroxymethyl)furfural, available Lysine, vitamin C, and α-tocopherol. In contrast, CPS exhibited greater discolouration and lipid oxidation than FPS. Antioxidant status values (total phenolics and ABTS, DPPH, and FRAP antiradical scavenging activities) were up to 51.5% lower in CPS than in FPS. Fractionation via PSD facilitates smoothie powdering; however, fractions generated under distinct thermo-oxidative conditions may exhibit different oxidative stability. The powders should be evaluated before blending to ensure consistent quality. They may require separate packaging, storage, or handling.
items.authors: Cristina Cedeño-Pinos, Israel Muñoz, Maria Dolors Guàrdia, Nisrine Tahori, Xavier Felipe, Antonia María Jiménez-Monreal

items.title: Maintenance of Auditory Deviance Processing Following Auricular Vagal Neuromodulation Therapy in Disorders of Consciousness
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Auricular Vagal Neuromodulation Therapy (AVNT) constitutes a promising non-invasive therapeutic approach for Disorders of Consciousness (DoCs). However, evidence regarding its effectiveness remains limited. In this context, although the Mismatch Negativity (MMN) is a well-established neurophysiological index associated with recovery in DoCs, its modulation by AVNT has not yet been investigated. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of AVNT on MMN in DoCs. Methods: Forty-four participants with DoCs were evenly assigned to either an experimental or a control group, alongside twenty-two healthy participants used to establish normative data in neurotypical conditions. The latency, peak and peak-to-peak MMN amplitude were assessed as a complement to the Coma Recovery Scale Revised (CRS-R). Subsequently, only the experimental group received AVNT, followed by a second assessment across all groups. Results: The control group showed extensive changes across sessions in both peak and peak-to-peak amplitudes. In contrast, the experimental group exhibited a significant change only in peak amplitude for the fronto-central region, with no changes in peak-to-peak amplitude. Between-session changes in peak and peak-to-peak amplitudes differed between the control and healthy groups in the parieto-occipital region. After adjustment for the inter-session interval, the ANCOVA showed an overall group effect on peak-to-peak amplitude changes in the parieto-occipital and right regions. No differences were detected between the control and experimental groups or between the experimental and healthy groups. Finally, no significant effects were found for MMN latency. Conclusions: These findings could be compatible with a possible effect of AVNT, although the evidence remained insufficient to demonstrate a direct effect of the intervention.
items.authors: Samuel López-Rodríguez, Barbara Postigo-Alonso, Myrtha O’Valle-Rodríguez, Marta Gómez-Herranz, María Dolores Navarro-Pérez, Joan Ferri-Campos

items.title: Virtual Reality and English Language Education: Instructional Design Study
items.abstract: This paper presents the design and formative evaluation of English-as-a-foreign-language (EFL) lesson prototypes conducted within immersive virtual environments (IVEs) and reports qualitative insights derived from this Research through Design (RtD) prototype evaluation study. The research involved the development and formative evaluation of prototype lessons grounded in pedagogical expertise and contemporary principles of IVE-based education. The findings identify features, tools, and platform functionalities that were perceived by expert participants as relevant to lesson feasibility, user experience, and prototype refinement, and that informed the design of a collaborative educational IVE. Conducted within a broader research project on education in immersive virtual spaces, the study employed a role reversal methodology in which four experienced EFL educators participated as learners. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed with attention to both the instructional design of the lessons and the operational characteristics of the IVE technology. A Research through Design (RtD) approach was used to iteratively refine the lesson prototypes. The results emphasize the need for systematic formative evaluation and practical testing of IVE-based educational tools before claims about pedagogical effectiveness can be made. Rather than providing generalizable evidence of pedagogical efficacy or policy-level recommendations, the study offers formative design insights, expert reflections, and directions for prototype refinement in EFL-oriented IVE instruction.
items.authors: Alžběta Šašinková, Natálie Káčová, Nicola Catherine Fořtová, Zuzana Juříková, Ladislava Zbiejczuk Suchá, Jiří Rambousek

items.title: Seropositivity and Antigen-Specific Seroreactivity to Leptospira spp. In Equids from Three Regions of Veracruz, Mexico
items.abstract: Information on Leptospira spp. exposure in Mexican equids remains limited. This cross-sectional study evaluated seropositivity and antigen-specific seroreactivity in 313 apparently healthy equids enrolled by convenience sampling in Los Tuxtlas (n = 119), Sotavento (n = 108), and Capital (n = 86), Veracruz, Mexico, from 2 October 2023 to 6 March 2024. Sera were examined by the microscopic agglutination test (MAT) against 13 antigens; titers ≥ 1:100 defined seropositivity. Overall seropositivity was 57.5% (180/313; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 52.0–62.9), with regional proportions of 49.6%, 65.7%, and 58.1%, respectively (unadjusted p = 0.048). Modified Poisson models with robust variance were fitted separately for region with species and region with sex. For Sotavento versus Los Tuxtlas, the adjusted prevalence ratio was 1.33 after adjustment for species (95% CI: 1.06–1.67) and 1.33 after adjustment for sex (95% CI: 1.06–1.66). Antigen-specific seroreactivity was most frequent for Australis (63/313; 20.1%), Bratislava (62/313; 19.8%), and Pyrogenes (57/313; 18.2%); these are overlapping antigen responses, not mutually exclusive serogroup estimates. Environmental and management exposures were not measured at the animal level. The findings support surveillance at the animal–human–environment interface but do not demonstrate active shedding or zoonotic transmission.
items.authors: Alejandro Taylor Estrada-Coates, Juan Manuel Pinos-Rodríguez, Jorge Genaro Vicente-Martínez, Isaac De Gasperin-López, Jessica Yamilete Rodríguez-Flores, Miriam Alva-Trujillo

items.title: Prioritising Content for Continuing Education in Non-Invasive Ventilation Care: A Needs Assessment Survey of Intensive Care Unit Nurses
items.abstract: Background: The success of non-invasive ventilation (NIV) depends on bedside nursing judgement, yet nurses report insufficient preparation, and educational content is usually decided before the competencies nurses most need are identified. Objectives: To prioritise NIV competencies, derived for this study from three clinical practice guidelines, by educational need, and, as secondary aims, describe intensive care unit nurses’ perceived knowledge, self-efficacy and implementation climate for evidence-based practice and their correlates. Methods: A cross-sectional survey questionnaire was completed by 142 nurses in four intensive care units of a tertiary teaching hospital in the Republic of Korea in June and July 2026 (response rate 97.3%). Each of 35 competencies was rated for importance and present competency; priorities were derived by combining the Borich needs assessment with the Locus for Focus model, and their stability was examined by bootstrap resampling. Results: Item means were 5.47 (SD 2.05) for perceived knowledge and 5.53 (SD 2.20) for self-efficacy on a 10-point scale and 1.81 (SD 0.78) for implementation climate on a 4-point scale. Perceived knowledge and self-efficacy were higher among nurses with experience of NIV care and previous NIV education, and these associations remained after adjustment. Length of intensive care experience was not independently associated with either variable, and neither was correlated with implementation climate. Importance exceeded present competency for all 35 items. Seven items were identified as priority candidates; ventilator waveform monitoring was the only item selected by both methods, but its classification was not stable across resamples. Conclusions: The self-perceived priorities concentrated on monitoring and recognising treatment failure, competencies that require interpretation of changing physiological data. Needs assessment before programme design can inform the selection of content, provided that its self-report basis and the instability of items near classification thresholds are recognised.
items.authors: Seung Eun Jung, Yoon Ju Noh, Jae Yong Yoo

items.title: The Effect of De-Cobalt Pretreatment of PDC on the Deposition of Diamond Coatings
items.abstract: During the preparation of polycrystalline diamond compact (PDC), Co is often added as a binder, which reduces the material’s heat resistance and catalyzes the transformation of diamond to graphite at high temperatures, thereby reducing the material’s mechanical properties. After the removal of Co, the exposure of holes beside the diamond grains could also affect the wear resistance of PDC. This article provides a new approach for the surface enhancement of PDC, which involves depositing a layer of diamond coating using the hot filament chemical vapor deposition (HFCVD) method after the removal of Co and investigating the effect of the pretreatment time of PDC on the deposition of diamond. The optimal pretreatment was obtained using the surface morphology, composition, and content of Co for a cross-section of the diamond coatings. A H2SO4-H2O2 solution was mixed in a ratio of 1:10 as the acid corrosion reagent, and the best etching time was 5 h. When the time was short, the residual amount of Co was high, which affected the quality of the diamond coatings. When the time was long, the area fraction of the substrate was high, and the deposited diamond was not able to easily fill the holes caused by corrosion.
items.authors: Cen Hao, Xiang Bo, Zhenhai Guo, Guoliang Liu, Fuming Deng

items.title: Impact of Process Parameters on the Quality Attributes of High-Dose Metformin Hydrochloride Film-Coated Tablets
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Formulating high-dose metformin hydrochloride film-coated tablets is challenging due to the poor flowability and compressibility inherent to high drug loading. To ensure process robustness and consistent product quality, understanding the impact of manufacturing variables is crucial. This study evaluated the effects of key process parameters on the quality attributes of 1000 mg metformin hydrochloride tablets to establish optimal processing conditions for reliable production. Methods: The manufacturing process, comprising wet granulation, compression, and film coating, was investigated to evaluate the influence of key process parameters on tablet quality attributes. Granules were characterized for bulk density, tapped density, and compressibility index. Core tablets were evaluated for physical appearance, weight variation, hardness, and dissolution at a 45 min sampling point across various compression forces and tableting speeds. Film-coating efficiency was assessed based on coating quality, dissolution behavior, and stability. Favorable manufacturing conditions were empirically identified through single-variable optimization and statistical analysis. Results: Wet granulation conducted at a chopper speed of 1400 rpm for 7 min yielded granules with the lowest compressibility index (11.88%), demonstrating significantly improved flowability. Compression at a force of 10 kN and a speed of 40 rpm produced core tablets with acceptable appearance, robust hardness (7.06–7.37 kP), and complete drug release (100%). Tablet hardness was governed by a strong interaction between compression force and tableting speed (partial η2 = 0.929, p 0.001) rather than by either factor alone: at 20 kN, hardness collapsed sharply once tableting speed reached 30 rpm, coincident with mild capping, identifying this force–speed combination as a process-failure condition. For the coating process, maintaining a tablet bed surface temperature of 40 °C ensured optimal coating uniformity without compromising product quality. Dissolution profile comparison against a coated reference product in the primary dissolution medium (pH 6.8) yielded f2 similarity values above 50 for all eight core tablet conditions, and stability testing under accelerated/thermal-stress conditions (up to 65 °C) confirmed maintained dissolution, assay, and related-substance (1-cyanoguanidine) compliance for both the test and reference products. The optimized manufacturing conditions successfully produced film-coated tablets that conformed to all predetermined quality specifications. Conclusions: Manufacturing process parameters significantly influenced the quality attributes of high-dose metformin hydrochloride film-coated tablets. Proper selection and control of these processing conditions ensured consistent granule properties, optimal tablet quality, and enhanced manufacturing robustness.
items.authors: Nguyen Tan Duc, Dang-Khoa Nguyen, Huynh Thanh Liet, Nguyen Huynh Thiet, Phan Nguyen Truong Thang, Phu Loc Lu

items.title: Association of Halliwick-Based Aquatic Physical Activity with Health-Related Quality of Life in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study
items.abstract: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and interaction, accompanied by restricted and repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities. Given the considerable heterogeneity in symptom severity and functional abilities, children with ASD require individualized educational and therapeutic interventions. Among the non-pharmacological approaches used to support this population, aquatic physical activity has emerged as a promising intervention. Material and Methods: The study included 45 children with ASD (ICD-11 code 6A02), comprising 19 girls and 26 boys, aged 8–17 years. Two groups were compared: Group G1, consisting of children and adolescents who had participated in Halliwick-based aquatic physical activity for at least 3 months, and Group G2, without aquatic activities. Health-related quality of life was assessed using the validated Polish version of the KIDSCREEN-52 questionnaire. Results: Children with ASD who participated in Halliwick-based aquatic physical activity (G1) had higher mean scores in all KIDSCREEN-52 domains. However, statistically significant differences were only found in the following domains: Psychological Well-Being, Moods and Emotions, Self-Perception, Autonomy, Financial Resources, and School Environment. Overall health-related quality of life, measured by the KIDSCREEN-10, compared with children who did not participate in aquatic activities. Conclusions: Halliwick-based aquatic physical activity was associated with better quality of life in children and adolescents with ASD, with higher scores observed according to sex, but further research is needed to confirm these findings.
items.authors: Małgorzata Stefańska, Wiktoria Smętek, Joanna Kowalska, Agnieszka Ptak

items.title: Verbal Cue Use and Domains of Pre-Competitive Confidence in Competitive Weightlifters
items.abstract: Competitive weightlifting requires athletes to perform complex technical movements under high physical and psychological demands. This study aimed to characterize pre-competition verbal cue use among competitive weightlifters, examine the structure of pre-competition confidence, and explore associations between cue categories and confidence domains. Athletes competing at the 2025 USA Weightlifting American Finals completed a survey prior to the start of the competition assessing verbal cues used and confidence in performance goals, mental resilience, and physical readiness. Verbal cues were categorized as control, neutral, internal, external, or promotion-focused. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a three-factor structure of confidence comprising performance goals, mental resilience, and physical readiness. Among 122 athletes who reported using verbal cues, external (39%) and control (35%) cues were most common, and more than half reported using multiple cue types. Women more frequently reported promotion-focused cues and less frequently reported control cues than men. Exploratory structural regression analyses indicated that control cues were positively associated with mental resilience and physical readiness, while promotion-focused cues were positively associated with physical readiness. These findings provide field-based descriptive evidence regarding verbal cue use among competitive weightlifters and suggest that different cue categories may be related to distinct dimensions of pre-competition confidence.
items.authors: Marianne Huebner, Nicholas Mortensen, Corinne T. Zimmerman, Wenjuan Ma, Nicholas D. Myers

items.title: Bibliometric Characteristics of the 1000 Most-Cited English-Language Publications per Decade in Anesthesiology, Surgery, and Medicine, 1980–2019: A Comparative Analysis
items.abstract: Background: Bibliometric comparisons can describe highly cited literature but do not represent the full output of a discipline. The NIH-supported Relative Citation Ratio (RCR) field- and time-normalizes citation rates, while the Altmetric Attention Score (AAS) summarizes online attention. This study compared article-level metrics and bibliometric features among the 1000 most-cited English-language publications per decade in the Web of Science (WoS) categories Anesthesia, Surgery, and Medicine during 1980–2019. Methods: The 1000 most-cited English-language records per decade in the WoS categories Anesthesia, Surgery, and Medicine were retrieved for four decades, 1980–2019, in September 2024. Mean RCRs were obtained from iCite. AAS values were obtained through Dimensions AI and treated as cross-sectional scores measured at the extraction date because historical attention-source coverage was not equivalent. Bibliometric features were summarized for this selected sample. Data linkage and analytic denominators: The 12 category-by-decade datasets each began with 1000 selected records, for 12,000 selections in total. The supplied analysis materials did not include a record-level flow table showing successful linkage to PMID/iCite, DOI/AAS, affiliations, or keyword fields for each field and decade. These counts were not imputed or reconstructed and are reported as a limitation. Results: Within this selected sample, MED had higher RCR values across the study period, whereas ANE and SUR did not show the same increase in RCR from their 1980s values. AAS values were summarized descriptively and were not interpreted as equivalent longitudinal growth because historical coverage and post-publication observation time differed. Funding rankings differed by measure: ANE had the highest NIH-funded proportion in 2010–2019, whereas MED had the highest non-NIH funding proportion. Semantic concentration measures varied by field and metric. Conclusions: Within this selected sample, ANE and SUR did not show the same increase in RCR observed for MED. Semantic measures showed field- and metric-specific changes. These descriptive findings do not establish that topic diversity, collaboration, or journal concentration caused differences in influence, and they should not be generalized to all anesthesiology, surgery, or medicine publications.
items.authors: David J. Boughanem, Chamanthi Konidala, Ryan Shargo, Tanjina Jalil, Joseph Sujka, John Hodgson

items.title: Probabilistic Foundation Design in Volcanic Boulder-Rich Lateritic Soils: A Random Field Monte Carlo Framework Applied to Nyabihu District, Rwanda
items.abstract: Conventional deterministic foundation design fails fundamentally in two-phase composite geomaterials such as volcanic boulder–laterite profiles, where bearing capacity is controlled by the spatial arrangement of discrete phases. This paper presents a random field Monte Carlo framework for bearing capacity and differential settlement assessment, validated through a G+1 reinforced concrete building case study in Nyabihu District, Rwanda. Field DCP testing (n = 48) revealed bearing capacities of 12.6–100.9 kPa (COV = 83.2%) within a 77% volcanic boulder matrix. Deterministic design yielded a natural-ground allowable bearing capacity of only 9.98 kPa (FS = 3), presenting an order-of-magnitude shortfall against real column service loads of 172.5–455.1 kPa. Spatially correlated log-normal random field Monte Carlo simulations under the actual 1.9 m × 1.9 m column pad footprints revealed pre-improvement failure probabilities of 99.5–100% and a 57.6% differential settlement exceedance probability ( 25 mm). Excavation to 3.0 m depth and replacement with compacted SW-SM murram (CBR = 26%, MDD = 1.697 Mg/m3) increased the footing-scale ultimate bearing capacity to 1534.8 kPa under general shear (allowable 511.6 kPa). This ground improvement reduced the column failure probability and differential settlement exceedance to 0.1%. Under conservative local shear, the failure probability remains 1% for three of four footings but reaches 59.8% under the heaviest column, emphasizing the critical role of field compaction quality control. Construction to suspended slab level has proceeded with zero observed distress, validating the probabilistic design.
items.authors: Schadrack Mwizerwa, E-Chuan Yan, Jing-Sen Cai, Theobald Niyomugabo

items.title: Restoring Force Model for Cross-Slanted Corrugated Steel Plate Shear Walls
items.abstract: To establish the restoring force model of the cross-slanted self-buckling-restrained corrugated steel plate shear wall (hereafter abbreviated as CCSPW), finite element parametric analysis was conducted on the hysteretic behavior of the CCSPW by considering four key influencing factors: the axial compression ratio, aspect ratio, inclination angle, and end plate thickness. Based on the obtained hysteresis curves and skeleton curves, the skeleton curves were dimensionlessly normalized and regression-fitted to establish a trilinear skeleton curve model together with the functional expressions for each loading stage. Furthermore, the stiffness-degradation laws of different loading and unloading paths were analyzed, and the corresponding stiffness-degradation functions were proposed to construct the restoring force model of CCSPW. The restoring force model was verified by comparing the calculated results with the finite element analysis results. The results indicate that CCSPW exhibits favorable energy-dissipation capacity and high bearing capacity; in particular, the energy-dissipation capacity weakens for the specimens with small aspect ratios, for which noticeable pinching of the hysteresis curves is observed. The proposed restoring force model is in good agreement with the finite element results, providing a theoretical reference for the seismic analysis of this shear wall.
items.authors: Tao-Chun Yang, Hao-Fan Liu, Xiu-Yong Liu, Wen-Wen Chen, Qun Xie

items.title: Effect of Auricular Acupoint Stimulation on Weight in Adults with Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Objectives: To systematically evaluate the effectiveness of auricular acupoint stimulation for weight reduction and metabolic outcomes in adults with overweight or obesity. Design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Methods: Six electronic databases (PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Scopus) were searched from inception to 5 February 2026. The primary outcome was body weight; secondary outcomes included body mass index, waist circumference, and metabolic markers. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. For the primary outcome, a multilevel random-effects model was fitted using restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with small-sample-adjusted cluster-robust variance estimation (CR2) to account for dependent comparisons within studies. Subgroup analyses, meta-regression, sensitivity analyses, and publication bias assessments were also conducted. Results: A total of 20 studies were included in the systematic review, of which 14 contributed 15 comparisons to the primary meta-analysis of post-intervention body weight. The pooled effect was Hedges’ g = −0.21 (95% CI: −0.42 to −0.01, p = 0.043). Heterogeneity estimates were I2 = 46.6% (95% CI: 8.1–76.8%) and τ2 = 0.06 (95% CI: 0.01–0.21), and the 95% prediction interval ranged from −0.71 to 0.29. Formal subgroup tests and univariate meta-regression yielded p values below 0.05 for publication year, funding status, and quality appraisal score. Sensitivity analyses produced estimates in the same direction, although the confidence interval included the null value in some leave-one-out analyses. Conclusions: The pooled estimate suggested a small reduction in post-intervention body weight with auricular acupoint stimulation, but the prediction interval included the null value, indicating uncertainty in the effect across comparable settings. Further well-designed trials with standardized intervention protocols are needed to clarify the magnitude and consistency of the effect.
items.authors: Mi Young Kim, Mi-Kyoung Cho

items.title: High-Level Constitutive Secretory Expression and Low-Temperature Adaptation Engineering of the Acid Protease RMAP9 from the Mangrove-Derived Yeast Rhodotorula mucilaginosa
items.abstract: Acid proteases can improve nitrogen availability during ethanol fermentation by hydrolysing feedstock proteins, but their catalytic performance at relatively low temperatures may be limited. In this study, an acid protease-producing Rhodotorula mucilaginosa strain, TSM-6, was isolated from mangrove sediment, and an acid protease gene, rmap9, was identified by whole-genome sequencing and candidate-gene screening. RMAP9 was constitutively expressed in Komagataella phaffii GS115, and secretion was enhanced through EXG1-derived secretion-signal engineering, tandem assembly of three expression cassettes, and fermentation optimisation. Molecular dynamics simulations and Rosetta-based ΔΔG scoring were further used to identify candidate residues for temperature-adaptation engineering, followed by the site-saturation mutagenesis of Ser125. The optimised recombinant strain reached a maximum extracellular acid protease activity of 312.07 ± 18.37 U/mL, representing a 223% increase over the parental constitutive strain. The S125K variant showed a shift in optimum temperature from 50 to 40 °C and approximately 50% higher relative activity at 40 °C than wild-type RMAP9. Moreover, the low-temperature-favoured variants retained more than 80% residual activity after 72 h at 30 °C. These variants combined improved catalytic performance at relatively low temperatures with long-term stability at 30 °C, thereby providing enzyme properties compatible with temperature-related operational requirements for industrial ethanol fermentation.
items.authors: Yibo Zhang, Jiasheng Cao, Mingming Luo, Zhijie Huang, Yu Tang, Zhizheng Zhao

items.title: Smartphone Dependence, Sleep Quality, and Suicidal Ideation Across Adolescence: A Six-Year Longitudinal Study
items.abstract: Suicide is a leading cause of death during adolescence, and both smartphone dependence and poor sleep have been associated with suicidal ideation. However, it remains unclear whether these associations reflect stable differences between adolescents or year-to-year changes within adolescents. This study examined the developmental trajectories of smartphone dependence, sleep quality, and suicidal ideation over six years spanning the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic and tested whether sleep quality accounted for the association between smartphone dependence and suicidal ideation at the between-person and within-person levels. Data were drawn from six annual waves (2018 to 2023) of the Korean Children and Youth Panel Survey 2018 middle school first-grade cohort (N = 2590; 54.2% boys). A parallel piecewise latent growth curve model (LGCM) and random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) were estimated. Smartphone dependence increased before the pandemic onset (B = 1.47 per year) and declined slightly thereafter (B = −0.16), sleep quality declined after the onset (B = −0.05), and suicidal ideation decreased before the onset (B = −0.10) and increased gradually thereafter (B = 0.03), with no immediate shift at the onset. In the LGCM, the indirect effect of smartphone dependence on suicidal ideation through sleep quality was significant for usual levels (B = 0.005, p 0.001) and pre-onset change (B = 0.008, p = 0.001) but not for post-onset change (B = −0.001, p = 0.570); Wald tests indicated that the path from sleep quality to suicidal ideation (p = 0.001) and the indirect effect (p = 0.004) differed between the two periods. In the RI-CLPM, higher-than-usual smartphone dependence predicted higher-than-usual suicidal ideation one year later (β = 0.05, p 0.001), whereas no within-person lagged paths involving sleep quality were significant. Smartphone dependence, poor sleep quality, and suicidal ideation thus co-occurred between adolescents, but annual within-person changes did not show a pathway through sleep quality. Because period differences cannot be separated from age-related development in a single cohort, they should not be interpreted as pandemic effects. These findings support attending to adolescents with high smartphone dependence and poor sleep within existing school-based screening systems, whereas the mechanisms through which risk is transmitted require studies with shorter measurement intervals.
items.authors: Yeonju Lee, Sung-Man Bae

items.title: Inversion of Apple Leaf Moisture Content and SPAD Values Using Multispectral Vegetation Indices and Band Reflectance from UAVs
items.abstract: Accurate monitoring of leaf chlorophyll-related status (SPAD) and water status is important for evaluating apple growth and supporting orchard management. In this study, SPAD and leaf water content (LWC) were considered complementary indicators of chlorophyll-related and water-related physiological characteristics, respectively. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral imagery and field measurements were collected during the flowering, fruit-setting, fruit-expansion, and fruit-coloring stages of Aksu red Fuji apples. Sensitive spectral features were screened using correlation analysis, and k-nearest neighbor (KNN), extreme learning machine (ELM), random forest (RF), and backpropagation neural network (BPNN) models were developed for SPAD and LWC estimation. The results showed clear relationships between multispectral features and both traits, with the RF model combining vegetation indices and band reflectance achieving the best overall performance. During the fruit-expansion stage, the optimal RF models achieved independent test-set R2 values of 0.767 for SPAD and 0.768 for LWC. These results demonstrate the potential of UAV multispectral remote sensing combined with machine learning for orchard-scale spatial monitoring of apple leaf chlorophyll and water status.
items.authors: Yuwei Wu, Qi Wang, Sumin Lv, Yasen Qin, Ning Yan, Jingming Wu

items.title: Timing-Dependent Neuromuscular Responses to Pulsed Electromagnetic Field (PEMF) Stimulation During Cycling Exercise in Sedentary Males
items.abstract: Pulsed electromagnetic field (PEMF) increases the amplitude of muscle activity during physical exercise. This study investigated the effects of PEMF stimulation timing on neuromuscular activation in young sedentary males, during moderate-intensity constant-load cycling. We examined whether a PEMF applied at the beginning or during the middle of continuous exercise elicits differential effects on muscle activation. The participants performed a 30 min cycling task at 50% of VO2max in which PEMF stimulation was alternately activated or deactivated in 15 min bouts. Surface electromyography (EMG) was recorded from the right vastus medialis and biceps femoris, and blood lactate samples were collected at baseline and during exercise. Data were analyzed via linear mixed-effects modeling. Active PEMF stimulation significantly increased normalized EMG amplitude in the vastus medialis (p 0.001) and biceps femoris (p = 0.001) compared to inactive conditions, with the greatest effect observed when stimulation was applied after 15 min of exercise. Blood lactate concentrations were significantly elevated during PEMF application relative to baseline and inactive stimulation (p 0.001). The timing of PEMF stimulation influenced neuromuscular responses during exercise, highlighting its potential as a tool to modulate muscle performance in sedentary individuals.
items.authors: Aurelio Trofè, Alessandro Piras, Michela Persiani, Luca Breviglieri, Alessandra Laffi, Andrea Meoni

items.title: Computational Design and Structure-Guided Optimization of Anti-Osteopontin Monoclonal Antibodies at the Intersection of Obesity, Type 2 Diabetes, and Hepatocellular Carcinoma
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are recognized metabolic risk factors for its development. In this study, disease-associated gene lists for T2D and obesity were integrated with differentially expressed genes from the Cancer Genome Atlas Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma cohort (TCGA-LIHC). Analysis of 371 primary HCC and 50 solid-tissue normal samples identified 2123 differentially expressed genes, including 715 upregulated and 1408 downregulated genes. The intersection of the 715 upregulated genes with 2055 T2D-associated and 1944 obesity-associated protein-coding genes identified 29 common candidates. Functional annotation identified 14 extracellular-region genes, which were evaluated using protein–protein interaction analysis and ranked using the maximal clique centrality algorithm. SPP1, encoding Osteopontin (OPN), was the highest-ranked candidate. SPP1 expression distinguished HCC from non-tumor tissues with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.714 (95% confidence interval: 0.666–0.760). High SPP1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival, and continuous log2-transformed SPP1 expression remained independently associated with survival after adjustment for age, sex, and pathological stage. OPN was subsequently subjected to structural modeling, molecular dynamics simulation, B-cell epitope prediction, and the structure-guided optimization of anti-OPN monoclonal antibodies. Molecular docking and binding affinity analyses revealed that optimized mAbs exhibited predicted Kd values corresponding to approximately 10- to 650-fold stronger binding affinity and increased predicted hydrogen bonding at the interface. These findings support SPP1 as a promising immunotherapeutic target in metabolically driven HCC, warranting further experimental validation.
items.authors: Elahe Shams, Elham Rismani, Pedram Asadi-Sarabi, Mohsen Nasiri-Toosi, Reza Malekzadeh, Moustapha Hassan

items.title: Spray-Dried Chitosan-Clay Nanocomposite Gels as Binders: Enhanced Compressibility and Micromeritic Properties of Lactose-Based Granules for Poorly Compressible Drug Tablets
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Nanocomposites of chitosan (CH) and magnesium aluminum silicate (MAS) clay can be produced by spray drying. This study aimed to characterize and evaluate spray-dried chitosan (SDCH) and SDCH-MAS nanocomposites, which were prepared using CH with MWs of 400 kDa (4M) and 800 kDa (8M), as binders of lactose granules containing propranolol HCl (PPN) and crude powder from Andrographis paniculata (ADP) intended for tablet formulation. Methods: Lactose granules were produced using SDCH and SDCH-MAS composites via wet granulation, and the granule properties were compared with those obtained using polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP K30). The lactose granules incorporating PPN and ADP crude powder were also prepared and compressed into tablets. The physical properties of both granules and tablets were evaluated. Results: SDCH-MAS composites formed intercalated or exfoliated nanocomposites, as proved by PXRD, and rapidly hydrated in water to form gels that functioned as binders. Lactose granules prepared with SDCH and SDCH-MAS composites exhibited fair to good flowability and demonstrated lower yield pressure and yield strength during plastic deformation than those prepared with PVP K30. Moreover, granules loaded with PPN offered acceptable flowability and could be compressed into tablets. Increasing MAS content reduced the disintegration time of tablets in 0.1 N HCl. The use of SD4MCH in tablets could retard PPN release, while the addition of MAS accelerated drug release. For ADP crude tablets with a 75:25 ADP-to-lactose ratio, acceptable hardness and friability were achieved when SD4MCH-MAS 1:0.6 composites and PVP K30 were used, and 75% of andrographolide dissolved within 30 min. Conclusions: SDCH-MAS nanocomposite gels are effective binders for lactose granules in wet-granulated tablets.
items.authors: Rapee Jarungsirawat, Peera Tabboon, Napaphak Jaipakdee, Duangkamon Sakloetsakun, Thaned Pongjanyakul
